# HoBo — full documentation

> The complete HoBo docs as one markdown document, in reading order.
> The condensed briefing lives at https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/llms.txt.

<!-- Guide · What is HoBo? · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/guide/ -->

# What is HoBo?

HoBo is an **AI-native meta-cloud** built on one guiding principle: **every app deserves a home — preferably a cheap one.** You describe your app once, HoBo places it on real infrastructure that passes your policies, and then — this is the part nobody else does — **it keeps looking**. When a better-value home opens up, continuous migration moves your app there, without a rewrite, a war room, or a weekend.

> **Honest status:** HoBo is **pre-release**, and the core loop already runs: pack a Bindle → `hobo plan` / `hobo up` / `hobo dev` against the default local lane, plus the `hobo-mcp` agent surface — with live deploy lanes credential-gated. See [the trail map](/HoBo/guide/status/) for what runs now.

## The pitch

*"Write your app once. HoBo finds it the cheapest home that meets your standards — and moves it when somewhere better opens up. Built for humans and the agents that work for them."*

A developer (or an agent) packs the app into a [**Bindle**](/HoBo/primitives/bindles/), runs `hobo up`, and the app lands in a [**Camp**](/HoBo/primitives/camps/) — inferred on the local lane by default, or pinned by topology you author. [**Yards**](/HoBo/primitives/yards/) select providers; camps describe environments. From then on, placement is a *standing decision*, not a historical one.

## Why "HoBo"?

The name is the philosophy. A hobo travels light, works where the work is, and moves on when a town stops being worth the rent:

- **Travel light.** Everything the app owns fits in its bindle. 
- **Work anywhere.** Ports and adapters mean any conforming provider is a valid home. 
- **Move when it's worth it.** Continuous migration re-plans placement for as long as the app lives.

# Getting started

Time to leave home. This guide takes you from an empty directory to an app that has a home — and a standing ticket to a cheaper one. You'll meet HoBo's two foundational primitives, in the order you need them:

1. **[Bindle](/HoBo/primitives/bindles/)** — *pack.* Everything your app owns, rolled into one provider-agnostic bundle. The one thing you must write: no bindle, nothing to host.
2. **[Camp](/HoBo/primitives/camps/)** — *settle.* The environment shape your app occupies (prod/staging/…). Every app lives in a camp, but **writing one is optional** — leave it out and HoBo infers a camp. **Provider selection lives on the [Yard](/HoBo/primitives/yards/)**, not inside the camp.

**[Yards](/HoBo/primitives/yards/)** and **[Junctions](/HoBo/primitives/junctions/)** are advanced scenarios — pin a provider, multi-region, or multi-cloud. Short section [at the end](#advanced--yards-and-junctions).

> **Pre-release note:** `@hobo/*` is **not on npm**. Public `npx hobo` is a *different* package. The local lane (`collect` / `plan` / `up` / `dev`) runs **after** you clone this repo, install with pnpm, and build the workspace. Default IaC is still an **in-memory Pulumi stand-in**. Live Cloudflare/Vercel/Pulumi lanes are credential-gated.

## Prerequisites

- **Node.js** ≥ 22 (`node:sqlite`; CI uses 24). TypeScript is the first reference implementation.
- **pnpm** 10 (`packageManager` in the repo root). A GitHub zip without `external/ts-autocode` is incomplete — clone with submodules / the full tree.
- No cloud account for the local lane.

## Run the local lane (clone — not npm)

```sh
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/Tyler-R-Kendrick/HoBo.git
cd HoBo
pnpm install
pnpm hobo doctor --cwd examples/hello-bindle
pnpm hobo plan --cwd examples/hello-bindle
pnpm hobo up --cwd examples/hello-bindle
pnpm hobo dev --cwd examples/hello-bindle   # serves a live local URL
```

`pnpm hobo` is the supported invocation — it builds `@hobo/hobo` and
`@hobo/adapter-hono` on first use, so there is no separate build step to
forget. (`pnpm --filter @hobo/hobo exec hobo …` does **not** work: pnpm never
links a package's own bin into its own `node_modules/.bin`.)

Do **not** run `npx hobo`. Use the composed `@hobo/hobo` binary from this workspace via `pnpm hobo`. `hobo new` exists on that binary only; it is not a public npm scaffold.

The same commands deploy the apps the [Examples console](/HoBo/examples/)
shows — they share one catalog:

```sh
pnpm hobo up --cwd examples/try-site/apps/hello-world
pnpm hobo plan --cwd examples/try-site/apps/todo-api
```

## Step 1 — Pack your bindle

The bindle is the first thing HoBo looks for and the only thing it ships. It's plain code — no YAML sidecar, no config dialect:

```ts
// src/bindle.ts
import { bindle } from "@hobo/bindles";

import { app as api } from "./api";
import { app as web } from "./webapp";

export default bindle("my-app", (b) => {
 const db = b.data().allow("read", "write"); // a SQL-ish data port, least-privilege verbs inline
 const jobs = b.queue().allow("enqueue"); // background work

 const apiSvc = b
.api(() => api.fetch) // HTTP API entrypoint
.dependsOn(db, jobs); // typed bindings, injected at runtime

 const webSvc = b.web(() => web.fetch).dependsOn(apiSvc);

 return { db, jobs, api: apiSvc, web: webSvc };
});
```

Three things to internalize — they're what make everything later cheap:

- **Resource names come from the returned object keys.** `{ db, jobs, api, web }` is your app's topology; the object *is* the manifest.
- **`.dependsOn(...)` is the wiring.** It declares edges *and* injects typed bindings at runtime. Nothing reaches a backend it didn't declare — deny by default.
- **`.allow(...)` is inline least privilege.** Verbs are scoped to the resource's kind — `"read"`/`"write"` on a data port, `"enqueue"` on a queue, `"get"`/`"set"` on a kv store. Permissions travel *in* the bindle, so they move when the app moves. That's the trick: a bindle carries everything needed to unpack it anywhere, which is exactly what makes migrating to a cheaper home a routine event instead of a rewrite.

That's a complete description. Against a **built** `@hobo/hobo` binary, `hobo up --cwd examples/hello-bindle` converges on the default **local lane** (offline, durable SQLite journal, in-memory Pulumi stand-in — not live multi-cloud). If a committed `hobo.bindle.json` is present it wins; otherwise the manifest is compiled from `src/bindle.ts`.

> **Starting from nothing?** You don't need existing code to pack a bindle. Declare a `@component` class whose `@operation` methods carry an intent, a typed contract shape, and an optional rubric — a `stub()` body declares *code to be generated* — and hand it straight to `b.api(...)`. See [Greenfield: declare the bindle, generate the code](/HoBo/primitives/bindles/#greenfield-declare-the-bindle-generate-the-code).

## Step 2 — Camps (optional) and providers (on the Yard)

A **camp** answers *what environment is this?* — not *which cloud account*. Camps declare env type, labels, and runtime **requirements**. They do **not** own the Bindle and do **not** select providers.

```ts
// src/camps.ts — optional; omit entirely for inferred local camps
import { camp } from "@hobo/camps";

export const prod = camp("prod", {
  envType: "prod",
  runtimeRequirements: ["runtime-local"],
});
```

**Provider selection belongs on the Yard** (advanced — day one can skip this and use the local lane):

```ts
// src/yard.ts
import { yard } from "@hobo/yards";
import { prod } from "./camps";

export default yard("aws-east", {
  provider: "aws",
  regions: ["us-east-1"],
  camps: [prod],
});
```

Converge:

```sh
hobo plan --camp prod   # dry run: placement, cost, warnings — read-only
hobo up --camp prod     # build, plan, gate, provision, deploy
hobo logs --camp prod   # live-tail through the camp runtime
```

Useful truths:

- **The camp is a *current address*, not a vow.** The bindle stays provider-agnostic so the home can change. Continuous migration reuses plan → gate → converge.
- **Writing a camp is optional.** No camp file → inferred local camp on the default lane. Explicit camps pin env semantics or satisfy locked-down placement policy.
- **Zero-setup first deploy:** after the workspace build above, `hobo up` / `hobo dev` need no cloud credentials. `hobo login` mints a local dev session; `hobo claim` binds an anonymous deployment to an account later. **Live** lanes are credential-gated: Cloudflare (`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` + `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`), Vercel (`VERCEL_TOKEN`), or live IaC credentials.
- **Provider-native power stays in the Bindle** as additive annotations (not a rewrite):

```ts
import { aws } from "@hobo/provider-aws";

const apiSvc = b
  .api(() => api.fetch)
  .with(aws.with.fargate({ cpu: 512, memoryMiB: 1024 }));
```

**You now know everything required to run HoBo.** A bindle is the whole entry fee. Everything below is for apps with wanderlust.

## Advanced — Yards and Junctions

Skip this on day one. Come back when you pin a provider or go multi-cloud.

### Yard: one provider, many camps

```ts
import { camp } from "@hobo/camps";
import { yard } from "@hobo/yards";

export default yard("aws", {
  provider: "aws",
  regions: ["us-east-1", "us-west-2"],
  camps: [
    camp("prod-east", { envType: "prod" }),
    camp("prod-west", { envType: "prod" }),
  ],
});
```

One yard per provider. Multi-region = several camps under one yard. Multi-cloud = several yards under a junction.

### Junction: many yards, many clouds

> **Early-stage:** `junction()` authoring and plan derivation ship; each yard still realizes its own half. Full multi-cloud realization is on the [trail map](/HoBo/guide/status/).

```ts
import { junction } from "@hobo/junctions";
import awsYard from "./yards/aws";
import azureYard from "./yards/azure";

export default junction("my-app", { yards: [awsYard, azureYard] });
```

Requires **at least two** member yards. Continuous migration then has a bigger map; residency and sovereignty policy decide what may cross which border.

## Where to next

- [Bindles](/HoBo/primitives/bindles/) and [Camps](/HoBo/primitives/camps/) — the full reference for the two primitives you just used.
- Worked examples ship with the product docs and starter templates.
- [Core concepts](/HoBo/guide/concepts/) — the vocabulary in one sitting.
- [The hobo CLI](/HoBo/guide/cli/) — the whole verb surface (it's deliberately small).
- [hobo-code](/HoBo/guide/hobo-code/) — talk to Bo after `hobo-code` starts the session.
- [HoBo for agents](/HoBo/agents/) — pointing an AI agent at HoBo? It gets its own credentials, not yours.

<!-- Guide · Core concepts · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/guide/concepts/ -->

# Core concepts

HoBo's metaphor is the itinerant worker who travels light, and the names lean into it — but every term has a precise technical meaning. Here's the whole vocabulary in one sitting.

## The four scopes

Scopes nest by breadth: **`Bindle ⊂ Camp ⊂ Yard ⊂ Junction`**. The bindle is the one thing you must write; the camp is where your app always lives (declare one to pin placement, or let HoBo infer it from the code you've configured); the last two are for apps that go places.

| Scope | What it is |
|---|---|
| **[Bindle](/HoBo/primitives/bindles/)** | The app, packed: services, resources, wiring, policies, and deployment intent. Provider-agnostic by construction — which is what makes it cheap to move. |
| **[Camp](/HoBo/primitives/camps/)** | Environment shape (prod/staging/…) and runtime **requirements**. Does **not** own the Bindle or select the cloud provider. Durable runtime ports (EventStore, Queue, ActorHost, Clock) are provided by the Camp substrate. |
| **[Yard](/HoBo/primitives/yards/)** | **Provider selection point** plus zero or more camps: cross-camp policy, identity, reconciliation, provider-global networking. One yard per provider. |
| **[Junction](/HoBo/primitives/junctions/)** | Where yards meet: cross-yard **federation** for hybrid/multi-cloud. Peer yards, no shared mutable state — the final edge is federation, not containment. |

Multi-region within a provider = several camps under one yard. Multi-cloud = several yards federated into a junction.

## App Kits (inside a Bindle)

Inside a Bindle, resources split into two families:

| Family | What it is | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **[App Kit](/HoBo/primitives/app-kits/)** | Application surface that hosts entrypoints or interactive runtime behavior | `api`, `web`, `service`, `ui`, `websocket`, `job`, `wasm-component` |
| **Infra Kit** | Port / infrastructure dependency — not an entrypoint host | `kv`, `bucket`, `queue`, `topic`, `secret`, `data`, … |

**[Session Replay](/HoBo/reference/session-replay/)** is default-supplied on every App Kit (not only `web`).

## Continuous migration

The guiding principle behind everything above: **placement is a standing decision, not a historical one.** Because the bindle is provider-agnostic and the camp is just its current address, HoBo's Dispatcher can keep re-planning placement for as long as the app lives — watching price, credits, reliability, and policy. When a better home clears the gates, the move runs through the same plan → gate → converge loop as any deploy. Migration isn't an emergency procedure in HoBo; it's a lifestyle.

- **Policy-gated:** an inferred or migrated placement is approved by policy, not automatically — your platform decides how much wanderlust to allow.
- **Reversible:** every move is a sequence of events; rolling back a migration is replaying the decision, not archaeology.
- **Cost-directed:** the default objective is simple and honest — the cheapest home that meets your standards.

## WIT/WASM ports

The portable contract between app code, runtime ports, and provider adapters is **WIT** (the WebAssembly Component Model's interface language, hosted on wasmCloud by default). App Kits sit above that contract:

- **Ports are WIT interfaces** — storage, messaging, HTTP, identity, and more.
- **Apps are wasm components** (with an OCI-container fallback for anything wasm can't host yet).
- **Providers are capability providers** linked to component imports — deny-by-default: a component reaches a backend only via a link the manifest declared.
- **Any Component-Model language** can author against the same interfaces. TypeScript is the first reference implementation, not a requirement.

That thin, typed port contract is what makes continuous migration economical: moving homes means re-linking ports to a new provider's adapters, not rewriting the app. App Kits *compose* those ports into Bindle-declared surfaces you author day to day.

## Ports and adapters, everywhere

Cloud providers, IaC engines (Pulumi, Crossplane, Terraform/OpenTofu), build/VM tools (Dagger, Packer, Firecracker), identity systems, and AI optimizers all sit behind replaceable ports. Two consequences:

- **Conformance is the contract.** Every port ships a contract test suite; any adapter — human- or AI-written — must pass it to be certified as a valid home.
- **Patchable, not just portable.** You can swap any engine, add any adapter, fork the Yard, and persist AI/human patches, with conformance as the trust bridge.

## The replayable event log

Control-plane state, projections, SRE workflows, and audit trails all derive from an **append-only event log**. Commands mutate state only by appending events (CQRS/event sourcing), which buys:

- **Recovery:** a crash anywhere — mid-deploy, mid-migration — is recovered by replaying the stream.
- **Audit:** every state transition, including *agent token issuance* and *every migration decision*, is a durable, attributable fact.
- **Time travel:** projections can be rebuilt at any point in history. "Where did this app live in March, and why did it move?" is a query, not a forensic investigation.

The default durable Camp EventStore is **SQLite behind ports** (one partition, one active writer; scale by partitions). Actors append under optimistic sequence **and** a fencing token so a stale holder cannot win after lease transfer. Catch-up projections use database-local positions; live callbacks are an optimization, not the only delivery path. Queue/timer/outbox side effects can stage in the **same** durable transaction as domain facts, while network dispatch happens outside that transaction.

## Contract effects (what a boundary can do)

Contracts are not only request/response shapes. A boundary can declare an **EffectSpec**: purity (pure vs varies vs transacts…), capability tags (may fail, may suspend…), and domain I/O (network, storage, identity, policy eval, agent tools…). Pure contracts isolate for unit tests with zero infrastructure; domain effects drive automatic harness mocks. When a revision **widens** effects (for example pure → network), can-deploy treats that as a potential breaking change for consumers that assumed a narrower set.

## Visible resiliency (secondary layer)

Operations that face flaky I/O may carry a **ResilienceProfile** — deterministic retry schedules, timeouts, circuit-breakers, and related strategies — as **contract-visible metadata**, not a new top-level control-plane noun. Application emits attempt/terminal facts for replay. Hard rules stay fixed: `policy.Decided` denials and typed terminal failures **never** retry; cancellation stops pending work; inspection is reconstructed from the event log, never process memory.

## Agent-native identity

AI agents are **first-class principals**, not scripts holding a human's API key:

- Workload identity (SVID/OIDC) with **brokered short-lived tokens** — secretless-first, no static credentials.
- A machine-readable **capability standard** so agents can self-provision exactly the credentials a task needs.
- Policy checks at every phase, and traceable actions in the same event log as everything else.
- An MCP control surface alongside the SDK and CLI, so the same capabilities are reachable by humans and agents alike.

## Where the details live

- [Bindles](/HoBo/primitives/bindles/) · [App Kits](/HoBo/primitives/app-kits/) · [Camps](/HoBo/primitives/camps/) · [Yards](/HoBo/primitives/yards/) · [Junctions](/HoBo/primitives/junctions/) — the primitive references.
- [Session Replay](/HoBo/reference/session-replay/) — default on every App Kit.
- [Architecture](/HoBo/architecture/) — the machinery that does the describing, placing, and moving.
- [HoBo for agents](/HoBo/agents/) — the agent identity model and MCP surface.

<!-- Guide · The hobo CLI · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/guide/cli/ -->

# The `hobo` CLI

The CLI is deliberately small — a hobo carries one stick, not a toolbox. **`up` and `down` are the only lifecycle verbs**: ship, promote, roll back, migrate, and even self-host bootstrap are flags on the same convergence loop, not separate commands. Every documented example on this site sticks to this canonical surface.

## Lifecycle

```bash
hobo up
hobo up --camp prod
hobo up --camp prod --to <revision>
hobo up --rollback
hobo up ./platform --seed
hobo down --camp pr-123
```

`up` realizes the current object graph: build, plan, gate, provision, deploy. `down` tears it back in reverse dependency order. `up` always reruns the applicable gate before mutation — a stale preflight can never authorize a deploy. Continuous migrations run this same loop; there is no separate `migrate` verb.

## The full verb surface

| Verb | Role | Semantics |
|---|---|---|
| `up` / `down` | lifecycle | Realize / tear down the object graph. |
| `dev` | local loop | Offline local-runtime camp; serve api/web handlers in-process. |
| `new` | local loop | Scaffold a runnable SDK program. |
| `login` / `claim` | identity | Dev identity (OIDC/SVID path); bind an anonymous deployment to an account. |
| `connection` | identity | Durable Connections (create / authorize / list / get / revoke / rotate). |
| `identity` | identity | Continuous identity migration status / inspect (zero Bindle config). |
| `access` | identity | Elevated / cross-env access or break-glass (short-lived, audited). |
| `feature` | delivery | OpenFeature flags / canary / experiment (`list` \| `eval` \| `set` \| `kill` …). |
| `deploy` | delivery | Attested continuous-delivery **status / logs / rollback** (not a second lifecycle). |
| `incident` | delivery | CD failure disposition: A2H handoff or sandboxed self-heal. |
| `plan` | read-only | Dry-run the `up` decision: plan, matching, cost, warnings. |
| `verify` | read-only | Unified Gatekeeper preflight. |
| `can-deploy` | read-only | Producer/consumer compatibility matrix. |
| `inspect` | read-only | Projections and time-travel views (`run`, `deploy`, `topology`, …). |
| `logs` | read-only | Live-tail Camp streams. |
| `doctor` | diagnostics | Environment, credential, connectivity, and portability hazards. |
| `messaging` | diagnostics | Messaging capability + delivery-guarantee readiness. |
| `codegen` / `build` / `collect` / `stub` | authoring | Bindings, wasm components, manifest IR, contract-backed stubs. |
| `drift` | diagnostics | Drift report + governed remediation paths. |
| `add` / `registry` | distribution | Install providers after sig/provenance/conformance; registry admin. |
| `import` | migration | Adopt an existing estate in place — never destroy/recreate on import. |
| `generate` | generation | Request the provider-generation loop for a missing backend. |
| `sandbox` / `test` | test loop | Isolated lanes; out-of-scope boundaries served from contracts. |
| `attest` / `erase` | governance | Signed evidence exports; crypto-shred with projection rebuild. |
| `broker` | governance | Conductor resolve / config / matrix (placement plane). |
| `yard` | control plane | Install and inspect the default bare-metal Yard. |
| `station` | control plane | Station ops/setup (`init` \| `up` \| `down` \| `status` \| `rails *`) — not lifecycle. |
| `serve` | control plane | Local control-plane HTTP+SSE for the Yard game UI. |
| `replay` | observability | Session Replay list/get/open/summarize/retention/doctor. |
| `derivative` | extensibility | Manage derived HoBo implementations. |
| `runbook` | SRE | Execute or replay incident runbooks under policy. |

## Not lifecycle (and not missing)

Where other tools invent ceremony commands, HoBo folds them into the model:

- **Lifecycle shipping** is only `up` / `down` (plus flags). A separate “deploy command” as *lifecycle* is rejected.
- **`deploy` as a verb still exists** — it is the continuous-delivery *observe* surface (`status` / `logs` / `rollback`), not a second ship path.
- `destroy`, `teardown`, `rollback`, and `promote` as standalone commands are rejected; use `down` or `up --rollback` / promotion via convergence.
- `train`, `crew`, and `fleet` are SDK code and projections, not CLI verbs.

## Status

The **canonical verb set** is on the composed `hobo` surface today and maps **1:1** to [`hobo-mcp`](/HoBo/agents/mcp/) tools (parity is contract-tested). Lifecycle is `up` / `down`; `hobo deploy` is **observe-only** delivery status, not the ship verb. Interactive authoring is [`hobo-code`](/HoBo/guide/hobo-code/). The default path is the **local lane**: offline Yard runtime, durable SQLite journal, no cloud account. Live deploy lanes are credential-gated (Cloudflare, Vercel, or live IaC credentials). Some advanced flags (`--to`, `--rollback`, `--seed`) and deeper multi-cloud depth are still maturing — see [the trail map](/HoBo/guide/status/). Global flags that work everywhere: `--json`, `--camp`, `--cwd`, `--verbose`, `-q`, `--help`.

---

<!-- Guide · hobo-code · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/guide/hobo-code/ -->

# hobo-code

`hobo-code` is the **interactive coding session** (Bo). `hobo` is the **control-plane CLI** (`up` / `down` / `plan` / `dev` and the rest of the canonical verb set). They are different binaries.

`@hobo/*` is **not on npm**. Do not run `npx hobo` or invent `npx hobo-code`. After you clone this repo:

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm exec turbo run build --filter @hobo/adapter-hono --filter @hobo/code --filter @hobo/hobo
pnpm --filter @hobo/code exec hobo-code
```

That starts the session. From there, **talk** for hello-world / run / debug. Zero-LLM pattern lookup is explicit: `hobo-code template …` or `/template web frontend backed by an api` (ADR-0153). Ordinary chat is not silently intercepted for arbitrary queries.

## What belongs where

| You want | Use |
|---|---|
| Plan / converge / tear down an existing Bindle | `hobo plan` / `hobo up` / `hobo down` / `hobo dev` |
| Author or extend an app by talking | `hobo-code` session |
| Search/render a pattern with no model | `hobo-code template` or `/template` |
| Agent tool calls over the same verbs | `hobo-mcp` — see [the MCP surface](/HoBo/agents/mcp/) |

## Honest limits

- Workspace build first. A half-built tree cannot import `@hobo/adapter-hono`.
- Default apply is still the in-memory Pulumi stand-in. Live lanes are credential-gated.
- Known intents fill templates. Implementation holes marked `"use training"` stay holes until training exists.

Next: [Getting started](/HoBo/guide/getting-started/) · [The hobo CLI](/HoBo/guide/cli/) · [Try HoBo](/HoBo/examples/).

<!-- Guide · The trail map · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/guide/status/ -->

# The trail map

Where is HoBo on the road? Here's the honest itinerary.

| Area | State |
|---|---|
| **Product** | **Pre-release.** Not accepting tenants; `@hobo/*` packages are **not published to npm** yet. |
| **Developer surface** | SDK primitives, the **canonical `hobo` verb set** (source: `packages/cli/src/shell/verbs.ts`), and the MCP surface documented here are **contract-pinned**: specified, validated, and stable to learn against. Product binary: `@hobo/hobo`; shell/factories: `@hobo/cli`. Interactive authoring is [`hobo-code`](/HoBo/guide/hobo-code/), a different binary. |
| **Implementation** | Progressing through staged build gates (below). Default deploy is an **in-memory Pulumi stand-in**, not live multi-cloud apply. See "What runs today" and ship targets. |
| **This site** | The canonical public developer documentation — for humans and agents. |

Ship targets stay **pre-release**: OSS public docs (this site), local-first developer tooling after a workspace build, hosted beta later. Default apply is an in-memory Pulumi stand-in. See [Getting started](/HoBo/guide/getting-started/) and [Architecture](/HoBo/architecture/) for what a visitor can run without a private repo checkout.

## What runs today

- **The TypeScript bindle flow.** After a workspace build of `@hobo/hobo` and `@hobo/adapter-hono`, a project whose `src/bindle.ts` default-exports a `bindle()` runs `hobo collect`, `hobo plan`, `hobo up`, `hobo down`, and `hobo dev` on the default **local lane** — no cloud account. `@hobo/*` is not on npm (`npx hobo` is the wrong package). Default IaC is an **in-memory Pulumi stand-in** (`HONEST SCOPE` in `@hobo/hobo` compose); a successful `up` does **not** imply real infrastructure was provisioned. A half-built tree used to look like “no Bindle”; import errors now surface. `hobo dev` serves the project's own api/web entrypoint handler in-process; a committed `hobo.bindle.json` manifest artifact wins when present.
- **Durable local EventStore.** The Camp EventStore defaults to a **single-owner SQLite partition** (`@hobo/storage-sqlite` + `@hobo/runtime-local`): stream-head CAS, actor fencing, positioned catch-up, durable subscription checkpoints, and atomic domain events with staged queue/timer/outbox effects. Browser hosts use `@hobo/runtime-browser` with OPFS when available (fail-closed when durable is required but OPFS is not).
- **Contract effects + visible resiliency.** `@hobo/contracts` BoundaryContracts may declare **EffectSpec** and **ResilienceProfile**; can-deploy treats effect widening as breaking when declared; Gatekeeper surfaces effect summaries; `@hobo/contract-harness` isolates pure contracts and runs never-retry fault injection. No Effect-TS/Polly/XState public dependency.
- **Station + pure Conductor.** `@hobo/stations` + `@hobo/broker` — control-plane isolation, Rails, receipts pin `stationId` + `railHash`.
- **Trails + continuous identity.** `@hobo/trails` recipes and hands-off dual-path identity continuous (`@hobo/identity`); pure identity continuous needs zero Trail authoring. **`hobo login` defaults to fixture/local session material**, not production OIDC/SPIRE.
- **Live migration & upgrade executors.** `@hobo/trails` ships upgrade preflight/compatibility evidence, a real expand→backfill→contract executor over SQLite (snapshot-before-mutation, compat-gated destructive contract), pooled→siloed zero-loss tenant moves (fence → drain → export/import → checksum-gated reap), and CDC data-dual ports. The `migration.*` event bodies are pinned in `@hobo/events`' append-only golden-replay corpus with an upcaster-totality gate.
- **Budget-driven routing.** `@hobo/dispatcher` (deterministic credit/budget selection, `dispatch.Decided`), `@hobo/broker` budget threshold signals, and the `@hobo/stations` closed routing control loop + progressive health-gated cutover. `pnpm run staging:cutover` rehearses a zero-downtime backend swap on a loopback lane (archived evidence); Vercel/Cloudflare lanes are credential-gated and fail closed.
- **Jurisdiction & residency.** Typed legal geography in `@hobo/core` (region→jurisdiction catalog, per-tenant residency constraints, fail-closed `evaluateResidency`) with a residency Gatekeeper gate, a residency policy pack, and OSCAL-aligned control→evidence packs in `@hobo/policy`.
- **Thin SaaS providers.** `@hobo/provider-convex` — honestly-scoped capability classes, typed impedance limits, credential-gated Management API (fails closed without a broker-minted key).
- **Harness progressive delivery.** OpenFeature-shaped flag evaluation, delivery, and experiments in `@hobo/identity`; CD apply plane in `@hobo/cloud`.
- **Connectivity foundations.** `@hobo/connectivity` — hierarchical naming (never bare `.hobo`), overlay/DNS, secretless connectors, env isolation, PAM hooks.
- **Messaging.** Unified `topic()` / messaging plane with Kafka and optional Dapr adapters; default remains the local in-process path.
- **Component host scaffolds.** `@hobo/runtime-wasm` (Wasmtime), `@hobo/runtime-oci` (kubectl transport), `@hobo/runtime-cloud-native` (mock default + a **real credential-gated Cloudflare provider** proving the remote FetchHandler contract; aws/gcp/azure/vercel stay declared-unimplemented fail-closed). See [Component hosts](/HoBo/reference/component-hosts/).
- **Componentize honesty.** `@hobo/componentize` has two lanes: the offline default emits **synthetic wasm contract bytes** (`buildWasmContractBytes`) for digest/boundary proofs, and `HOBO_COMPONENTIZE_REAL=1` drives the **real jco/`componentize-js` pipeline** (toolchain-gated, fail-closed — never a silent synthetic fallback) producing genuine component-model binaries.
- **Session Replay on every App Kit.** `@hobo/replay` + default annotation on all App Kits (`api`, `web`, `service`, `ui`, `websocket`, `job`, `wasm-component`) — not only `web` (ADR-0137). Prefer **App Kit** over "membrane type" at Bindle authoring; WIT membrane stays ADR-0069. Local dual fixtures default-on; `hobo dev` wraps HTTP Kits with bootstrap + `/__hobo/replay/*`; production flag/sample gated; `hobo replay *`. See [Session Replay](/HoBo/reference/session-replay/) · [App Kits](/HoBo/primitives/app-kits/).
- **The MCP control surface.** The `hobo-mcp` binary (`@hobo/hobo`) serves the **canonical verb set** as MCP tools over stdio, dispatching through the same command registry as the CLI, with verb/tool parity contract-tested, deny-by-default auth, and audited decisions. See [the MCP surface](/HoBo/agents/mcp/).
- **Login.** `hobo login` runs a real RFC 8628 device-code grant when an issuer is configured (`HOBO_OIDC_ISSUER` → OIDC discovery → device authorization → token polling → JWKS verification), fail-closed with typed remediation; the offline fixture session remains the no-issuer default. `hobo verify` runs the ADR-0146 residency dimension from environment-supplied tenant constraints (`HOBO_RESIDENCY_ALLOW` et al) through the policy layer.
- **Credential-gated live lanes.** Cloudflare and Vercel deploys unlock via env tokens; the real pinned Pulumi engine unlocks via `HOBO_PULUMI_LIVE=1`. These are opt-in; they are not the default offline path.
- **Examples in the repo:** `hello-bindle` (`hobo up` after adapter build), `multi-cloud-shop` (local Yard kv+queue), `durable-agent` (**tests only**, no Bindle), `self-host-yard` (in-process Yard). Pages [Examples](/HoBo/examples/) ship local-bridge apps; browser-WIT hello-world needs local `astro dev`.
- **Not yet shipped / design-stage:** npm registry publish, full certified multi-cloud provider adapters (fly/aws/azure/gcp production apply paths), Junction package maturity toward S4, production OIDC/SPIRE defaults, and alternate EventStore engines (`runtime-postgres` / Temporal / Restate / Cloudflare DO).

## How the build is staged

One leg at a time:

- **Local toolchain** — hello Bindle through CI with guards green. 
- **Local fidelity** — offline `hobo dev`, replay equals live. 
- **First cloud + Yard** — first provider and drift policy. 
- **Agent autonomy** — scoped agent auth and operator hooks. 
- **Multi-cloud** — overlays, placement across providers, Junctions. 
- **Extensibility** — provider generation and forge hooks. 
- **Production hardening** — HA/DR, canary, FinOps. 

## What “contract-pinned” means

Public surfaces — SDK signatures, CLI verbs, event families — are pinned by executable contracts and conformance suites. Documented examples track the canonical CLI. When this site changes, it is because the **product contract** changed, not because marketing drifted.

## Following along

- [Getting started](/HoBo/guide/getting-started/) 
- [Core concepts](/HoBo/guide/concepts/) 
- [Agent docs](/HoBo/agents/) and [`llms.txt`](/HoBo/llms.txt)

<!-- Architecture · Architecture overview · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/architecture/ -->

# Architecture

## In this section

| Page | Topic |
|---|---|
| [Data plane](/HoBo/architecture/data-plane/) | Event log, aggregates, projections, SQLite default |
| [Control plane](/HoBo/architecture/control-plane/) | Yard: plan → gate → converge |
| [WASM & WIT surface](/HoBo/architecture/wasm/) | Component Model ports & hosts |
| [Air-gapped & sovereign](/HoBo/architecture/air-gapped/) | Zero-egress profiles |

A condensed tour of the machinery that packs, places, and — crucially — *keeps re-placing* your app.

## The one-paragraph model

A developer (or agent) writes a **Bindle** (app topology) and optionally `camp()`/`yard()`/`junction()` scope objects mapping ports to providers. The **Yard** — HoBo's provider-specific control plane — receives a deploy request; the **Planner** turns Bindle + mapping into a **DeploymentPlan** (a DAG of resource plans); the **Orchestrator** drives each resource to reality through **ResourceActors** that call IaC/build adapters inside sandboxed **Executors**, brokering short-lived credentials from **Identity**. Every state transition is an event in an append-only log, so the whole system is replayable, auditable, and recoverable. The app lands in a **Camp**, which also supplies the durable runtime the app's actors and workflows run on. And then the **Dispatcher** keeps watching: when a cheaper valid home appears, the same pipeline runs again as a migration.

## Control plane vs data plane

Keeping these separate is a core architectural commitment:

- **Control plane (the Yard)** decides *what infrastructure should exist* and makes it exist. Event-sourced, actor-based, multi-tenant — and **never on the critical path** of a running app's request. If the Yard is down, deployed apps keep serving. (They just can't move that day.)
- **Data plane (the running Bindle)** is your actual app plus the Camp's durable runtime (event store, queues, streams, actors, clock). It uses HoBo's runtime SDK primitives but does not depend on the Yard at request time.

## Control-plane components

| Component | Responsibility | Emits |
|---|---|---|
| **Gateway** | Authn/z; SDK RPC + REST + MCP; accept commands; serve read models | `DeployRequested`, … |
| **Identity** | Workload identities (SVIDs); OIDC; broker provider tokens | `IdentityIssued`, `TokenGranted` |
| **Registry** | Catalog of providers + their Capability Manifests | `ProviderRegistered` |
| **Planner** | Resolve mappings → `DeploymentPlan` DAG; capability/region/cost constraints | `Planned`, `PlanRejected` |
| **Broker** (branded "the Conductor") | Policy-governed placement decisions across providers; wraps the policy/contract/billing/delivery/connector planes ([details](/HoBo/primitives/stations/#the-conductor)) | `broker.Resolved`, `broker.Rejected` |
| **Dispatcher** | Continuous placement: watch cost/policy/reliability signals; propose policy-gated migrations to better homes | `MigrationPlanned`, … |
| **Orchestrator** | One ResourceActor per resource reconciling desired↔actual; sagas for ordering & compensation | `Provisioning`, `Provisioned`, `Failed`, `Deployed` |
| **Executors** | Run IaC apply/preview/destroy + builds in sandboxes with scoped, short-lived credentials | `ExecStarted`, `ExecSucceeded`, `ExecFailed` |
| **Event Store** | Append-only source of truth; durable subscriptions; snapshots (default engine: single-owner SQLite partition behind ports) | *(is the log)* |
| **Read models** | Materialized projections for queries and dashboards | *(query API)* |

Two runtime/IfC additions: the **wasm host** (runs components; holds the link table binding each import to a capability provider) and the **Collector** (runs components in resource-collection mode to produce the manifest IR the Planner consumes).

## The deploy path (and the migration path — same path)

```text
hobo up
 → Gateway authenticates the principal → DeployRequested
 → Planner solves the plan → Planned
 → Orchestrator spawns ResourceActors → Provisioning … Provisioned
 → (failure? sagas compensate) → Failed → Compensating
 → DAG completes → Deployed

…and later, unprompted:
 Dispatcher spots a cheaper valid camp → MigrationPlanned
 → policy gate approves (or a human does)
 → the exact same convergence loop → Migrated
```

A crash anywhere is recovered by replaying the deployment's event stream. Inspection (`hobo inspect run <id>`) reads projections and never touches providers. There is deliberately no separate "migration engine" to trust — if you trust `hobo up`, you already trust a move.

## Key invariants

1. **Commands mutate only via events.** No component writes resource state except by appending an event.
2. **Executors are the only thing that touches a cloud** — always sandboxed, always with a short-lived scoped token.
3. **The Yard is itself a Bindle**, deployed by an earlier Yard or bootstrapped locally (self-host = hosted).
4. **Same code, many Camps.** Swapping a Camp's runtime backend changes durability backing, never app logic — that's what keeps moves cheap.
5. **Deny-by-default linking.** A deployed component reaches a backend only via a link the manifest declared.

## Capability layers

Public surfaces stack like this — adapters plug in without rewriting apps:

| Layer | What you work with |
|---|---|
| **Authoring** | Bindles, App Kits, Camps, Yards, Junctions |
| **Contracts & policy** | Boundary contracts, Gatekeeper, policy packs, effects/resiliency intent |
| **Runtime ports** | EventStore, Queue, Messaging, Streamer, ActorHost, Clock |
| **Hosts & engines** | Local/browser journals, Wasmtime, OCI/Kubernetes, optional cloud-native hosts |
| **Control** | Stations, Conductor, Trails, progressive delivery (Harness) |
| **Surfaces** | `hobo` CLI, MCP, identity, connectivity |

See the [capability map](/HoBo/reference/packages/) for the product-facing overview and the [trail map](/HoBo/guide/status/) for what ships today.

### Durable event log default

The Camp durable EventStore defaults to **SQLite**, with one database file (**partition**) owned by one active writer. Scale by partitions — not multi-writer access over shared network storage. SQLite is an **engine**, not the portability boundary: the same EventStore ports and storage capability can be implemented by other stores later. Stream revision uses a stream head (not a full scan), actor **fencing tokens** reach storage, and domain events can commit atomically with staged queue/timer/outbox work. Store-local **positions** support catch-up without becoming domain identity.

### Contract effects + visible resiliency

Boundary contracts may declare optional **effects** (pure vs network/storage/…) and optional **resiliency profiles** (deterministic retry, timeouts, circuit-breakers). Effect widening can break can-deploy when consumers assumed purity. Resiliency stays **secondary** — it is not a top-level control-plane noun — and policy denials / terminal failures **never** enter a retry schedule.

---

<!-- Architecture · Data plane · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/architecture/data-plane/ -->

# Data plane

The data plane is where **facts live**. Control plane (Yard) decides infrastructure; data plane runs your app and the Camp’s durable runtime. If the Yard is down, camps keep serving — they just cannot re-place that day.

## Why event sourcing is the foundation

| Benefit | What you get |
|---|---|
| **Recovery** | Crash mid-deploy or mid-workflow → replay rebuilds exact state |
| **Audit** | Every infra change and credential issuance is an ordered fact |
| **Time-travel** | Reconstruct as-of; diff two points (`hobo inspect`) |
| **Determinism** | Durable workflows replay over cached step results |

## One log, two folds

| Fold | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **Write model (aggregate)** | Authoritative state for invariant checks inside a single-writer actor |
| **Read model (projection)** | Rebuildable views for queries, dashboards, reactive UI |

Both fold the **same append-only event log**. Snapshots are **caches**, never sources of truth. Snapshot ahead of head → hard error (`SNAPSHOT_AHEAD`).

## Commands → past-tense facts

1. Commands enter at a boundary (HTTP, MCP, workflow step) — they are **not** stored as events.
2. Aggregate `decide` runs pure business rules against folded state.
3. Aggregate `emit` past-tense facts.
4. Append uses **`expectedSeq`** (optimistic concurrency) and optional **`fenceToken`** (lease fencing).
5. Optional **`stageEffect`** stages queue/timer/outbox work for the same durable transaction.
6. After commit, live subscribers wake; network dispatch of staged work is at-least-once.

## Default durable store

Camp EventStore defaults to a **single-owner SQLite partition** behind ports:

| Property | Detail |
|---|---|
| Stream head | Revision + `owner_epoch` on a head row — not `COUNT(*)` |
| Positions | Database-local `bigint` for catch-up (`EventPosition`) |
| Checkpoints | Durable subscription positions |
| Atomic effects | Domain events + staged work in one commit |
| Scale model | Add partitions; not multi-writer NFS WAL |

Details: [EventStore reference](/HoBo/reference/eventstore/) · [Durability tests](/HoBo/testing/durability/).

## Reactivity

Default reads are **subscriptions** over materializations (**replay-then-live**). GraphQL facades and point lookups are escape hatches over the same models. Session consistency is the usual default; stronger/weaker levels are entity-configurable.

## Upcasters & quarantine

Event bodies evolve via forward-only upcasters. Poison events produce `*.Quarantined` facts so folds skip deterministically instead of wedging forever. Crypto-shred / erase rebuilds projections without rewriting history bytes in place.

## What is *not* the event log

| Data | Home |
|---|---|
| Streamer **frame bodies** | Streamer journal (tokens, logs, progressive UI) |
| Authoritative-external provider DBs | Explicit escape hatch with staleness labels |
| Blob/object payloads | Bucket resources — store refs in events |

## Multi-aggregate work

Cross-aggregate operations are **eventually consistent** by design. Use sagas/choreography (events library) and correlation ids — do not invent a distributed transaction across aggregate streams.

## Related

[Architecture](/HoBo/architecture/) · [Control plane](/HoBo/architecture/control-plane/) · [Aggregates testing](/HoBo/testing/aggregates/) · [Runtime ports](/HoBo/reference/runtime-ports/)

<!-- Architecture · Control plane · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/architecture/control-plane/ -->

# Control plane

The **Yard** is HoBo’s provider-specific control plane: it decides *what infrastructure should exist* and drives it to reality. It is **never** on the critical path of a live user request to your app.

## Components

| Component | Job |
|---|---|
| **Gateway** | Authn/z; SDK / REST / MCP ingress |
| **Identity** | Workload SVIDs, OIDC, brokered short-lived provider tokens |
| **Registry** | Provider + capability catalog; certification records |
| **Planner** | Bindle + mapping → DeploymentPlan DAG; Matching |
| **Conductor (Broker)** | Policy-governed multi-provider placement |
| **Dispatcher** | Continuous re-placement (cost/policy/reliability) |
| **Orchestrator** | ResourceActors reconcile desired ↔ actual; sagas compensate |
| **Executors** | Sandboxed IaC/build with scoped credentials |
| **Event Store** | Append-only control-plane truth |
| **Read models** | Dashboards, inspect, status |

## Same path for deploy and migrate

`hobo up` and continuous migration share **plan → gate → converge**. There is no separate “migration engine” to trust. Dispatcher re-enters the same loop when a better home opens.

## Gates before reality

Nothing mutates cloud state until Gatekeeper (and friends) allow:

1. Contract compatibility (can-deploy)
2. Policy packs + obligations
3. Cost / quota
4. Golden suite (when enabled)
5. Optional secretless-config / can-migrate / can-trail / effects visibility

Machine-readable reasons ship on `gatekeeper.Decided` for agents and humans.

## ResourceActors & choreography

One ResourceActor per resource owns reconciliation. Independent subtrees provision concurrently. Failure past threshold choreographs rollback via events — not a single brittle coordinator thread. See [Matching & ResourceActors](/HoBo/reference/matching/).

## Executor sandbox

- Firecracker-class isolation; **no ambient cloud creds**
- Short-lived capability-scoped tokens per resource + action
- Stdout via Streamer; IaC state per resource backend
- Concurrency bounded per tenant and provider

## Self-host = hosted

The Yard is itself a Bindle. Bootstrapping a self-host Yard is the same lifecycle as any other app. Air-gapped profiles use signed offline bundles and in-boundary substitutes — see [Air-gapped](/HoBo/architecture/air-gapped/).

## Stations

A Conductor occupies a **Station** (hard isolation boundary). App topology (Bindle ⊂ Camp ⊂ Yard ⊂ Junction) is separate. Missing Station fails closed for control-plane work.

## Related

[Conductor](/HoBo/primitives/stations/#the-conductor) · [Identity](/HoBo/security/identity/) · [Stations](/HoBo/primitives/stations/) · [Matching](/HoBo/reference/matching/)

<!-- Architecture · WASM & WIT surface · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/architecture/wasm/ -->

# WASM & WIT surface

HoBo’s portability contract is **WIT/WASM** (Component Model / wasmCloud-shaped). TypeScript is the first reference implementation language, not a requirement for the architecture.

**[App Kits](/HoBo/primitives/app-kits/)** (Bindle-declared `api`/`web`/`service`/… surfaces) compose those ports at authoring time. WIT interfaces are the capability boundary the hosts and providers implement.

## Why WIT

| Property | Benefit |
|---|---|
| Typed capability imports | Deny-by-default sandbox is structural |
| Host-supplied storage | Engines swap without guest SQL |
| OCI fallback | Pragmatic packaging where components are not ready |
| Same Bindle, N runtimes | Conformance-tested portability |

## Storage capability

Guests use `hobo:storage@0.1.0` — **not** filesystem paths. Hosts bind SQLite partitions or other engines. See [WIT & storage](/HoBo/reference/wit-storage/).

## Messaging capability

Publish/subscribe is **the messaging port** (`topic()`). Hosts may bind:

- Kafka / Redpanda / MSK via Kafka provider
- Dapr pub/sub via optional optional Dapr runtime (Camp opt-in)
- Local in-memory for offline tests

App code never imports Kafka or Dapr clients. See [Messaging, Kafka & Dapr](/HoBo/reference/messaging/).

## Build

`hobo build` compiles services to components; generated drift fails closed. `hobo stub` keeps contract-backed stand-ins while implementation is generated.

## Isolation dimension

WASM capability security sits beside data / compute / credentials / network isolation. Compromised guest code should not inherit ambient cloud credentials.

## Related

[Architecture](/HoBo/architecture/) · [Messaging, Kafka & Dapr](/HoBo/reference/messaging/) · [Capability map](/HoBo/reference/packages/) · [Security](/HoBo/security/)

<!-- Architecture · Air-gapped & sovereign · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/architecture/air-gapped/ -->

# Air-gapped & sovereign

HoBo supports a **zero-egress** Yard profile for sovereign and regulated deployments. Deploy / match / migrate / route must work **without phone-home**.

## Capability substitutes

| Capability | Connected | Air-gapped substitute |
|---|---|---|
| Registry | Crawl capability manifests | **Signed offline bundle import** |
| Images | Public pull | Mirrored in-boundary OCI |
| TLS | Public ACME | Internal CA / private ACME |
| Identity / SVID | Yard-issued | Unchanged (already in-boundary) |
| Secrets | Provider KMS | In-boundary KMS/HSM |
| Embeddings | Hosted API | Local model or BYO vectors |
| AI generation | Hosted LLM | Local LLM or human-authored only |
| Telemetry | 3p sinks | In-boundary OTel collector |

## Rules

1. Registry refuses unsigned/unproven plugins even offline — trust moves to the **bundle signer**, not to “files on a USB.”
2. No feature may require egress for core deploy/migrate.
3. Metering and audit stay in-boundary; export is operator-controlled.
4. Provider free-tier games still forbidden — sovereign is not a loophole for multi-account free tiers.

## CLI

`hobo registry` offline bundle import; `hobo doctor` should report egress assumptions.

## Related

[Security](/HoBo/security/) · [Control plane](/HoBo/architecture/control-plane/) · [CLI](/HoBo/reference/cli/)

HoBo is **secure-by-default, zero-trust, defense-in-depth**. This section is the home for identity, access, tenancy, and network isolation — not scattered under Guide.

<!-- Security · Identity & auth · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/security/identity/ -->

# Identity & auth

HoBo is **secretless-first**. Long-lived static cloud keys are the residual path, not the default.

## Principals

| Principal | Notes |
|---|---|
| Humans | Org RBAC roles; OIDC/SSO |
| Workloads | SVID/OIDC per Camp/service |
| Agents (users) | First-class principals with scoped, short-lived credentials |
| Crew operators | Built-in Yard agents under the same model |

## Brokered credentials

1. Task declares needed capabilities.
2. Policy decides allow / deny / mutate / require-approval.
3. Identity brokers a **short-lived, scoped** token to the provider.
4. `CredentialAudit` records access **by reference**, never plaintext secrets in the log.

Confused-deputy and runaway spend are mitigated by scoped SVIDs, policy gates, spend caps, and full replay.

## Continuous identity migration

When identity providers or principal shapes change:

- Dual-path continuity is Matching/policy-driven.
- **Zero required Bindle config** for pure identity continuous.
- Dual fixtures extend offline fixtures.
- Observe with `hobo identity status` / `hobo doctor`.
- Do not invent a parallel IdP DSL or Bindle-only migration product.

Trails may *compose* `identity.continuous`; pure identity continuous needs no Trail authoring.

## Secrets residual path

`secret(name)` / `hobo:secrets` remain for legacy-compatible and residual classical credentials. Prefer `fromBinding`, bound resources, and federation. Config resolution ranks secretless sources first — [Config & secrets](/HoBo/reference/config-secrets/).

## Multi-tenant context

`HOBO_TENANT` / `HOBO_PROJECT` / `HOBO_BRANCH` / `HOBO_ENV` carry soft multi-tenancy. Hard isolation is phased; PolicyEngine is the baseline enforcer. Extreme isolation uses separate Yards/Stations.

## Agents

Agents authenticate like any principal, get tool scopes via MCP, and never receive ambient admin. Details: [Agents](/HoBo/agents/) · [Credentials](/HoBo/security/credentials/) · [Audit](/HoBo/observability/agent-audit/).

## Related

[Security](/HoBo/security/) · [Identity reference](/HoBo/reference/identity/) · [Connections via Station](/HoBo/primitives/stations/)

---

<!-- Security · Multi-tenant & policy · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/security/multi-tenant/ -->

# Multi-tenant & policy

Posture: **secure-by-default, zero-trust, defense-in-depth**. Every principal (human, workload, agent) is authenticated and authorized per action — not trusted because it is “inside the VPC.”

## Threat model (summary)

| Asset | Primary mitigations |
|---|---|
| Provider credentials | Keyless OIDC federation; short-lived resource-scoped tokens |
| Tenant data & streams | Per-tenant isolation; claim enforcement on envelopes |
| Executors | MicroVM isolation; no ambient creds; no egress by default |
| Generation plugins | Signed + conformance; sandboxed runs |
| Capability Manifest prose | Treat discovery text as untrusted (prompt-injection aware) |
| Yard itself | Append-only log + fencing; least privilege; immutable history |
| Agents | Scoped SVIDs; policy gates; spend caps; full replay |

## Deny by default

Unlisted `(role, action, resource)` tuples are denied. Control-plane CLI/MCP verbs must map to `hobo:<resource>:<verb>` actions or conformance fails.

## Policy as code

Policy packs attach to Yard/Junction. **Mandatory** rules are deny-ceilings (children may only further restrict). **Default** rules are overridable. Decisions always emit `policy.Decided` — even allows. See [Policy](/HoBo/reference/policy/).

## Lanes & sandboxes

Sandbox lanes isolate experimental traffic and contract observations so they cannot poison baseline contracts or training trajectories. Baseline subscribers ignore sandbox-lane events by default.

## Guardrails

AI operators and generation paths run under enforced guardrails (PII, jailbreak, unsafe tool use). Blocks are events: `guardrail.Blocked` + `policy.Decided`.

## Network isolation

Hard environment isolation and optional Privileged Access Gateway bound who can reach what. Overlay (Tailscale/Netbird-class) and hierarchical DNS names live in connectivity — never bare `.hobo` TLD. Details: [Connectivity](/HoBo/reference/connectivity/) · [Naming](/HoBo/reference/naming/).

## Supply chain

- Plugins: signed, SLSA-style provenance, conformance report required
- Images: reproducible builds, digest-pinned, scanned
- Dependencies: SBOM + vuln gates
- Air-gap: signed offline bundles — [Air-gapped](/HoBo/guide/air-gapped/)

## Audit & compliance

The event log *is* the audit log. Security-relevant families export as **OCSF** to SIEM. Audit streams are never-compact by policy. Data residency constraints are Planner-enforced.

## Provider terms

Registered providers are **the operator’s own accounts**. Never pool free-tier headroom across tenants; never rotate accounts to reset free tiers. Rotation is **across providers**, not across accounts within a provider.

## Runtime isolation (WASM)

WASM capability security is a **structural** isolation dimension (deny-by-default imports), alongside data / compute / credentials / network.

## Related

[Identity](/HoBo/security/identity/) · [Policy reference](/HoBo/reference/policy/) · [DevSecOps role](/HoBo/roles/devsecops/) · [Agent audit](/HoBo/observability/agent-audit/)

---

<!-- Security · Connectivity & networking · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/security/connectivity/ -->

# Connectivity & networking

Networking in HoBo is **identity-aware and name-first**. Apps dial hierarchical named endpoints; material stays brokered; isolation tiers fail closed.

## Named endpoints

- Pure hierarchical naming (DNS-safe labels, never bare `.hobo`)
- Local: `*.hobo.localhost`
- Overlay: `*.hobo.test`
- **Never** bare `.hobo`

See [Naming reference](/HoBo/reference/naming/).

## Overlay & DNS

Connectivity hosts overlay adapters (Tailscale/Netbird-class), pluggable DNS providers, and Junction dynamic DNS for federation without shared mutable control state.

## Secretless connectors

Workloads use connector plugins (postgres/tcp/mysql/redis, …) that dial **names**. Classical URL+password is residual and audited.

## Isolation & PAM

Environment isolation tiers + optional Privileged Access Gateway sessions. Cross-Station dials need federation grants.

## Local DX

`hobo dev` registers named endpoints; optional portless mode; `HOBO_PORTLESS=0` forces ports. `hobo doctor` reports connectivity hazards.

## Related

[Connectivity reference](/HoBo/reference/connectivity/) · [Security](/HoBo/security/) · [Stations](/HoBo/primitives/stations/)

---

<!-- Security · Agent credentials · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/security/credentials/ -->

# Agent credentials

Agents are first-class principals. They receive **scoped, short-lived** credentials — never ambient org-admin by default.

## Issuance loop

1. Agent authenticates (SVIDs / OIDC device flows as applicable). 
2. Declares needed capabilities for the task. 
3. Policy allow / deny / require-approval. 
4. Broker issues time-boxed token/scopes. 
5. Audit refs only in the log. 

## Rules

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Least privilege | Scope to tools + resources needed |
| Short TTL | Rotate; no long-lived agent PATs as default |
| No plaintext in context | Schema-only views and fixtures for secrets |
| Spend caps | Policy breakers on runaway tool use |
| MCP auth | Same policy plane as CLI |

## Related

[Agents overview](/HoBo/agents/) · [MCP](/HoBo/agents/mcp/) · [Identity](/HoBo/security/identity/) · [Audit](/HoBo/observability/agent-audit/)

# CI/CD & continuous delivery

Placement and delivery are **standing decisions**. Deploy, migrate, and progressive rollout share one gated path.

| [Deployment rehearsal](/HoBo/testing/deployment/) | Offline plan / local lane / Gatekeeper tests |

<!-- CI/CD · Continuous migration · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/cicd/migration/ -->

# Continuous migration

HoBo’s differentiator: placement is a **standing decision**, not a historical one. When a cheaper or better-policy home opens, the platform plans the move, gates it, and converges — without a rewrite or a weekend war room.

## Same path as deploy

| Step | Deploy (`hobo up`) | Continuous migrate |
|---|---|---|
| Plan | DeploymentPlan DAG | Same |
| Gate | Gatekeeper | Same (+ can-migrate / can-trail as needed) |
| Converge | ResourceActors | Same |
| Observe | Events + inspect | Same |

There is **no** separate migration engine with different trust properties.

## What triggers re-placement

- Price / credit / free-tier ranking updates (as **ranking input**, dated sources)
- Policy or residency changes
- Reliability / SLO signals
- Explicit human or Crew proposal
- Trail recipe readiness

Dispatcher owns continuous re-entry; FinOps Crew **advises**.

## Dual windows

Schema/data duals, identity dual-path, and traffic duals (Harness weights) let you run old and new in parallel until cutover gates pass. Fail closed on integrity — never “best effort drop events.”

## Trails

App-owned recipes compose platform steps (schema dual, junction rebind, `identity.continuous`, progressive cutover). Pure identity continuous still requires **zero** Trail authoring. See [Trails](/HoBo/primitives/trails/).

## What migration is not

- Not downtime-required by default (progressive + dual)
- Not a free pass around can-deploy
- Not silent rebinding of external customer domains without policy
- Not account-hopping within a provider to reset free tiers

## Testing

[Migration fixtures](/HoBo/testing/migration/) · [Dual fixtures](/HoBo/testing/dual-fixtures/) · [Deployment rehearsal](/HoBo/testing/deployment/)

## Related

[Progressive delivery](/HoBo/cicd/progressive-delivery/) · [Control plane](/HoBo/architecture/control-plane/) · [Matching](/HoBo/reference/matching/)

---

<!-- CI/CD · Progressive delivery · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/cicd/progressive-delivery/ -->

# Progressive delivery

Progressive delivery is how HoBo shifts **traffic, flags, and contract observation** without treating every change as a big-bang deploy.

## Building blocks

| Block | Role |
|---|---|
| **Harness flags** | Ranked evaluation with audit facts |
| **Experiments** | Bounded exposure |
| **Gateway weights** | Split traffic across revisions/camps |
| **Sandbox lanes** | Isolate experimental observations |
| **Trails** | Multi-step cutover recipes when infra + data move together |
| **Gatekeeper** | Still admits infra mutations |

## Safe defaults

1. Baseline contracts ignore sandbox-lane events.
2. Flag and weight changes are **events** — replayable.
3. Auto-rollback hooks pair with canary live-fix (Crew SRE path).
4. Prod writes often `require-approval` under policy packs.

## CLI

- `hobo feature …` — flags / progressive ops 
- `hobo trails plan|status|inspect` — recipe observation 
- `hobo inspect` — projections and time-travel 

## Testing

Shadow Bridge mode, dual fixtures (flag on/off), and chaos partial shifts. See [Harness reference](/HoBo/reference/harness/) · [Bridge modes](/HoBo/testing/bridge-modes/).

## Related

[Continuous migration](/HoBo/cicd/migration/) · [Trails](/HoBo/primitives/trails/) · [Crew SRE](/HoBo/operations/sre/)

---

<!-- CI/CD · Generation pipeline · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/cicd/generation/ -->

# Generation pipeline

HoBo treats AI generation as a **governed factory**, not a paste bin. Generated providers, patches, and app assistance run under the same contract, policy, and audit spine as human work.

## Loop (conceptual)

1. Request generation (`hobo generate` / MCP / Crew SWE·UX)
2. Produce candidate artifacts in a **sandbox lane**
3. Conformance + tests + SBOM/vuln gates
4. Human or policy approval when required
5. Registry certification / promote out of sandbox
6. Patchability preserved — generated code is not a black box seal

## Guardrails

- Prompt/tool safety → `guardrail.Blocked` + `policy.Decided`
- Capability Manifest prose is untrusted input (injection-aware)
- No ambient credentials in generation executors
- Training trajectories exclude sandbox poison by default

## What generation must not claim

- Silent production mutate without Gatekeeper
- Skipping conformance because “the model was confident”
- Embedding secrets into generated IaC or docs

## Related

[Progressive delivery](/HoBo/cicd/progressive-delivery/) · [SWE Crew](/HoBo/operations/swe/) · [Security](/HoBo/security/) · [Conformance testing](/HoBo/testing/conformance/)
