<!-- Primitives · Bindles · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/primitives/bindles/ -->

# Bindles

> *A hobo's bindle is everything they own, tied to a stick. If it doesn't fit in the bindle, it doesn't come along.*

The **Bindle** is HoBo's first primitive and the only thing HoBo ships. It's your whole application — services, resources, wiring, policies, deployment intent — packed into one **provider-agnostic** bundle. You cannot run HoBo without one, and the discipline it imposes is the whole business model: an app that fits in its bindle is an app that's cheap to move, and an app that's cheap to move is an app whose rent goes down.

## Declaring a bindle

A bindle is plain code, and this surface ships today in `hobo/bindles`: the default export of your project's `src/bindle.ts` is exactly what `hobo collect`, `hobo plan`, `hobo up`, and `hobo dev` load (a committed `hobo.bindle.json` manifest artifact wins when present). `bindle(name, build)` hands your build function a resource builder; the object you return *is* the manifest:

```ts
import { bindle } from "hobo/bindles";

import { app as api } from "./api";
import { app as web } from "./webapp";

export default bindle("my-app", (b) => {
 const db = b.data().allow("read", "write");
 const jobs = b.queue().allow("enqueue");
 const cache = b.kv().allow("get", "set");
 const uploads = b.bucket();
 const apiKey = b.secret().allow("access");

 const apiSvc = b
.api(() => api.fetch)
.dependsOn(db, jobs, cache, apiKey);

 const webSvc = b.web(() => web.fetch).dependsOn(apiSvc);

 return { db, jobs, cache, uploads, apiKey, api: apiSvc, web: webSvc };
});
```

## App Kits vs Infra Kits

Resources fall into two authoring families:

| Family | Kinds | Session Replay |
|---|---|---|
| **[App Kits](/HoBo/primitives/app-kits/)** | `api`, `web`, `service`, `ui`, `websocket`, `job`, `wasm-component` | **Default-on** (privacy-first) |
| **Infra Kits** | `data`, `kv`, `bucket`, `queue`, `topic`, `secret`, … | Off unless explicitly annotated |

WIT/WASM is how ports and providers link at runtime; App Kits are the Bindle-facing surfaces you declare.

## The builder surface

| Builder | Kind | Family | What it declares |
|---|---|---|---|
| `b.api(handler?)` | `api` | App Kit | HTTP API entrypoint. **Session Replay default-on.** |
| `b.web(handler?)` | `web` | App Kit | Web app entrypoint. **Session Replay default-on.** |
| `b.service(handler?)` | `service` | App Kit | Long-running service. **Session Replay default-on.** |
| `b.data()` | `data` | Infra Kit | A SQL-ish managed data port. |
| `b.kv()` | `kv` | Infra Kit | Key-value storage. |
| `b.bucket()` | `bucket` | Infra Kit | Object storage. |
| `b.queue()` | `queue` | Infra Kit | Point-to-point work queue. |
| `b.topic()` | `topic` | Infra Kit | Pub/sub topic. |
| `b.secret()` | `secret` | Infra Kit | A secret reference — never a secret value. |

Every resource supports three chainable refinements:

| Method | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `.dependsOn(...resources)` | Declares wiring edges **and** injects typed bindings at runtime. Deny-by-default: no declared edge, no access. |
| `.allow(...verbs)` | Inline least privilege, with verbs typed per resource kind (`"read"`/`"write"`/`"query"` on `data`, `"enqueue"`/`"dequeue"` on `queue`, `"get"`/`"set"` on `kv`, …). Permissions travel in the bindle. |
| `.with(...annotations)` | Typed provider-specific options — the escape hatch. Includes `sessionReplay(...)` to opt a Kit out of Session Replay or set sample rate. |

## Session Replay on every App Kit

Every App Kit is annotated with platform option `session-replay` by default — **api, web, service, ui, websocket, job, wasm-component**, not only `web`. Local `hobo dev` wraps HTTP App Kits: HTML gets a privacy-first bootstrap; `/__hobo/replay/*` serves ingest/list — **no app tracker code required**.

```ts
import { sessionReplay } from "hobo/bindles";

// opt out one Kit
b.api(() => handler).with(sessionReplay({ enabled: false }));
```

Details: [Session Replay](/HoBo/reference/session-replay/) · [App Kits](/HoBo/primitives/app-kits/).

## Greenfield: declare the bindle, generate the code

Packing an existing app — the brownfield path above — is only half the story. A component can also be **declared**: a `@component` class whose `@operation` methods carry the groundings HoBo generates code from — an **intent** (what it's for, in prose), a **contract declaring the shape** (typed input and output, plus invariants and forbidden outputs — the boundary generated code may never cross; the shape is never optional), and an optional **rubric** (named scorers with promotion thresholds, enforced as policy at the gate — omit it and the gate defaults to exact-match over your contract's examples). An operation with a `stub()` body is **code to be generated**; a hand-written body is a baseline the optimizer improves.

```ts
import { bindle } from "hobo/bindles";
import { component, operation, param, stub } from "hobo/runtime";
import { z } from "zod";
import { Cart, Order, Photo, RankInput, submitOrder } from "./domain";

@component({ intent: "Public storefront API: ranked feed, cart, checkout." })
class Storefront {
 @operation({
 intent: "Order photos to maximize dwell without burying brand-new sellers.",
 contract: {
 input: RankInput, // the shape — required
 output: z.array(Photo),
 forbiddenOutputs: ["output[0] is nsfw"],
 },
 params: { input: param("Candidate photos with engagement signals") },
 rubric: { dwellLift: 0.8, newSellerShare: 0.75 }, // optional — sharpens the gate
 })
 rankFeed = stub<RankInput, Photo[]>(); // no implementation: generate it

 @operation({
 intent: "Turn a priced cart into an order exactly once.",
 contract: { input: Cart, output: Order },
 })
 async checkout(cart: Cart): Promise<Order> {
 "use training"; // hand-written baseline the optimizer keeps improving
 return submitOrder(cart);
 }
}

/** The bindle hands the declared component straight to the builder. */
export default bindle("snapshop", (b) => {
 const photos = b.bucket();
 const catalog = b.data().allow("read", "write");
 const api = b.api(Storefront).dependsOn(catalog, photos);
 return { photos, catalog, api };
});
```

`rankFeed` has zero implementation, and the loop from declaration to running code is the same convergence loop as everything else in HoBo:

1. **Declare.** The bindle above is a complete, plannable manifest — `hobo plan` and `hobo up` work on it unchanged. Under the hood each `@operation` lowers to a **trainable** bound to its resource — signature-only for stubbed operations. That's the same machinery as `"use training"`, but you never touch it directly.
2. **Stub.** `hobo stub` emits the generated registrations and a typed client into your project's generated output. Every declared operation is servable from day one by a **contract-derived stub**, so the whole app runs end-to-end before any implementation exists — and every stub call is recorded as a **specification-by-example** trace.
3. **Generate.** The same **generation pipeline** that writes [provider adapters](/HoBo/customizations/providers/) synthesizes each operation's implementation from its interface + contract + recorded traces, in a capability-scoped sandbox with no egress.
4. **Gate.** Promotion needs all three lenses: **conformance green** (the contract must never break), **eval thresholds met** (the rubric — scorer by scorer), and **policy allows** (prod promotions can require human approval).
5. **Promote.** A passing candidate is written back into the operation's generated region as an AST-aware edit with signed provenance — auto-applied when low-risk, raised as a PR when not. Prior candidates live in the event log, so promotion is reversible.

Prefer declaring one grounding at a time? Every decorator is optional and the options object decomposes into **granular decorators** — `@intent`, `@returns` on methods, `@description` on parameters (in legacy-decorator projects; as a `params:` value under standard decorators), with a bare `@trainable` composing the class. The declaration can even be **ambient** — a `declare class` with only signatures, no bodies at all — which `hobo stub` scans statically, taking the TypeScript signature as the declared shape:

```ts
@trainable
export declare class Program {
 @intent("Produce a simple hello-world program")
 @returns("Hello World! or Hello, <name>! when supplied")
 trainableMethod(
 @description("Optional person to greet")
 name?: string,
 ): string;
}
```

Anything you don't declare is inferred: intent from the method name, a synthesized `decl://` contract ref, the default exact-match rubric.

Escalation is **per operation, not per app** — `Storefront` above already shows all three rungs. Swap `rankFeed`'s `stub()` for a real body when you're ready to own it; keep `"use training"` on it (like `checkout`) and the optimizer keeps improving the body against the same intent + contract + rubric, under the same gates; drop the directive and it's plain hand-maintained code. The manifest never changes shape along the way.

Brownfield and greenfield converge on the same artifact: one manifest, one `hobo up`, one event log. Pack code you have, declare code you don't, and mix freely — a half-implemented bindle is a normal bindle.

## Rules the bindle enforces

- **Names come from the returned object keys.** `{ db, api }` yields stable IDs like `data:db` and `api:api`. Duplicate stable IDs are a hard error.
- **The manifest is pure data.** Serializing a bindle yields exactly `{ name, resources, edges }` — handlers are reachable for tooling via `definition.entrypoint(name)` but never leak into the graph.
- **Everything is frozen.** A built bindle is deeply immutable. The manifest you planned against is the manifest that ships.
- **Provider-agnostic by construction.** Nothing in the builder surface names a cloud. Provider choices live in [Camps](/HoBo/primitives/camps/); provider *hints* live in `.with(...)` annotations, which any other provider is free to ignore.

## Why this shape matters

Every classic lock-in mechanism is a thing that lives *outside* your app description: the console-clicked queue, the IAM policy in a wiki, the env var that only exists in one region. The bindle's job is to leave nothing outside. When permissions (`.allow`), wiring (`.dependsOn`), and intent are all in the bundle, **unpacking it somewhere cheaper is a mechanical operation** — which is what lets [continuous migration](/HoBo/guide/concepts/#continuous-migration) be routine rather than heroic.

## Where bindles go next

- A bindle needs a home: [Camps](/HoBo/primitives/camps/) — pitch one to pin placement, or let HoBo infer it from the code you've configured.
- Multiple homes under one provider: [Yards](/HoBo/primitives/yards/).
- Homes across clouds: [Junctions](/HoBo/primitives/junctions/).

---

<!-- Primitives · App Kits · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/primitives/app-kits/ -->

# App Kits

An **App Kit** (short: **Kit**) is a Bindle-declared **application surface** — the kinds that host entrypoints or interactive runtime behavior. Kits compose runtime ports into something you pack in a Bindle; providers implement those ports behind WIT interfaces.

## App Kit kinds

| Label | Kind | Role |
|---|---|---|
| API Kit | `api` | HTTP API entrypoint |
| Web Kit | `web` | Web / HTML entrypoint |
| Service Kit | `service` | Long-running HTTP service |
| UI Kit | `ui` | UI render surface |
| Realtime Kit | `websocket` | Realtime rooms / sockets |
| Job Kit | `job` | Batch / async work |
| Component Kit | `wasm-component` | Wasm component dependency as surface |

Helpers: app kit kinds and labels in the Bindles SDK.

## Infra Kits (not App Kits)

Infrastructure/port resources that are **not** entrypoint hosts:

`kv` · `bucket` · `queue` · `topic` · `secret` · `data` · `schedule` · `external` · `container` · `flag` · `auth` · `crypto` · `notify` · `guardrail` · `golden` · `experiment` · `rollout`

See infra kit kinds in the Bindles SDK.

## HTTP App Kits

Subset of App Kits that local Yard hosts serve as fetch handlers:

`api` · `web` · `service` · `ui` — `HTTP_app kit kinds` / `isHttpAppKitKind`.

## Session Replay

**Every App Kit** is Session-Replay capable by default: privacy-first capture, dual fixtures locally, progressive gating in production. Infra Kits are not auto-annotated.

Opt out per Kit:

```ts
import { sessionReplay } from "hobo/bindles";

b.api(handler).with(sessionReplay({ enabled: false }));
```

Kill switch: `HOBO_REPLAY=0`. Full surface: [Session Replay](/HoBo/reference/session-replay/).

## Naming split

| Term | Layer | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **App Kit** | Bindle authoring | Entrypoint-bearing resource kinds |
| **Infra Kit** | Bindle authoring | Port / infrastructure resources |
| **WIT port** | Runtime capability interface | Host/provider link for a Kit |

## Related

[Bindles](/HoBo/primitives/bindles/) · [Resource catalog](/HoBo/primitives/resources/) · [Session Replay](/HoBo/reference/session-replay/) · [WASM & WIT](/HoBo/architecture/wasm/) · [Core concepts](/HoBo/guide/concepts/)

---

<!-- Primitives · Camps · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/primitives/camps/ -->

# Camps

> *A camp is where you stay, not who you are. Good campsites are worth appreciating — and leaving, when the rent goes up.*

The **Camp** is HoBo's second foundational primitive: the answer to *what kind of home is this?* — environment type, requirements, and preferences — **not** which cloud account or which Bindle owns the slot.

Every running app occupies a camp, but **writing one is optional**: leave it out and HoBo infers a camp from policy and approved providers. You write one to pin environment semantics yourself, or because placement is locked down to explicit camps.

## What a camp is (and is not)

| Camps **do** | Camps **do not** |
|---|---|
| Name an environment (`prod`, `staging`, `pr-123`, …) | Own a Bindle |
| Carry `envType`, labels, require/prefer constraints | Select a cloud provider |
| Declare runtime **requirements** (substrate needs) | Embed long-lived credentials |
| Attach under a [Yard](/HoBo/primitives/yards/) | Mix providers in one camp |

**Provider selection belongs on the Yard.** **Bindles stay provider-agnostic** and are placed by deployment request — not nested inside `camp(...)`.

## Authoring

```ts
import { camp } from "hobo/camps";

// Environment shape only — no bindle, no provider.
export const prod = camp("prod", {
  envType: "prod",
  require: ["durable-storage"],
  prefer: ["low-latency"],
  runtimeRequirements: ["runtime-local"],
  labels: { tier: "gold" },
});

export const staging = camp("staging", {
  envType: "staging",
});
```

Attach camps when you author a yard:

```ts
import { yard } from "hobo/yards";
import { prod, staging } from "./camps";

export default yard("aws-east", {
  provider: "aws",
  regions: ["us-east-1"],
  camps: [prod, staging],
});
```

Then converge with the CLI:

```sh
hobo plan --camp prod   # dry run: placement, cost, warnings
hobo up --camp prod     # converge
```

> **Day-one path:** you often never write a camp file. `hobo up` / `hobo dev` against the default **local lane** infers a local camp and durable SQLite journal with no cloud account. Explicit camps matter when you pin multi-env topology or platform policy requires them.

## Rules camps enforce

- **One home at a time.** Mixing providers in one camp is invalid — that's what [Yards](/HoBo/primitives/yards/) (one provider) and [Junctions](/HoBo/primitives/junctions/) (many providers) are for.
- **Runtime is a requirement, not a vendor SDK.** Camps declare substrate needs (`runtimeRequirements`); engines that satisfy them plug in behind Camp ports (EventStore, Queue, ActorHost, Clock). The **local runtime** ships today; alternate engines (Postgres-backed, Temporal, Restate, …) are on the roadmap.
- **Environment comes from the name.** `prod`, `staging`, `preview`/`pr-*`, and `dev` get sensible `envType` inference; override when your naming is more creative.
- **Rejected at parse:** `bindle`, `defaultProvider`, `tiers`, and `bindings` on `camp(...)` — those belonged to an older model. Prefer Yard provider + Bindle deploy.

## Writing a camp is optional

- **Inferred camps (the default).** With no camp declared, the Dispatcher infers one from configured code and approved providers, optimizing for price under policy.
- **Locked-down placement.** A junction broker admin can require explicit, approved camps.
- **Local camp.** `hobo dev` runs your bindle against the local runtime — offline on your laptop, with honest fidelity labels where local behavior differs from cloud.

## Camps and continuous migration

**The camp is your app's current address, not its identity.** Because the bindle is provider-agnostic and every camp exposes the same runtime contract, the Dispatcher can propose a cheaper camp at any time — and the move is the same plan → gate → converge loop as `hobo up`.

## Where camps go next

- Provider scope and multi-region: [Yards](/HoBo/primitives/yards/).
- Multi-cloud federation: [Junctions](/HoBo/primitives/junctions/).
- Bindle authoring: [Bindles](/HoBo/primitives/bindles/).
- Trail map: [Status](/HoBo/guide/status/).

---

<!-- Primitives · Yards · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/primitives/yards/ -->

# Yards

> *The rail yard is where a line's traffic gets sorted. One company's yard, one company's rules.*

The **Yard** is where **provider selection** lives. It composes **one provider** with zero or more [Camps](/HoBo/primitives/camps/) and carries what is shared across those camps: policy defaults, identity scope, reconciliation, and provider-global networking. It is also, not coincidentally, where HoBo's control-plane scope shows up for that provider.

**Day one? You may not need this page.** A Bindle plus the default local lane is enough — [Getting started](/HoBo/guide/getting-started/). Come back when you pin a real provider or multi-region topology.

## Building a yard

```ts
import { camp } from "hobo/camps";
import { yard } from "hobo/yards";

const prod = camp("prod", { envType: "prod" });
const staging = camp("staging", { envType: "staging" });

// Provider is required on the Yard — never on the Camp.
export default yard("aws-east", {
  provider: "aws",
  regions: ["us-east-1"],
  camps: [prod, staging],
});
```

That's the authoring shape: a name, a **provider**, optional regions/labels/requirements, and member camps (may be empty for a requested shape before live camps exist).

## Rules yards enforce

- **One provider, strictly.** A yard cannot mix providers. Multi-region within a provider = several camps under one yard. Multi-cloud = several yards under a [Junction](/HoBo/primitives/junctions/).
- **Provider is required.** Camps do not carry `defaultProvider`; the yard is the only direct selection point.
- **Camps are shapes, not Bindle owners.** Attach env camps; place Bindles via deploy/converge, not by nesting `bindle:` inside `camp(...)`.
- **Provider-native properties are refs only** — no credentials in yard properties.

## When to reach for a yard

- **Pin a provider** for prod/staging fleets.
- **Multi-region:** `prod-east` and `prod-west` camps behind one policy scope.
- **Environment fleets:** prod, staging, and ephemeral `pr-*` camps that share identity and promotion rules.
- **Governance:** one place to enforce conformant provider builds across camps.
- **Self-host control:** run a local/bare-metal yard (`hobo yard …`) when you own the control plane substrate.

## The yard is itself a bindle

HoBo's control plane ships *as a bindle*. Self-hosting is converging that bindle into a yard you operate — same tooling app teams use. No enterprise-edition fork, no second product.

## Where yards go next

- Crossing clouds: [Junctions](/HoBo/primitives/junctions/).
- Environment shapes: [Camps](/HoBo/primitives/camps/).
- Machinery: [Architecture](/HoBo/architecture/).

---

<!-- Primitives · Junctions · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/primitives/junctions/ -->

# Junctions

> *Junctions are where lines cross. Nobody owns a junction — that's the point.*

The **Junction** is HoBo's most advanced primitive: the federation layer that connects [Yards](/HoBo/primitives/yards/) **across clouds** for hybrid and multi-cloud operation. Yards remain peers — there is no super-controller and **no shared mutable state**. The final edge of HoBo's scope model is federation, not containment.

**This is graduate-level wandering.** Most apps live happily in one camp for a long time; many never need a second yard. If you're just arriving, start with [Getting started](/HoBo/guide/getting-started/).

> **Early-stage:** Junction authoring now ships the authoring and inference surface — `junction()`, connectivity-tier selection, the federated DNS plan, per-yard plan extraction, and the trust/policy/registry federation records. It's a local derivation engine: each yard still realizes its own half, and the realization machinery lands with the multi-cloud stage (see [the trail map](/HoBo/guide/status/)).

## Wiring a junction

```ts
import { junction } from "hobo/junctions";

import awsYard from "./yards/aws";
import azureYard from "./yards/azure";

export default junction("my-app", { yards: [awsYard, azureYard] });
```

Just the members — connectivity is inferred. The junction reads the member yards' manifests and derives the cross-cloud connectivity plane (peering/tiering plus DNS), and **each yard realizes its own half**. Trust federation, signed policy packs, and signed registry bundles ride the same mechanism.

## Rules junctions enforce

- **Peer yards only.** A junction adds yards; it does not reach into them. Each yard keeps its own event log, its own control plane, its own blast radius.
- **No shared mutable state.** What crosses a junction is signed, versioned artifacts — policy packs, registry bundles, trust roots — not live coordination.
- **Policy at the border.** Data-residency, sovereignty, and egress rules attach at the junction scope: what may cross which border is an explicit, auditable decision.
- **The broker admin holds the keys.** Junction governance is also where camp inference can be switched off: a junction broker admin can require explicit, approved [camps](/HoBo/primitives/camps/), so placement stays a deliberate act instead of an inferred one. The lockdown is enforced by [the Conductor](/HoBo/primitives/stations/#the-conductor), and no narrower policy can switch inference back on.

## When to reach for a junction

- **Hybrid:** a cloud yard federated with the yard running on your own metal.
- **Multi-cloud by policy:** EU data in an EU yard, everything else wherever it's cheapest.
- **Credit surfing:** when your app's cheapest home this quarter is on the cloud that just handed you startup credits — and next quarter it isn't.
- **Exit insurance:** the practical difference between "we could leave AWS" and "we have left AWS twice this year, briefly, and nobody noticed."

## Junctions and continuous migration

A junction is where the guiding principle gets its full range. Within one camp, migration means rebalancing resources; within a yard, moving between regions; **across a junction, the Dispatcher weighs whole clouds against each other** — price, credits, egress, residency, reliability — and proposes policy-gated moves across the border. The same plan → gate → converge loop as everything else. The map got bigger; the walking stayed the same.

## Where junctions go next

- The vocabulary in one sitting: [Core concepts](/HoBo/guide/concepts/).
- The machinery that plans cross-cloud moves: [Architecture](/HoBo/architecture/).

---

<!-- Primitives · Stations & Conductor · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/primitives/stations/ -->

# Stations & the Conductor

A **Station** is the hard control-plane isolation boundary a **Conductor** occupies. It is **not** Bindle ⊂ Camp ⊂ Yard ⊂ Junction containment. The **Conductor** (sometimes called the broker in lower-level surfaces) is a **pure runtime** that mounts a Station client + active Rail(s), runs resolve/scale/deliver, and emits receipts that pin `stationId` + `railHash` (+ catalog/policy hashes). It owns no durable Connections or policy packs — the Station does.

## Station owns

| Asset | Role |
|---|---|
| Connections | Authorized dial/control relationships |
| Rails | Content-addressed profiles / pins |
| Bootstrap Rail | Initial trusted least-privilege profile |
| Local client state | Under `HOBO_HOME/stations/` |

Authoring and ops surfaces: `station()` helpers, Rails, local client, and Privileged Access Gateway hooks.

## Station CLI (ops/setup)

```text
hobo station init|up|down|status|rails *
```

These are **ops**, not app lifecycle verbs. Missing Station **fails closed** for control-plane work — run `hobo station init`.

### Profile requirements

| Field | Role |
|---|---|
| `defaultStation` | Which Station is active |
| `activeRail` | Which Rail pins policy/profile |
| `defaultBrokerUri` | Remote Conductor HTTP endpoint only — **not** a setup path |

Cross-Station Connection use fails closed without federation grant.

## PAM

Privileged Access Gateway sessions can be Station-aware — break-glass paths still audit.

---

## The Conductor

Somebody has to decide which provider hosts your bindle, whether a deploy is allowed, whether it fits the budget, whether it breaks a downstream contract, whether the app scales up or down to zero. That somebody is **the Conductor** — the one who decides which train you're riding. In code: **broker** (Conductor). Same component.

The Conductor decides *only* from the policies it is configured to maintain, while **occupying a Station**.

### What it does

It takes a brokering request — "place these resources for this [bindle](/HoBo/primitives/bindles/), in this scope" — and answers with exactly one of:

- a **Resolution Receipt**: per-resource placements (provider, region, SKU, price), pinned to content hashes of the provider catalog and the policy set — optionally **Ed25519-signed**; or
- a **Resolution Rejection**: machine-readable reasons from a **closed rejection catalog**, each naming the enforcement plane that refused (`policy`, `contracts`, `billing`, `placement`, `connectors`) with a remediation agents can act on.

Placement is brokered **per resource, across providers**. Spin-up/spin-down (`up` / `down` / `zero`) are Conductor commands; accepted receipts go to delivery (Argo CD Application rendering / live submission when wired).

### The five planes it wraps

| Plane | What it enforces | Default | Also shipped |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Policy** | placement, approvals, junction lockdowns | TypeScript policy packs | OPA/Rego fail-closed |
| **Contracts** | can-deploy compatibility | Gatekeeper / PACT | external Pact broker feed |
| **Billing** | budget, spend caps, quotas | in-proc billing policy | metered plane over usage facts |
| **Delivery** | rolling out accepted receipts | rendered Argo Applications | live Argo CD API, fail-closed |
| **Connectors** | external systems the Conductor may act through | connector registry | external catalog |

Unreachable external policy engines **fail closed** — no engine, no placement.

### Policies are layered — lockdowns win

Merge outside-in: **junction → yard → camp → bindle**. Choice-shaped fields can be overridden by narrower scopes; **restrictions accumulate** (denied providers stay denied). Junction broker-admin lockdowns cannot be relaxed by bindle policy.

### Connector registry

Connectors (GitHub App, Pulumi, Azure, Vercel, Cloudflare, …) are registered with **credentialRef pointers only** — never secrets in the registry. The Conductor brokers short-lived access through identity/Station connections.

### CLI

```text
hobo broker config [--init]
hobo broker up
```

Requires Station context when available (`HOBO_STATION` / profile / `--station`). With no cloud config, the local machine can register as a zero-cost local provider host so the loop is testable offline.

### Related

[Control plane](/HoBo/architecture/control-plane/) · [Security](/HoBo/security/) · [Matching](/HoBo/reference/matching/) · [CLI](/HoBo/reference/cli/) · [Connectivity](/HoBo/reference/connectivity/)

---

<!-- Primitives · Trails · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/primitives/trails/ -->

# Trails

**Trails** are app-owned, versioned continuous migration recipes (Trails package). They compose platform capabilities — schema duals, junction rebinds, progressive cutover, `identity.continuous` — without forcing Trail authoring for pure identity continuous.

## Step kinds (conceptual)

| Kind | Role |
|---|---|
| Schema/data dual | Open dual window; cut over when safe |
| Junction rebind | Peer routing change |
| Progressive | Compose Harness weights/flags |
| `identity.continuous` | Dual-path principal continuity |
| Custom recipe | PlatformRecipe catalog entries |

## Gates

- **can-trail** — readiness/evidence before run
- **Gatekeeper** — still admits infra mutations
- **Golden oracles** — pin expected plan/run verdicts in tests

## CLI

```text
hobo trails status|plan|inspect
```

Observe and plan; do not invent parallel progressive/ETL planes.

## Rules

1. Pure identity continuous still requires **zero** Trail authoring when Matching/policy drives dual-path continuity.
2. Trails do not replace can-deploy.
3. History and run state are facts — replayable.
4. Progressive delivery prefers existing Harness.

## Related

[Continuous migration](/HoBo/cicd/migration/) · [Harness](/HoBo/reference/harness/) · [Identity](/HoBo/security/identity/) · [Migration fixtures](/HoBo/testing/migration/)

---

<!-- Primitives · Resource catalog · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/primitives/resources/ -->

# Resource catalog

App resources are declared in **`hobo/bindles`** — the app authoring surface — not in lower-level runtime ports. Names come from record keys the builder returns; explicit Bindle v1 methods do not take resource name arguments.

Resources group as **App Kits** (entrypoint surfaces) and **Infra Kits** (platform resources). Ports and providers link via WIT/WASM ([WASM & WIT](/HoBo/architecture/wasm/)).

## App Kits

Entrypoint-bearing surfaces — [App Kits](/HoBo/primitives/app-kits/). **Session Replay default-on** for each.

| Factory | Role |
|---|---|
| `api` / `web` / `service` / `ui` | HTTP App Kits |
| `websocket` | Realtime Kit |
| `job` | Job Kit |
| `wasm-component` | Component Kit |

## Infra Kits

Port / infrastructure resources — no default Session Replay.

| Factory | Role |
|---|---|
| `kv` / `bucket` | Key-value and object storage |
| `queue` / `topic` | Messaging |
| `secret` | Managed secret resource (residual; prefer secretless) |
| `data` | Portable data dependency (paradigm chosen by Matching) |
| `schedule` | Time-based work |
| `flag` / `auth` / `crypto` / `notify` / `guardrail` / `golden` / `experiment` / … | Cross-cutting catalog |

## Wiring

| Method | Role |
|---|---|
| `.allow()` | Least-privilege capability grants |
| `.with(...)` | Provider-specific optimization escape hatch |
| `connector` | External dependency protocols (e.g. A2A/ACP for agents) |
| `config` / `env` / `secretRef` / `fromBinding` | Config references |

## Lowering

Collection produces provider-agnostic **manifest IR**. Planner lowers nodes to **ResourceIntent** for Matching, cost routing, and DeploymentPlan DAGs.

## What is not a factory

- `search` is not a top-level factory (search extensions are opt-in).
- Topology (`camp`, `yard`, `junction`) is **not** re-exported from bindles.
- Stations/Trails are not Bindle resource factories.

## Related

[Bindles](/HoBo/primitives/bindles/) · [Matching](/HoBo/reference/matching/) · [Config & secrets](/HoBo/reference/config-secrets/) · [Capability map](/HoBo/reference/packages/)

# Operations

Built-in **Yard operator agents** (the historical “Crew roster”) that detect, diagnose, and **policy-gated** remediate. Custom third-party agents live under [The Crew](/HoBo/crew/) (ACP).

## Roster

| Operator | Mission | Deep dive |
|---|---|---|
| **SRE** | Detect → diagnose → gated remediate | [SRE](/HoBo/operations/sre/) |
| **Endpoint Monitor** | Synthetics, SLO burn, drift | [Endpoint Monitor](/HoBo/operations/endpoint-monitor/) |
| **GitOps** | When/what deploys; promotion | [GitOps](/HoBo/operations/gitops/) |
| **Platform Engineer** | Definitions, packs, policy proposals | [Platform Engineer](/HoBo/operations/platform-engineer/) |
| **SWE** | Implement / refactor / repair app code | [SWE](/HoBo/operations/swe/) |
| **UX Designer** | UI against design.md | [UX Designer](/HoBo/operations/ux-designer/) |
| **FinOps** | Advisory cost & anomalies | [FinOps](/HoBo/operations/finops/) |

Also: [Shared model](/HoBo/operations/shared-model/) · [Handoffs & A2H](/HoBo/operations/handoffs/) · [Runbooks](/HoBo/operations/runbooks/) · [Engines & ports](/HoBo/operations/engines/)

## Guarantees

- Org RBAC — cannot exceed role 
- Event-sourced observations and tool calls 
- MCP tools where applicable 
- Engine behind a port (swappable) 
- Writes policy-gated (often require-approval in prod) 

## Related

[The Crew (custom ACP)](/HoBo/crew/) · [Observability](/HoBo/observability/) · [CI/CD](/HoBo/cicd/)

<!-- Operations · Shared model · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/operations/shared-model/ -->

# Crew shared model

## Identity & policy

- Each operator is a **principal** with workload identity and short-lived brokered credentials.
- Actions are deny-by-default RBAC on `hobo:*` control-plane verbs.
- Mandatory org policy is a **deny ceiling** — operators cannot widen what policy denies.
- Credential audit answers: *what did this operator access, with which token, when?*

## Event families

| Family | Use |
|---|---|
| `crew.*` | Roster-level: dispatched, proposed, applied/denied, handoff |
| `run.*` | Durable agent run lifecycle |
| Domain families | `incident.*`, `pipeline.*`, `deployment.*`, `gen.*`, … |

**No per-agent event silos.** Remediation facts stay on domain streams.

## Engines behind ports

| Concern | Default | Optional swap |
|---|---|---|
| SRE reasoning | Built-in | HolmesGPT adapter |
| Runbooks | Pipelines engine | StackStorm-class engines |
| Coding | Built-in / configured coding agent | External coding engine port |
| UI generation | `ui-render` adapters | OpenUI / json-render / mcp-apps |
| Cost advice | Built-in FinX projections | External recommender port |

Swapping an engine is per-Yard config; the deterministic core (events, gates, RBAC) stays.

## Decision pattern

1. Observe signal (projection, alert, burn, drift, gate fail).
2. Dispatch operator (`crew.AgentDispatched`).
3. Propose action + blast radius (`crew.ActionProposed`).
4. Policy decides (`policy.Decided`) → apply or deny (`crew.ActionApplied` / `ActionDenied`).
5. Escalate via `crew.HandoffRequested` (agent→agent or agent→human / A2H).

## Integration ports

Crew drives:

- **`issue-tracker`** — JIRA / GitHub Issues / Linear
- **`knowledge`** — Confluence / Obsidian / Wikis (runbooks, postmortems-by-replay)

Writes ride `crew.ActionApplied` + `policy.Decided`.

## Guardrails

Jailbreak/PII-laden prompts → `guardrail.Blocked` + `policy.Decided`, replayable. Operators stay sandboxed under AI governance.

## Related operator pages

[SRE](/HoBo/operations/sre/) · [Endpoint Monitor](/HoBo/operations/endpoint-monitor/) · [GitOps](/HoBo/operations/gitops/) · [Platform Engineer](/HoBo/operations/platform-engineer/) · [SWE](/HoBo/operations/swe/) · [UX Designer](/HoBo/operations/ux-designer/) · [FinOps](/HoBo/operations/finops/)

---

<!-- Operations · SRE · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/operations/sre/ -->

# SRE operator

**Mission:** incident detection → root-cause → **gated remediation**.

The SRE is the Crew member with the deepest product model: it binds alerting/SLO, live-fix, drift + auto-rollback, chaos findings, and pipelines into a governed incident lifecycle.

## Signals in

- `alert.Fired`, `slo.BudgetBurned`
- `resource.DriftDetected`, `compat.GateFailed`
- `spend.CircuitTripped` / cost degradation signals
- golden suite continuous failures

## Incident aggregate

Stream `incident:<id>` — single-writer, rebuildable from the log.

Lifecycle (simplified):

`Opened → Triaged → RootCauseIdentified → RemediationProposed → RemediationApplied|Failed → Resolved → PostmortemFiled` (+ `SLABreached` on MTTD/MTTR overrun).

Multiple alerts fold into **one** incident via correlation/causation IDs — not N pages.

## Decision tree

```text
signal → open Incident
 → diagnose (projections; optional HolmesGPT engine)
 → classify (runtime + contract taxonomy)
 → decide:
 low-risk reversible → auto-fix (canary live-fix + auto-rollback)
 needs review → propose gated Delta/PR
 high-impact/unknown → escalate (on-call / A2H handoff)
 → policy gate always
```

### A2H (agent-to-human)

Escalate with a structured handoff: failing check, proposed fixes, blast radius, decision required. Routed over notify + obligation deadlines. Human apply / re-bless / abort is event-sourced. Security or money-touching goldens marked `requiresHuman` skip auto-fix.

## Runbooks

Trigger → diagnosis steps (MCP queries) → gated fix actions. Runbooks are versioned/signed, event-sourced (`runbook.*`), and built on the pipelines engine. Unmatched fix class → escalate.

## Failure taxonomy (examples)

| Class | Direction |
|---|---|
| Runtime regression | live-fix / rollback |
| Contract skew | shim / deploy-order / migration window |
| Drift | converge / gated repair |
| Cost-induced degradation | shed QoS via costAvailabilityProfile; propose rightsizing |

Unclassifiable → escalate; never silent action.

## SLOs

`sre.mttd` and `sre.mttr` as OpenSLO-style budgets. Burn can freeze risky deploys or deepen postmortem obligations.

## Postmortem

The incident stream **is** the timeline. Blameless postmortem-by-replay; failed remediations become permanent regression tests.

## MCP surface (illustrative)

`diagnose` · `heal` / propose remediation · rides `incident.*` + `policy.Decided`

## Related

[Endpoint Monitor](/HoBo/operations/endpoint-monitor/) (feeds SRE) · [Shared model](/HoBo/operations/shared-model/) · [Chaos testing](/HoBo/testing/chaos/)

---

<!-- Operations · Endpoint Monitor · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/operations/endpoint-monitor/ -->

# Endpoint Monitor

**Mission:** synthetic probes, health/SLO watch, drift surfacing — the eyes that feed remediation.

## What it does

- Continuously probes camp endpoints and critical user journeys.
- Emits burn/alert/drift signals (`slo.BudgetBurned`, `alert.*`, drift facts).
- **Does not** own remediation — it **feeds the SRE**.

## Why separate from SRE

Separation of observation and action keeps blast radius honest: monitors stay autonomous; fixes stay policy-gated. A noisy probe cannot silently rewrite production without the SRE decision tree and Gatekeeper/policy path.

## Engine

External synthetic-check providers sit behind a port; built-in probing is the default. Swappable per Yard.

## Events & consumers

| Emits | Consumed by |
|---|---|
| SLO burn / alert / drift | SRE operator, dashboards, status page pipeline |
| Credential audit on probes | Security review |

## Testing angle

Availability tests in CI often **replay** historical burn/resolution sequences rather than paging production. Live synthetics belong in real camps; see [Chaos & availability](/HoBo/testing/chaos/).

## Related

[SRE](/HoBo/operations/sre/) · [Shared model](/HoBo/operations/shared-model/)

---

<!-- Operations · GitOps · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/operations/gitops/ -->

# GitOps operator

**Mission:** drive *when* and *what* deploys; promote across environment groups under contract and policy gates.

## What it does

- Coordinates delivery pipelines and publishers (Argo/Flux-class engines optional behind a port).
- Promotes staging → prod **only** when `can-deploy` / Gatekeeper is green.
- On skew: blocks with a **precise, machine-readable reason** an agent can fix.
- Opens/rollback paths via MCP (`promote`, `rollback`) with policy checks.

## Gates it respects

| Gate | Why |
|---|---|
| can-deploy | Producer/consumer version skew |
| policy packs | Org deny ceilings, approvals |
| golden suite | Reproducible multi-check bundle |
| cost/quota | Budget breakers |

## Events

Rides `pipeline.*` / `deployment.*` plus `crew.ActionProposed` / `ActionApplied`. No separate GitOps-only log.

## RBAC example

Without Deployer role, GitOps may **propose** but not **promote**. Role bindings are mandatory-policy aware.

## Related

[Contracts & Gatekeeper](/HoBo/reference/contracts/) · [Deployment testing](/HoBo/testing/deployment/) · [Shared model](/HoBo/operations/shared-model/)

# Platform Engineer (Crew)

Authors and proposes **platform** changes: resource definitions, packs, policy pack deltas, Matching hints — not day-to-day business features (that is SWE).

## Mission

| Does | Does not |
|---|---|
| Propose policy packs | Silently weaken mandatory deny ceilings |
| Draft resource definitions | Bypass Registry conformance |
| Suggest Matching/Driver changes | Apply prod without obligations when required |

<!-- Operations · SWE · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/operations/swe/ -->

# SWE operator

**Mission:** implement / refactor / repair **business and message** code behind ports; generate per-language idiom-layer SDKs from `hobo:sdk` under conformance.

## What it does

- Opens gated Deltas/PRs for region-scoped AST edits with provenance.
- Runs implement / refactor / repair loops against contracts and tests.
- Generates language idiom layers — **only** promoted when conformance + eval + policy pass.
- Files issues on the issue-tracker port when human follow-up is required.

## MCP surface (illustrative)

`implement` · `refactor` · `repair` — each produces reviewable diffs, not silent production patches.

## Gates

| Gate | Role |
|---|---|
| Conformance | Port honesty |
| Evals / rubrics | Quality thresholds for generated code |
| Policy | Prod often require-approval |
| Golden | Regression lock |

## What it is not

- Not the Platform Engineer (platform definitions vs app business code).
- Not unbounded “agent with cloud keys” — short-lived credentials + audit.

## Related

[Generated stack concepts in Architecture](/HoBo/architecture/) · [Shared model](/HoBo/operations/shared-model/) · [UX Designer](/HoBo/operations/ux-designer/)

# UX Designer (Crew)

Generates and maintains application UI against design specs — for this site the Google [DESIGN.md](https://github.com/google-labs-code/design.md) contract is `site/DESIGN.md` (rubberhose / Steamboat Willie / Cuphead) — under the same guardrails and sandbox rules as other generators.

## Mission

- Propose UI diffs in sandbox lanes 
- Keep components aligned with design tokens/specs 
- Never ship unguarded prompt output to prod without policy 

## Boundaries

- Uses MCP/tools with scoped credentials 
- Pairs with SWE for behavioral code 
- Accessibility baselines are gates, not suggestions

<!-- Operations · FinOps · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/operations/finops/ -->

# FinOps (Crew)

The FinOps Crew member **advises** on cost and efficiency. It does not auto-spend, auto-destroy, or pool free-tier headroom across tenants.

## Mission

| Input | Output |
|---|---|
| Metering facts / showback projections | Anomaly flags |
| Price/tier ranking inputs (dated sources) | Move / commitment **proposals** |
| Budget policy | Alerts; breaker recommendations |

## Hard rules

1. Ranking input ≠ billing invention. 
2. Free-tier never pooled across tenants. 
3. Rotation across **providers**, not multi-account free-tier games. 
4. Enforcement via policy breakers/tiers — not chatty overrides.

## Related

[Metering](/HoBo/reference/metering/) · [FinOps role](/HoBo/roles/finops/) · [Continuous migration](/HoBo/cicd/migration/)

<!-- Operations · Handoffs & A2H · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/operations/handoffs/ -->

# Handoffs & A2H

**A2H** (agent-to-human) handoffs are first-class: when policy requires approval or confidence is low, the agent opens an obligation with a deadline and an evidence pack — not a chat message that disappears.

## Loop

1. Agent proposes action (`crew.ActionProposed` / handoff request).
2. Obligation recorded (who, what, deadline).
3. Human approves, rejects, or amends with reasons.
4. Agent resumes from **events**, not process memory.
5. Satisfaction/closure is itself a fact.

## Rules

- Deadlines create operational urgency without silent auto-approve (unless policy explicitly says so).
- Evidence packs must be redaction-safe for the audience.
- Handoffs are not a bypass of Gatekeeper for infra mutate.

## Related

[Shared model](/HoBo/operations/shared-model/) · [Runbooks](/HoBo/operations/runbooks/) · [Policy](/HoBo/reference/policy/)

---

<!-- Operations · Runbooks · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/operations/runbooks/ -->

# Runbooks

Runbooks encode operational knowledge as **data**: trigger → diagnose → gated fix. Execution is event-sourced; write actions still pass policy obligations.

## Properties

| Property | Detail |
|---|---|
| Declarative | Steps and gates, not opaque scripts only |
| Replayable | What ran is in the log |
| Policy-gated | Prod fixes often require-approval |
| CLI | `hobo runbook` execute / replay |

## Relation to SRE Crew

SRE may select and execute runbooks during incidents. Custom engines can propose runbook steps; they cannot skip Gatekeeper.

## Related

[SRE](/HoBo/operations/sre/) · [CLI](/HoBo/reference/cli/) · [Incidents in shared model](/HoBo/operations/shared-model/)

---

<!-- Operations · Engines & ports · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/operations/engines/ -->

# Engines & ports

Every Crew member is **pluggable**: the Yard depends on a **port**; a default engine ships; operators may swap engines that pass the same contract.

## Why ports

| Benefit | Detail |
|---|---|
| Swap brains | Better model / specialist engine without rewriting dispatch |
| Testability | Fake engines in CI |
| Policy | Engine choice is still RBAC-scoped |
| Audit | Tool calls and outputs remain events regardless of engine |

## Patterns

- Default built-in engine per operator
- Optional external engines (e.g. HolmesGPT-class for SRE)
- MCP tool surface stays stable — engines are implementation
- Never give an engine ambient admin outside its role

## Related

[Shared model](/HoBo/operations/shared-model/) · [SRE](/HoBo/operations/sre/) · [MCP](/HoBo/agents/mcp/)

<!-- The Crew · Custom ACP agents · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/crew/ -->

# The Crew — custom ACP agents

**The Crew** (this section) is for **custom agents you bring** — ACP/A2A-connected, policy-gated, audited. Built-in Yard operators (SRE, GitOps, FinOps, …) live under **[Operations](/HoBo/operations/)**.

## Disambiguation

| Term | Where |
|---|---|
| **Custom ACP / A2A agents** | This section |
| **Built-in operator agents** | [Operations](/HoBo/operations/) |
| **Agents-as-users** (developer copilots) | [HoBo for Agents](/HoBo/agents/) |
| **`agent()` runtime primitive** | SDK — both kinds use it |
| **Relay** | Network proxy — *not* an agent |

## What you configure here

| Topic | Page |
|---|---|
| Agent-as-user identity & MCP | [HoBo for Agents](/HoBo/agents/) · [MCP surface](/HoBo/agents/mcp/) |
| Credentials (scoped, short-lived) | [Agent credentials](/HoBo/security/credentials/) |
| Pluggable engines / ports | [Engines](/HoBo/operations/engines/) (shared machinery) |
| Connector protocol (`a2a` / `acp`) | [Connectors](/HoBo/customizations/connectors/) · Bindle `connector(..., { protocol: "acp" })` |

## Rules for custom agents

1. Authenticate as first-class principals — never ambient org-admin 
2. Every tool call and token grant is an auditable fact 
3. High-risk writes pass Gatekeeper / policy obligations 
4. Prefer connector protocols HoBo owns (ACP/A2A) over inventing a private agent SDK 

## Related

[Operations](/HoBo/operations/) · [Security](/HoBo/security/) · [Observability / audit](/HoBo/observability/agent-audit/)

<!-- The Crew · HoBo for Agents · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/agents/ -->

# HoBo for agents

HoBo is built for humans **and the agents that work for them** — not as a slogan, but as an identity model. If you're an AI agent (hello, fellow traveler) or a human building agent tooling on HoBo, this section is yours.

> **Reading this as an agent?** The condensed, machine-readable briefing lives at [`llms.txt`](/HoBo/llms.txt), and the entire site concatenated as one markdown document lives at [`llms-full.txt`](/HoBo/llms-full.txt). Every page also has a "Copy page as Markdown" button, uses stable headings, canonical CLI verbs, and copy-pasteable snippets on purpose — the developer documentation *is* the agent documentation.

## Agents are principals, not scripts

The standard failure mode elsewhere: an agent runs with a human's long-lived API key, invisible to audit and unbounded by scope. HoBo's model (the full brokered-identity flow below is contract-pinned design; the shipping `hobo-mcp` binary runs today with a deny-by-default, scoped local-operator identity and audits every decision):

- **Own identity.** Agents get workload identity (SVID/OIDC), not borrowed keys.
- **Brokered, short-lived tokens.** Secretless-first — credentials are issued per task, scoped to the task, and expire fast.
- **Self-provisioning within policy.** A machine-readable **capability standard** describes what each capability needs, so an agent can request *exactly* the credentials a job requires — and policy decides whether it gets them.
- **Every action is an event.** Token issuance, deploys, migrations — an agent's whole working day lands in the same append-only, replayable log as everything else. "What did the agent do?" is a query.

## One surface, three doors

Every HoBo capability is reachable three ways, with identical semantics:

| Door | For | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **SDK** | code | The same typed objects the [primitives](/HoBo/primitives/) docs describe. |
| **CLI** | humans & scripts | The [canonical verb surface](/HoBo/guide/cli/) — deliberately small, stable to memorize. |
| **MCP** | agents | Ships today as the `hobo-mcp` stdio binary: the canonical verb set as tools, parity contract-tested — see [the MCP surface](/HoBo/agents/mcp/). |

No agent-only side entrance with different rules: if policy would stop a human doing it, it stops an agent doing it, and vice versa.

## The Crew: operators included

HoBo ships a built-in roster of operator agents — the **Crew**: SRE, endpoint-monitor, GitOps, and platform-engineer operators that run as autonomous, policy-gated services in the Yard. HoBo ships the operators, not just the APIs they'd call. Your agents can work alongside them, under the same identity model.

## Agents and continuous migration

The guiding principle — *find the cheapest home that passes policy, keep looking* — is agent-shaped by design. The Dispatcher that plans migrations is itself an optimizing agent under policy gates, and third-party agents can participate: propose placements, watch spend, pre-approve moves within bounds you set. The event log means every optimization an agent makes is attributable and reversible.

## Generating new homes

Missing a provider adapter? Agents can invoke the **generation pipeline**: synthesize an adapter for a port, then have the port's conformance suite certify it. A certified adapter is a certified adapter regardless of author — human or machine. More homes on the map, cheaper moves for everyone.

The full extension surface — every implementable port, the adapter-authoring path, the conformance bar, and the ACP/A2A protocol-connector integration points — is documented in [Custom providers](/HoBo/customizations/providers/).

## Contracts agents can read (and test)

When you call `hobo verify` / can-deploy or inspect a BoundaryContract, look for optional **effects** and **resilience** fields:

- **EffectSpec** — purity + domain I/O tags. Pure contracts isolate with zero infrastructure; network/storage domains imply harness mocks. Effect widening is a compatibility signal.
- **ResilienceProfile** — secondary retry/timeout/circuit-breaker metadata. Deterministic schedules only; **never** retry a `policy.Decided` deny or a terminal failure. Prefer reconstructing state from event facts over process memory.
- **EffectManifest** — exportable summary for policy, SRE tooling, and training trajectories (with redaction).

Durable Camp storage defaults to a **single-owner SQLite partition** behind EventStore ports. Do not assume multi-writer shared filesystems; do not invent parallel event-store engines when the ports already exist.

## Start here

- [The MCP surface](/HoBo/agents/mcp/) — the shipping `hobo-mcp` binary: stdio transport, the canonical verb set as tools, `HOBO_MCP_TOOLS` scoping, deny-by-default audited decisions.
- [hobo-code](/HoBo/guide/hobo-code/) — the interactive Bo session. Not a `hobo` verb.
- [`llms.txt`](/HoBo/llms.txt) — the machine-readable site briefing.
- [Architecture](/HoBo/architecture/) — package layout, durable EventStore default, contract effects.
- [Testing](/HoBo/guide/testing/) — effect-aware isolation and offline durability tests.
- [Getting started](/HoBo/guide/getting-started/) — the same ten-minute path humans take; it works verbatim for agents.

---

<!-- The Crew · The MCP surface · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/agents/mcp/ -->

# The MCP surface

HoBo exposes its control plane over **MCP (Model Context Protocol)** — and this surface **ships today**. The `hobo-mcp` binary serves every canonical CLI verb as an MCP tool over stdio, and every tool call dispatches through the *same command registry* as the `hobo` binary itself. Anything the [CLI verb surface](/HoBo/guide/cli/) can express, an agent can call over MCP. It isn't a chat integration bolted onto the side — it's a second transport into the same surface.

## Running it

`hobo-mcp` ships alongside the `hobo` binary and speaks the MCP **stdio transport** — newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 (`initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `ping`). Point any MCP client at the binary:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "hobo": { "command": "hobo-mcp" }
  }
}
```

Like the CLI, it defaults to the **local lane**: `plan`, `up`, and `down` converge against an offline Yard runtime with a durable SQLite journal — no cloud account required. Live deploy lanes are **credential-gated by environment**: Cloudflare (`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` + `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`), Vercel (`VERCEL_TOKEN`), or live IaC credentials.

## Tools = the canonical verbs

The tool surface is **derived from the canonical CLI verb set**, one tool per verb — `up`, `down`, `plan`, `dev`, `station`, `trails`, `replay`, and the rest (see [the hobo CLI](/HoBo/guide/cli/)). Parity is a contract, not a convention: a structural parity check fails whenever the tool set diverges from the verb set, so there is no MCP-only subset and no MCP-only side door in either direction. A tool call becomes `hobo <verb> --json` over the shared dispatch path, and the result is the same JSON envelope the CLI emits, returned as inert data.

Tool inputs accept `cwd` (resolve the project directory), `camp` (target camp), and `args` (extra verb arguments).

## Auth: deny by default, audited always

Authorization is checked **before** dispatch, and every decision is recorded:

- **Deny-by-default scopes.** Each tool maps to a capability scope. A call outside the caller's scope is refused (`MCP_SCOPE_DENIED`); a tool that isn't part of the derived surface is refused (`MCP_UNKNOWN_TOOL`). Fail closed, never fall through.
- **Every decision is an audit event.** Allow or deny, each tool-call decision is recorded with the principal, tenant, tool, effect, and reason attached.
- **Scope down with `HOBO_MCP_TOOLS`.** Set a comma-separated verb list (e.g. `HOBO_MCP_TOOLS=plan,inspect,logs`) and the served surface shrinks to exactly those tools — every other verb is out of scope for that server process.
- **Local-operator trust model.** Over stdio, `hobo-mcp` acts with the invoking user's authority — the same trust model as running `hobo` directly — bounded by the scoped tool surface above. `HOBO_MCP_SUBJECT` / `HOBO_MCP_TENANT` name the principal and tenant the audit trail records.

## What agents typically do with it

| Task | Tool |
|---|---|
| "Deploy this bindle" | `up` — the same convergence loop as `hobo up`; local lane by default |
| "What would change, and roughly what would it cost?" | `plan` — read-only dry run |
| "Tear the preview back down" | `down` |
| "What happened on the last run?" | `inspect` / `logs` |
| "Anything drifting?" | `drift` |

## Designed, not yet shipped

The fuller agent-identity design — workload identity (SVID/OIDC), brokered short-lived per-task credentials, and a machine-readable capability standard for scope discovery — is contract-pinned design, tracked on [the trail map](/HoBo/guide/status/). What ships now is the surface above: full verb/tool parity, deny-by-default scoping, and audited decisions.

## Reading the docs as an agent

This site is maintained as a first-class agent surface:

- [`llms.txt`](/HoBo/llms.txt) is the canonical machine-readable briefing — start there.
- Headings are stable; CLI examples use only canonical verbs; code snippets are complete enough to run, not fragments.
- The [primitives](/HoBo/primitives/) pages define the exact vocabulary the tool surface uses — bindle, camp, yard, junction mean the same thing to the parser as to you.

# Observability

HoBo’s primary observability substrate is the **event log** plus rebuildable projections. Metrics and traces export — they do not replace the log as authority.

## In this section

| Page | Topic |
|---|---|
| [Agent audit & replay](/HoBo/observability/agent-audit/) | Tool calls, token grants, handoffs as facts |
| [Session Replay](/HoBo/reference/session-replay/) | Privacy-first DOM/session reconstruction |
| [Metering](/HoBo/reference/metering/) | Usage facts and showback projections |
| [Streamer](/HoBo/reference/streamer/) | High-volume frames outside the domain log |
| [Endpoint Monitor](/HoBo/operations/endpoint-monitor/) | Synthetics and SLO burn |

## Principles

1. “Why did the system do X?” → **replay**, not SSH folklore. 
2. Crew and agent actions are facts. 
3. Sandbox lanes are labeled so experiments do not pollute baseline views.

# Agent audit & replay

If an agent acted, the log can explain it. “The model said so” is not an audit trail.

## What is recorded

| Fact class | Examples |
|---|---|
| Dispatch | `crew.AgentDispatched` (operators) / session open |
| Tools | MCP invocations + results (redacted) |
| Tokens | Grants by **reference** |
| Policy | `policy.Decided`, obligations |
| Guardrails | `guardrail.Blocked` |
| Handoffs | A2H request/resolve |

## Replay questions

- What tools ran between T0 and T1? 
- Which policy version allowed the destroy proposal? 
- What was the fence/deployment correlation id? 

Use `hobo inspect`, event exports, and `hobo attest` for external GRC — not screenshots of secrets.

## Related

[Credentials](/HoBo/security/credentials/) · [Event families](/HoBo/reference/events/) · [Crew shared model](/HoBo/operations/shared-model/)

<!-- Observability · Session Replay · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/reference/session-replay/ -->

# Session Replay

**Session Replay** reconstructs user DOM/sessions (and Kit-level interactive capture) for debugging and support. It is **not** control-plane event-log replay and **not** auth `session.*`.

## Naming split (critical)

| Concept | Meaning | Family / surface |
|---|---|---|
| **Event-log replay** | Fold durable facts for projections/audit | EventStore / `hobo inspect` |
| **Auth session** | Login/refresh/revoke | `session.Started` / `Refreshed` / `Revoked` |
| **Session Replay** | DOM/session reconstruction | `replay.*` + Session Replay |
| **App Kit** | Bindle-declared app surface (`api`, `web`, `service`, …) | `hobo/bindles` `app kit kinds` |

Heavy rrweb streams **never** enter the control-plane event log — only content-addressed blob refs.

## Defaults

| Environment | Default |
|---|---|
| Local / dual fixtures / Station air-gap / every **App Kit** | **On** (zero Bindle config) |
| Production / staging | **Off** unless OpenFeature `hobo.session-replay` or sample rate |
| Kill switch | `HOBO_REPLAY=0` (or flag false) |

## Deep Bindle integration (App Kits)

Every **App Kit** receives a default platform annotation `session-replay` at construction — **not only** `web`:

| App Kit | Kind | Default Session Replay |
|---|---|---|
| API Kit | `api` | **On** |
| Web Kit | `web` | **On** |
| Service Kit | `service` | **On** |
| UI Kit | `ui` | **On** |
| Realtime Kit | `websocket` | **On** |
| Job Kit | `job` | **On** |
| Component Kit | `wasm-component` | **On** |

**Infra Kits** (`kv`, `bucket`, `queue`, `topic`, `secret`, `data`, …) are **not** entrypoint hosts — no default Session Replay.

Local Yard / `hobo dev` wraps every **HTTP App Kit** (`api`, `web`, `service`, `ui`) so HTML gets a privacy-first bootstrap and `/__hobo/replay/*` serves ingest/list — **no app tracker code required**. JSON API Kits still expose the ingest path on the same wrap.

| Piece | Package / surface |
|---|---|
| Annotation helper | `sessionReplay({ enabled?, sampleRate? })` from `hobo/bindles` |
| Kit taxonomy | `app kit kinds`, `isAppKitKind`, `appKitLabel` |
| Runtime plan + wrap | Session Replay bindle integration |
| Local host | `hobo dev` / Yard entrypoints |
| Ingest path | `/__hobo/replay/*` |
| Response marker | `x-hobo-session-replay: 1` when HTML wrap applied |

```ts
import { bindle, sessionReplay } from "hobo/bindles";

export default bindle("shop", (b) => {
 const api = b.api(() => apiHandler); // API Kit — Session Replay default-on
 const web = b.web(() => storefront); // Web Kit — Session Replay default-on
 const worker = b.service(() => worker); // Service Kit — Session Replay default-on
 const cache = b.kv(); // Infra Kit — no default Session Replay
 // opt out one Kit:
 // const api = b.api(() => apiHandler).with(sessionReplay({ enabled: false }));
 return { api, web, worker, cache };
});
```

## Privacy (client-side before send/persist)

- Mask password / email / tel inputs
- Mask `[data-hobo-mask]`, `.hobo-mask`, payment autocomplete fields
- Redact `Authorization` / `Cookie` in network capture
- Continuous-identity **`principalRef` only** — no free-text PII

## CLI / MCP

```text
hobo replay doctor
hobo replay list
hobo replay get <sessionId>
hobo replay summarize <sessionId>
hobo replay open <sessionId>
hobo replay retention
```

MCP tool parity via canonical verbs. Player surfaces are read-oriented; mutation stays on CLI under policy/PAM. `hobo doctor` lists contract boundary ids.

## Event family (`replay.*`)

`Started` · `ChunkIngested` · `Ended` · `ErrorLinked` · `RetentionApplied` · `Accessed` · `Disabled` · `Metered`

## Composition

| Composes with | How |
|---|---|
| **App Kits** | Default annotation + host wrap on every Kit |
| **Station** | Isolation + local path |
| **Harness / OpenFeature** | Prod enablement + sampling |
| **Trails** | Platform recipe `replay.retention` |
| **Continuous identity** | Principal refs only |
| **Metering** | Ingest bytes, storage, player access |
| **PAM** | Access policy for open/list |
| **PACT** | Integration boundaries via the replay HTTP surface |

## Performance budget (targets)

| Metric | Budget |
|---|---|
| Batch interval | 1000 ms |
| Batch size | 50 events |
| Main-thread per flush | ≤ 16 ms |
| Tracker overhead beyond rrweb | ≤ ~15 KB gzipped |

## Honest scope

- Live multi-cloud object storage + Junction federation: **ports present**; dual fixtures prove the path
- Full OpenReplay Assist / Helm stack: **optional**, not default
- High-volume product analytics warehouse: **residual**

[Bindles](/HoBo/primitives/bindles/) · [App Kits](/HoBo/primitives/app-kits/) · [Trail map](/HoBo/guide/status/) · [Harness](/HoBo/reference/harness/) · [CLI](/HoBo/reference/cli/) · [Event families](/HoBo/reference/events/) · [Dual fixtures](/HoBo/testing/dual-fixtures/) · [Stations](/HoBo/primitives/stations/)

<!-- Observability · Metering · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/reference/metering/ -->

# Metering

Metering turns **replayable facts** into usage evidence for showback, FinOps projections, dispute support, and ranking — **not** silent invoice invention.

## Model

1. Workloads and control plane emit usage-related facts (`meter.UsageRecorded` and related; also derived from `run.*`, `deployment.*`, `resource.*`, `gen.*`).
2. A **metering bus** fans out to sinks (in-process, export, warehouse adapters).
3. FinOps views (showback, anomalies, forecasts) are **projections** over facts.
4. Humans and the FinOps Crew **advise**; breakers, tiers, and policy **enforce**.

## Dimension matrix (required for M0 contracts)

| Dimension | Why |
|---|---|
| Tenant | Showback isolation + support lookup |
| Workspace / Project | Customer grouping and policy reconciliation |
| Environment | Prod vs preview vs test separation |
| Camp / Bindle | Operational and package grouping |
| Run / Agent | Runtime + AI attribution and dispute lineage |
| Team | Org-level reporting |

## Fact classes (examples)

| Class | Typical family | Sensitive? |
|---|---|---|
| Control-plane operation | `deployment.*` | No |
| Runtime compute | `run.*` | No |
| Storage / egress | `resource.*` | No |
| Generation run | `gen.*` | Often yes |
| Support adjustment | `meter.*` | Yes |

Sensitive classes require redaction/retention rules before customer export.

## Legal / ranking hygiene

- Third-party **price and free-tier** facts are **ranking input** with source URL + human-checked date — never fabricated “vendor signed” attestations.
- Free-tier headroom is **never pooled** across tenants.
- Rotation is **across providers**, never across accounts within a provider to reset free tiers.
- Metering/billing data stays **tenant-scoped**.

## FinOps Crew

The FinOps operator agent reads metering projections, flags anomalies, and proposes commitment/move advice. It does **not** auto-spend or auto-destroy. See [FinOps Crew](/HoBo/operations/finops/).

## Related

[Policy](/HoBo/reference/policy/) · [FinOps role](/HoBo/roles/finops/) · [Security](/HoBo/security/)

<!-- Troubleshooting · Common failures · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/troubleshooting/common-failures/ -->

# Common failures

Start with **read-only diagnosis**, then gated mutate. Prefer CLI verbs that emit machine-readable reasons.

## Quick map

| Symptom | First command | Likely page |
|---|---|---|
| Local env weird | `hobo doctor` | this page · [CLI](/HoBo/reference/cli/) |
| Deploy blocked | `hobo verify` / `hobo can-deploy` | [Contracts](/HoBo/reference/contracts/) |
| Policy deny | inspect `policy.Decided` | [Policy](/HoBo/reference/policy/) |
| Append fails OCC | reload & retry | [EventStore](/HoBo/reference/eventstore/) |
| `STALE_FENCE` | re-acquire lease | [ActorHost](/HoBo/reference/actor-host/) |
| DB won’t open | schema version / OPFS | [Schema](/HoBo/reference/schema/) |
| Control plane refuses | `hobo station status` | [Stations](/HoBo/primitives/stations/) |
| Identity dual weird | `hobo identity status` | [Identity](/HoBo/security/identity/) |
| Agent can’t tool | scopes + MCP auth | [MCP](/HoBo/agents/mcp/) |

## Gatekeeper denied

1. Read `gatekeeper.Decided` reasons (`gate` field). 
2. Contracts → fix producer/consumer skew (`can-deploy`). 
3. Policy → change pack or satisfy obligation — **do not retry** denials. 
4. Cost → quota/budget. 
5. Effects/resilience → visibility only unless configured as hard gate.

## Durability failures

| Code | Action |
|---|---|
| `OPTIMISTIC_SEQUENCE_CONFLICT` | Reload aggregate; retry decide/append |
| `STALE_FENCE` / `MISSING_FENCE` | Lease discipline — not OCC retry |
| `UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION` | Upgrade runtime to match DB |
| `PERSISTENCE_UNAVAILABLE` | Browser without OPFS while durable required — change mode or environment |
| `SQLITE_BUSY` | Single-owner violation or short busy timeout — check writers |

## Station / broker

Missing Station fails closed. `hobo station init` then set `defaultStation` / `activeRail`. Broker receipts must pin `stationId` + `railHash`.

## Still stuck

- Replay the stream with `inspect` 
- Check Crew handoffs for open obligations 
- File evidence with `attest` exports — not screenshots of secrets 

## Related

[Doctor in CLI guide](/HoBo/guide/cli/) · [Errors](/HoBo/reference/errors/) · [Anti-patterns](/HoBo/testing/anti-patterns/)

# Local debugging

## First loop

1. `hobo doctor` — environment, credential, and portability hazards 
2. `hobo dev` — offline local Camp / in-process handlers 
3. `hobo plan` / `hobo verify` — dry-run and Gatekeeper without cloud mutate 
4. Project tests — effect isolation, durability, contracts (see [Testing](/HoBo/testing/))

## Useful defaults

| Concern | Local default |
|---|---|
| EventStore | SQLite single-owner partition |
| Secrets | Schema-only view + fixtures — no plaintext in agent context |
| Session Replay | On for local dual fixtures (`HOBO_REPLAY=0` kills) |
| Named endpoints | `.hobo.localhost` |

## When local is green but remote fails

Compare Bridge modes and credentials — [Remote development](/HoBo/troubleshooting/bridge/) · [Remote debugging](/HoBo/troubleshooting/remote/).

<!-- Troubleshooting · Remote development · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/troubleshooting/bridge/ -->

# The Bridge

> *Tag your traffic, fork your boundary, keep everyone else live.*

Bridge to Kubernetes had one great idea: develop **one** service on your laptop while it participates in the **real** deployed environment — your requests detour to your machine, everyone else's don't. Its limits were structural: it worked by intercepting pod traffic, so it only worked on Kubernetes.

HoBo's version keeps the idea and drops the requirement. Every service boundary is a WIT port whose peers are PACT-emulable, and every boundary supports per-request routing modes (`live · mock · bridge · replay · shadow · fault`). Forking traffic to your laptop is just one more route — applied **at the WIT port boundary**, not in any orchestrator — so it works identically on any provider, a mix of them, or your own metal.

## The three moves

**1. Tag your traffic.** A dev session is a string — your branch name is the natural one. Session tags ride with requests (as baggage on wire transports; explicitly in-process). Untagged traffic can never hit a fork.

**2. Bridge the boundary.** Point the boundary at the implementation you're editing, scoped to your session:

```ts
import { createBoundaryRouter } from "hobo/runtime";

const router = createBoundaryRouter();
const payments = router
.boundary<Charge, Receipt>("payments")
.live(deployedPayments); // the version running in the camp

await payments.bridge(myLocalPayments, {
 session: "tyler/feature-refunds",
 contract: paymentsPact, // the boundary's PACT interactions
});
```

**3. Work against reality.** Your requests take the bridge; the rest of the team's — and production's — stay live:

```ts
await payments.call(charge, { session: "tyler/feature-refunds" }); // → your laptop
await payments.call(charge); // → the deployed camp
```

Tear it down with `payments.unbridge("tyler/feature-refunds")`. A bridge with **no** session forks the whole boundary — the classic "route this service to me" mode — and `unbridge()` restores it.

## The part Bridge-to-Kubernetes never had

A bridge is **contract-gated**. Before your local implementation carries a single request, it's verified against the boundary's contract — the PACT interactions every implementation of that boundary must satisfy, using the same subset matching as provider verification. A local build that would break consumers **never activates**; the error tells you which interactions failed, and your session's traffic keeps flowing to the live route:

```ts
await payments.bridge(brokenLocalBuild, {
 session: "tyler/feature-refunds",
 contract: paymentsPact,
});
// BridgeContractError: bridged implementation for boundary "payments"
// fails its contract (1 interaction): for input {"amount":42,…}
// expected {"status":"charged",…} ⊆ actual, got {"status":"declined",…}
```

And because **recording is always on**, every call your bridged session serves is captured as a specification-by-example trace — your dev session's traffic becomes tomorrow's contract candidates and regression inputs.

## Composing with preview environments

A dev branch's preview environment is a camp with your branch's session tag pre-applied. The two compose naturally:

- **Preview env alone** — the whole branch deployed, isolated, shareable.
- **Preview env + bridge** — the branch deployed *except* the one service you're actively editing, which detours to your laptop. Save a file, hit the endpoint, no redeploy.
- **Shared env + bridge** — the lightest loop: nothing deployed at all for your branch; just your session forked out of the shared environment.

## The rest of the modes

The bridge is one routing mode of six, and they compose per boundary:

| Mode | What it does | Use for |
|---|---|---|
| `live(handler)` | the deployed route | normal traffic |
| `mock(examples)` | serve PACT examples, no dependency | [unit tests](/HoBo/guide/testing/), offline dev |
| `bridge(handler, { session })` | session-scoped fork | local/remote dev |
| `replay()` | serve recorded outputs | deterministic re-runs |
| `shadow(candidate)` | duplicate traffic, compare, discard | testing the next version on real load |
| `fault({ message, session })` | scoped failure injection | [chaos with no blast radius](/HoBo/testing/chaos/#session-scoped-faults) |

`router.status()` reports every boundary's routing state — who's bridged, what's shadowed, which faults are armed — so "what is my environment actually doing right now" is one call.

## Honest status

The boundary router above ships today with in-process session tagging, and its tests are the executable example of everything on this page. Session baggage on wire transports, the `hobo bridge` CLI verb (open tunnel, register fork, stream contract verification), automatic pact-broker → bridge-contract conversion, and branch-tagged preview environments are staged next — the design is pinned even where the plumbing isn't.

## Related

- [Testing](/HoBo/guide/testing/) — the same modes, pointed at tests.
- [Core concepts](/HoBo/guide/concepts/) — WIT/WASM ports the routing lives in.
- [Custom providers](/HoBo/customizations/providers/) — why boundaries are provider-agnostic in the first place.

# Customizations

HoBo is ports-and-adapters all the way down. Customize by **registering** conforming engines — not by forking the control plane.

## In this section

| Page | Topic |
|---|---|

## Rules

1. Every adapter ships conformance suite for the ports it claims. 
2. Secrets stay refs — connectors use `credentialRef`, not ambient keys. 
3. Custom **ACP agents** live under [The Crew](/HoBo/crew/) — not here.

<!-- Customizations · Custom providers · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/customizations/providers/ -->

# Custom providers

Every place HoBo touches the outside world is a **WIT port** with swappable **adapters** behind it. A "provider" is just an adapter someone wrote — human or machine — that passed the port's conformance suite. This page is the map of the extension points and the path to certifying a new one.

## The ports you can implement

| Port family | What an adapter maps | Reference adapters |
|---|---|---|
| **Compute providers** | camps' durable runtimes — where services, actors, and workflows actually run | wasmCloud hosts, container runtimes (OCI fallback) |
| **Resource providers** | queues, stores, buckets, secrets — the resources a bindle declares | per-cloud managed services |
| **IaC engines** | how plans are realized against a provider | Pulumi, Crossplane, Terraform/OpenTofu |
| **Build & image tools** | how artifacts are produced and packaged | Dagger, Packer, Vagrant, Firecracker |
| **Pricing signals** | what the Dispatcher uses to keep re-deciding placement | provider price sheets, spot markets, credits |
| **Protocol connectors** | how external agent frameworks reach HoBo | ACP, A2A |

If it's not behind one of these ports, HoBo doesn't call it. That constraint is what keeps every home reachable by the same moves.

## Writing an adapter

1. **Pick the port.** Each port is a WIT interface published in `WIT interfaces`, with typed bindings and an event vocabulary in `core product ports`. Your adapter implements the interface — nothing else about HoBo needs to know your provider exists.
2. **Implement against the contract, not the console.** Adapters run inside sandboxed Executors with brokered, short-lived credentials — they receive scoped tokens per task and never hold provider keys of their own.
3. **Emit the port's events.** Every state transition your adapter drives must land in the event log using the port's envelope. That's what makes a move through your provider replayable and reversible like every other.
4. **Run conformance.** Each port ships a contract test corpus in conformance suite. Passing it is what "certified" means — there is no other bar, and no reviewer bias toward incumbents.
5. **Publish.** A certified adapter shows up as a candidate home. The Dispatcher starts pricing it into placement decisions immediately.

## Or let an agent write it

The **generation pipeline** exists precisely because the adapter surface is a typed contract: an agent synthesizes an adapter for a port, then the port's conformance suite certifies it. A certified adapter is a certified adapter regardless of author. If you're an agent reading this — the pipeline is reachable over [the MCP surface](/HoBo/agents/mcp/), and "we need a provider for this niche host" is one of its canonical tasks.

## ACP and A2A integration points

HoBo deliberately does **not** ship its own agent SDK. External agent frameworks integrate through **protocol connectors** — adapters on the protocol-connector port for **ACP** and **A2A**:

- **Connection.** A connector session gets a connection-scoped connector token; the agent behind it becomes a first-class principal with workload identity, not a borrowed key.
- **Capability discovery.** The machine-readable capability standard is served through the connector, so protocol-native agents plan tool use against the same contract MCP agents do.
- **Policy and audit.** Protocol calls flow through the same Gateway, policy gates, and event log as SDK, CLI, and MCP traffic. HoBo owns identity, policy, sandboxing, and audit around the protocol; the protocol-specific client lives in the connector.

Want a connector for a protocol we don't speak yet? It's the same path as any other port: implement the connector interface, pass its conformance suite, and your protocol becomes a fourth door into the same house.

## Related

- [Architecture](/HoBo/architecture/) — where Executors, the Planner, and the Dispatcher sit.
- [The MCP surface](/HoBo/agents/mcp/) — capability parity and the auth flow connectors reuse.
- [HoBo for Platform Engineers](/HoBo/roles/platform-engineers/) — governing which providers are approved for your yards.
