# IaC engines

Executors apply infrastructure through **IaC adapters** behind ports — sandboxed, short-lived credentials, no ambient cloud keys.

## Shipped / scaffolded

| Adapter family | Role | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **Pulumi** (Pulumi IaC engine) | Automation API — primary path | Live gated by `provider live credentials` |
| **Crossplane** | Kubernetes-shaped control | Design / stage-gated |
| **Terraform / OpenTofu / CDKTF** | Familiar plan/apply | Design / adapter scaffolds |

## Rules

- Executors run in Firecracker-class isolation when available 
- Identity brokers **scoped tokens per resource + action** 
- Drift remediation is gated the same as deploy 
- Never hand long-lived provider keys to the app or the executor ambient env

# Connectors

The Conductor acts on the outside world through a **connector registry** (GitHub App, Pulumi, cloud accounts, delivery systems). Entries hold **capability metadata + credentialRef** — never long-lived secrets in the catalog.

## Rules

1. Register → sign/provenance/conformance when required 
2. Broker short-lived access via Station connections + identity 
3. Fail closed when the connector or policy engine is unavailable

<!-- Testing · Testing overview · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/testing/ -->

# Testing overview

> *Trust the bindle, test the journey — without a cloud account until you want one.*

HoBo collapses a lot of “special testing tools” into one idea: **every boundary is typed and contract-backed**, so you can point it at a different **mode** (live, mock, replay, bridge, shadow, fault) without rewriting the app. The patterns below are deliberate product features, not ad-hoc test helpers.

## Mental model

| Idea | What it buys you |
|---|---|
| **Contracts bound shape** | Consumer-driven expectations; providers can grow without breaking consumers |
| **Boundary modes** | Same production code path, different routing (mock / live / replay / bridge / shadow / fault) |
| **EffectSpec** | Pure work isolates with zero infra; domain I/O drives automatic mocks |
| **ResilienceProfile** | Fault-injection guided by the contract; never retries policy denials or terminal failures |
| **Event log** | Replay-equals-live; inspection without re-running side effects |
| **SQLite journal** | Real durability semantics offline (CAS, fencing, atomic effects) |

## Layers (read in this order)

1. **[Unit tests & boundaries](/HoBo/testing/unit/)** — unit tests; boundaries auto-mock from contract examples.
2. **[Aggregates & CQRS](/HoBo/testing/aggregates/)** — pure decide, fenceToken, conflict vs invariant.
3. **[Contracts & PACT](/HoBo/testing/contracts/)** — consumer/provider executable contracts; subset matching.
4. **[Effect-aware isolation](/HoBo/testing/effects/)** — pure vs domain-effect harness modes.
5. **[Dual fixtures](/HoBo/testing/dual-fixtures/)** — pure path vs effect path from the same metadata.
6. **[Durable EventStore](/HoBo/testing/durability/)** — stream-head CAS, fencing, positions, restart.
7. **[Migration fixtures](/HoBo/testing/migration/)** — legacy schema → current, fail-closed integrity.
8. **[Queue, timer, outbox](/HoBo/testing/queue-outbox/)** — lease fences, once-after-restart timers.
9. **[Deployment rehearsal](/HoBo/testing/deployment/)** — `hobo plan`, local lane, Gatekeeper.
10. **[Bridge modes](/HoBo/testing/bridge-modes/)** — live/mock/bridge/replay/shadow/fault.
11. **[Chaos & availability](/HoBo/testing/chaos/)** — session faults, synthetics, shadow.
12. **[Property & model](/HoBo/testing/property/)** — journal ≡ reference model.
13. **[Behavior & Cucumber](/HoBo/testing/behavior/)** — Gherkin evidence, not live E2E.
14. **[Benchmarks](/HoBo/testing/benchmarks/)** — catch algorithmic regressions.
15. **[Conformance & golden](/HoBo/testing/conformance/)** — port suites + deploy golden gate.
16. **[Anti-patterns](/HoBo/testing/anti-patterns/)** — what not to do.

## What you should *not* do

- Hand-write long-lived mocks that drift from contracts — use contract examples / effect harness mocks.
- Treat `COUNT(*)` stream length or multi-writer shared SQLite as “the real” store — the product uses stream heads and single-owner partitions.
- Retry `policy.Decided` denials or terminal WIT failures in tests “to be resilient” — that is a **bug** in the product model.
- Run broad full-repo test sweeps to discover code — search first, then narrow package tests.

## Related

- [Architecture](/HoBo/architecture/) — EventStore default, package map.
- [The Bridge](/HoBo/troubleshooting/bridge/) — local/remote development on the same modes.
- [Reference: effects](/HoBo/reference/effects/) · [EventStore](/HoBo/reference/eventstore/) · [contracts](/HoBo/reference/contracts/)

<!-- Testing · Unit tests & boundaries · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/testing/unit/ -->

# Unit tests & boundaries

Your services, actors, and workflows are ordinary TypeScript functions. Dependencies are **boundaries**. Boundaries should be mocked from **contract examples**, not invented response shapes.

## Boundary router pattern

```ts
import { createBoundaryRouter } from "hobo/runtime";
import { expect, test } from "node:test";

const router = createBoundaryRouter();

const payments = router.boundary<Charge, Receipt>("payments").mock([
 {
 input: { orderId: "o-1", amount: 42 },
 output: { orderId: "o-1", status: "charged" },
 },
]);

test("checkout charges the cart", async => {
 const receipt = await payments.call({ orderId: "o-1", amount: 42 });
 expect(receipt.status).toBe("charged");
});
```

- Matched inputs return the example’s output.
- Unmatched inputs still get a correctly-typed canned response (first example) so tests stay unblocked.
- Greenfield **declared operations** work the same way: contract-derived stubs serve day-one traffic and record specification-by-example traces.

## Trainables

A `@trainable` / `@operation` contract’s examples double as its **eval suite**. Resolve the same instance by token in a test; those assertions are what the training loop reuses later.

## Aggregate / CQRS unit style

Write-model aggregates fold streams and emit past-tense facts. Unit tests typically:

1. Use an in-memory EventStore or a temp SQLite partition.
2. Acquire a lease (in-memory ActorHost for pure unit speed, durable host for lease persistence).
3. Assert appended facts and folded state — never assert on mutable read models the aggregate should not touch.

## Prefer package-scoped runs

```bash
run the package tests
run the package tests
```

Do not use full-repo test globs as a discovery tool. Search first.

## Next

- [Contracts & PACT](/HoBo/testing/contracts/)
- [Effect-aware isolation](/HoBo/testing/effects/)

---

<!-- Testing · Aggregates & CQRS · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/testing/aggregates/ -->

# Aggregates & CQRS

Aggregates are **single-writer actors**. Tests prove pure business rules and concurrency semantics without a cloud account.

## What to unit-test first

| Concern | Assert |
|---|---|
| Happy path decide | Given history + command → expected facts |
| Invariant reject | `AGGREGATE_INVARIANT` (or domain equivalent) — **not** retryable |
| OCC conflict | Stale `expectedSeq` → conflict; reload & retry succeeds |
| Fence | Stale/missing fence fails closed — **not** treated as OCC |
| Idempotency | Same key does not double-apply effects |
| Fold purity | Fold(events) has no I/O |

## Pattern

```text
history facts → fold state → decide(command) → facts
append(expectedSeq, fenceToken?) → store accepts/rejects
projection.fold(facts) → read model
```

Use in-memory EventStore + ActorHost for pure tests; use SQLite partition tests when proving durability (see [Durability](/HoBo/testing/durability/)).

## Multi-aggregate

Cross-aggregate workflows are eventually consistent. Test sagas with correlation ids and failure compensation — do not pretend distributed transactions exist.

## Anti-patterns

- Calling wall-clock inside pure decide
- Treating `STALE_FENCE` as “retry with same token”
- Asserting on projection without replaying from facts
- Sharing one aggregate stream across unbounded entity ids

## Related

[Data plane](/HoBo/architecture/data-plane/) · [ActorHost](/HoBo/reference/actor-host/) · [Unit tests](/HoBo/testing/unit/)

---

<!-- Testing · Contracts & PACT · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/testing/contracts/ -->

# Contracts & PACT

Every service boundary owns **executable contracts**. HoBo’s source of truth is the **Contract IR** (`BoundaryContract`). PACT documents are the common **export/import shape** and the local test harness format — not a parallel product model.

## Project layout

```text
your-app/
  contracts/
    inventory.md
    pacts/<boundary>.pact.json
    consumer/<boundary>.contract.test.ts
    provider/<boundary>.provider.test.ts
    provider/fixtures/
```

Inventory columns track boundary → consumer → provider → protocol → status (`consumer_tested` → `provider_verified`).

## Consumer and provider

1. **Consumer tests** generate or refresh the pact document against expected interactions.
2. **Provider verification** replays interactions against the real implementation with **subset matching**: the expected response must be a subset of actual, so providers may grow fields without breaking consumers.
3. The same interactions feed **[Bridge](/HoBo/troubleshooting/bridge/)** activation: a local fork must pass the BoundaryContract before carrying traffic.

## Harness

The contract harness parses pact documents, builds in-process consumer mocks, runs provider verification, and gates inventory drift (declared boundaries must match files on disk).

## Contract IR vs PACT

- **Contract IR** — versioned producer/consumer edge + shape + optional **EffectSpec** / **ResilienceProfile**; feeds can-deploy and Gatekeeper.
- **PACT** — interaction-level request/response evidence for a boundary implementation.
- Developers usually never “turn PACT on”; it is the harness detail under the contract engine.

## Compatibility gates

`can-deploy` / Gatekeeper answer version-skew: *will this next revision still satisfy deployed consumers?* Removed required fields and (when declared) **effect widening** are breaking. See [Reference: contracts](/HoBo/reference/contracts/).

## Next

- [Effect-aware isolation](/HoBo/testing/effects/)
- [Deployment rehearsal](/HoBo/testing/deployment/)

---

<!-- Testing · Effect-aware isolation · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/testing/effects/ -->

# Effect-aware isolation

This is one of the patterns that feels unfamiliar if you came from “hand-roll mocks.” HoBo puts **side-effect intent on the contract**. Tests read that metadata and choose isolation automatically.

## EffectSpec in one minute

A `BoundaryContract` may declare:

| Axis | Examples |
|---|---|
| **Purity** | `pure` → `varies` → `transacts` → `noRollback` |
| **Capabilities** | `decides`, `suspends`, `allocates`, `concurrent` |
| **Domains** | `network`, `storage`, `identity`, `policyEval`, `eventEmit`, `clock`, `agentTool`, … |

- Composition is **union** of callee effects.
- **Subtyping:** safer (fewer/purer) effects may be used where more effects are expected.
- **Widening** (pure → network, etc.) is a **breaking** can-deploy reason when effects are declared.

## Harness modes

```ts
import { createBoundaryContract, pureEffects } from "hobo/contracts";
import { createEffectIsolation } from "hobo/testing";

const pure = createBoundaryContract({
  id: "pure-math",
  effects: pureEffects(),
});
createEffectIsolation(pure);
// → isolationMode: "zero-infra", mocks: []

const net = createBoundaryContract({
  effects: {
    purity: "varies",
    capabilities: ["decides", "suspends"],
    domains: ["network", "externalCall"],
  },
});
createEffectIsolation(net);
// → isolationMode: "domain-mocked", mocks per domain
```

| Isolation mode | When |
|---|---|
| `zero-infra` | Pure contracts |
| `domain-mocked` | Domain I/O declared |
| `conservative` | Unknown / no usable domains |

## Resilience fault injection

Attach a **ResilienceProfile** (secondary metadata — not a new top-level primitive):

- Deterministic retry schedules (stable seed + budget + attempt facts).
- **Never** retry `policy.Decided` deny, terminal failures, or cancellation.
- Inspection is reconstructed from **facts**, not process memory.

```ts
// Fault-injection harness: one policy deny, no blind retries
await runResilienceFaultInjection({
  contract: netWithProfile,
  failures: [{ attempt: 1, failureClass: "policy.Decided", message: "deny" }],
});
// attempts === 1 — policy denies are never retried
```

## Capture without re-execution

Effect capture records `contract.EffectDeclared` / `contract.EffectInvoked`. Replay **inspects those facts** — it does not re-invoke handlers. That matches the product rule: inspection is event-sourced.

## Export

CLI and MCP can describe a contract or export an effect manifest for policy and SRE tooling.

## Next

- [Reference: effects](/HoBo/reference/effects/)
- [Durable EventStore tests](/HoBo/testing/durability/)

<!-- Testing · Dual fixtures · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/testing/dual-fixtures/ -->

# Dual fixtures

**Dual fixtures** keep pure and effectful (or dual-path identity) tests aligned from the **same metadata** so they cannot silently diverge.

## Effect duals

| Path | When | Infrastructure |
|---|---|---|
| **Pure** | `isPure` / no domain I/O | Zero infra; effect isolation harness |
| **Effectful** | Domains present | Automatic mocks from EffectSpec + optional live |

Same contract id, same examples, different routing. If pure path asserts X and effectful asserts ¬X, the fixture definition is wrong — fix metadata, not only one side.

## Identity duals

Continuous identity migration uses dual-path principal fixtures:

- Old and new principal shapes evaluate together
- Matching/policy decides continuity
- Offline fixtures extend without live IdP

## Migration duals

Schema/data dual windows: produce fixtures that assert both old and new folds during the dual period, then cutover.

## Session Replay duals

Local Session Replay (default on every **App Kit**) stores heavy blobs via **dual-fixture** adapters (memory/fixture engines) so privacy + tracker/player contracts stay offline-green without multi-cloud object storage. Production binds object-storage ports; dual fixtures remain the proof path. See [Session Replay](/HoBo/reference/session-replay/) · [App Kits](/HoBo/primitives/app-kits/).

## Rules

1. One source of truth for input shapes (contract examples / fixture tables).
2. Name duals explicitly in test titles (`pure:` / `effect:` / `dual-id:`).
3. Never hand-maintain two mock graphs that claim to be the same boundary.

## Related

[Effect-aware isolation](/HoBo/testing/effects/) · [Migration fixtures](/HoBo/testing/migration/) · [Identity](/HoBo/security/identity/)

---

<!-- Testing · Durable EventStore · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/testing/durability/ -->

# Durable EventStore testing

The Camp **EventStore** defaults to SQLite behind ports. Tests should exercise the **real semantics**, not an idealized in-memory fake, whenever durability is the claim under test.

## What “default SQLite” means

| Rule | Test implication |
|---|---|
| One **partition** file, one active writer | Don’t test multi-writer shared NFS/WAL as supported |
| Stream **head** holds revision + `owner_epoch` | Assert CAS; no `COUNT(*)` for revision |
| **Fence tokens** reject stale holders | Correct `expectedSeq` + lower fence still fails |
| **`global_position`** is store-local | Positions for catch-up ≠ ULID order ≠ domain identity |
| Atomic **commit** of events + effects | Rollback leaves neither events nor queue/timer/outbox |
| Snapshots are **caches** | Cannot write snapshot ahead of stream head |

## Where it lives

Exercise durability through the Camp EventStore and your package tests — not a toy fake of the journal.


## Minimum durability matrix

1. Append + read stream; optimistic conflict on stale `expectedSeq`.
2. Multi-event batch atomicity (crash mid-append leaves whole batches only).
3. Idempotency key retry returns deduped without advancing head incorrectly.
4. Fence: stale token / missing token on fenced stream.
5. `readAll(after)` positioned catch-up; checkpoint monotonicity.
6. Commit events + queue/timer/outbox; failure rolls all back.
7. Migrate legacy schema fixtures; integrity_check; reopen is idempotent.
8. Close/reopen file (and Worker recreate when testing browser).

## In-memory QueueClockStore

Runtime-local still has an **explicit in-memory** queue/clock adapter for deterministic pure unit tests. That is **not** the production durability claim. When the durable path is configured, queue/timer/outbox stage through the journal.

## Browser policy in tests

- `allowTransient: true` → in-memory journal for semantic coverage in Node CI.
- Durable required + no OPFS → `PERSISTENCE_UNAVAILABLE` (must not claim OPFS success).

## Next

- [Reference: EventStore](/HoBo/reference/eventstore/)
- [Chaos & availability](/HoBo/testing/chaos/)

---

<!-- Testing · Migration fixtures · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/testing/migration/ -->

# Migration fixtures

Migrations are product features — test them as such.

## Classes

| Class | Prove |
|---|---|
| **Journal schema** | v1 → v2 user_version; integrity checks; fail closed |
| **Event upcast** | Old body bytes → current fold state |
| **Identity continuous** | Dual principal fixtures offline |
| **Trail recipes** | `can-trail`, plan evidence, golden oracles |
| **Infra re-place** | Same Gatekeeper path as deploy |

## Fail closed

| Failure | Expected |
|---|---|
| Noncontiguous seq after migrate | `STREAM_INTEGRITY` / migrate fail |
| Opening newer DB with older code | `UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION` |
| Snapshot ahead of head | `SNAPSHOT_AHEAD` |
| Trail gate fail | No partial cutover mute |

## Dual window tests

While dual is open, both old and new projections must answer consistently for in-window subjects. Cutover tests assert the gate and the terminal single-path state.

## Trail golden

Trails package golden oracles pin plan/run verdicts for recipe shapes — treat like contract tests for migration recipes.

## Related

[Schema](/HoBo/reference/schema/) · [Trails](/HoBo/primitives/trails/) · [Continuous migration](/HoBo/cicd/migration/) · [Dual fixtures](/HoBo/testing/dual-fixtures/)

---

<!-- Testing · Queue, timer, outbox · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/testing/queue-outbox/ -->

# Queue, timer, outbox

Deferred work is where “it worked on my machine” goes to die. Prove lease and restart semantics explicitly.

## Must-pass cases

| Case | Assert |
|---|---|
| Enqueue + lease + complete | Happy path |
| Lease expiry + re-lease | Previous complete fails closed (stale fence) |
| Idempotent consumer | Duplicate delivery → one external effect |
| Stage in commit | Crash after commit still delivers at-least-once |
| Crash before commit | No phantom dispatch |
| Timer once-after-restart | Deadline fires once; no double-fire |
| Cron/schedule | Deterministic with virtual Clock |

## Transactional staging

Domain events + staged queue/timer/outbox rows commit atomically. Network I/O is **after** commit. Tests should kill the process in both windows.

## Clock

Use virtual Clock — wall sleeps make CI flaky and hide bugs.

## Related

[Queue port](/HoBo/reference/queue/) · [Clock](/HoBo/reference/clock/) · [EventStore](/HoBo/reference/eventstore/) · [Durability](/HoBo/testing/durability/)

---

<!-- Testing · Deployment rehearsal · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/testing/deployment/ -->

# Deployment rehearsal

Deploys are **plans before actions**. You can fail a gate without provisioning anything.

## Three speeds

| Speed | Command / API | Needs cloud? |
|---|---|---|
| **Plan only** | `hobo plan` | No |
| **Local lane** | `hobo up` / `hobo dev` against local Camp | No |
| **Gatekeeper** | `hobo verify` / Gatekeeper | No |

### `hobo plan`

Pure rehearsal: resolution, cost, policy verdicts. A blocked gate is a **no-op** on infrastructure — the plan output *is* the test result.

### Local lane

Full plan → gate → provision → deploy against the default local Camp. CI can run a complete deployment every commit without provider credentials.

### can-deploy + Gatekeeper

- **can-deploy** builds a compatibility matrix of candidate contracts vs deployed state.
- **Gatekeeper** composes: contracts · policy pack · obligations · cost/quota · optional secretless-config / can-migrate dimensions.
- Every evaluation records **`policy.Decided` even on allow** so “why did this pass?” is replayable.
- Decision payloads can include **effect summaries** when contracts declare EffectSpec / ResilienceProfile.

## What to assert in tests

- Breaking field removal → `compat` reasons with machine codes.
- Effect widening (when effects declared) → `effect-widened`.
- Policy deny → Gatekeeper `deny`; never treated as a transient retry class.
- Obligation pending → `require-approval`.
- Quota exceeded → `deny`.

## Suggested package tests

```bash
run the package tests
```

## Next

- [Reference: contracts](/HoBo/reference/contracts/)
- [Bridge modes](/HoBo/testing/bridge-modes/)

---

<!-- Testing · Bridge modes · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/testing/bridge-modes/ -->

# Bridge modes

Boundary modes are not only a test helper. They are the same routing model used by **[the Bridge](/HoBo/troubleshooting/bridge/)** for local/remote development.

## Mode table

| Mode | Behavior |
|---|---|
| **live** | Call the real implementation / deployed boundary |
| **mock** | Serve contract-conformant fakes (examples / effect mocks) |
| **bridge** | Fork only the tagged **session’s** traffic to a local implementation; must pass contract check before activation |
| **replay** | Serve recorded outputs; no original dependency required |
| **shadow** | Candidate receives traffic; output compared and **never** returned to callers |
| **fault** | Inject failures for a **session only** |

## Session scoping

Fault and bridge modes are **session-tagged**. Break a dependency for `tyler/chaos` without taking down production traffic for everyone else.

```ts
payments.fault({ message: "simulated outage", session: "tyler/chaos" });

await payments.call(charge, { session: "tyler/chaos" }); // fails for you
await payments.call(charge); // fine for others
```

## Contract gate on bridge activation

A bridge that would carry traffic **must** satisfy the BoundaryContract first. Failures surface as typed contract errors — not silent skew.

## Recording

Recording stays on: interactions become specification-by-example traces and training material (with lane-origin events excluded from baseline promotion by default).

## Next

- [The Bridge](/HoBo/troubleshooting/bridge/)
- [Chaos & availability](/HoBo/testing/chaos/)

---

<!-- Testing · Chaos & availability · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/testing/chaos/ -->

# Chaos & availability

Availability testing is the only layer that *should* touch real camps. Everything else stays offline by construction.

## Session-scoped faults

Use boundary **fault** mode with a session tag so chaos stays personal:

- Your session sees the outage.
- Everyone else keeps the live path.
- Results are events — not a screenshot.

## Synthetics (Crew)

The **Endpoint Monitor** Crew operator probes camp endpoints continuously and emits burn/alert signals that feed the **SRE** operator. See [Crew: Endpoint Monitor](/HoBo/operations/endpoint-monitor/) and [Crew: SRE](/HoBo/operations/sre/).

## SLOs as projections

Availability targets are **materialized views** over the event log. Test them in CI by replaying history — not by scraping a dashboard.

## Shadow lanes

`.shadow(candidate)` sends real inputs to a candidate implementation, compares outputs, and **never** returns candidate output to callers. Availability testing for the next version, paid for by the current one.

## Resilience fault injection (offline)

For contract-level resiliency metadata (not live chaos), use [effect-aware fault injection](/HoBo/testing/effects/):

- Transient failures may retry under deterministic schedules.
- `policy.Decided` / terminal / cancellation **never** retry.

## Blast radius rules

- Prefer session tags over global fault flags.
- Prefer shadow over dual-writing production responses.
- Prefer replay/fork lanes for golden suite failures before production self-heal.

## Next

- [The Crew](/HoBo/crew/)
- [Conformance & golden](/HoBo/testing/conformance/)

<!-- Testing · Property & model tests · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/testing/property/ -->

# Property & model tests

When unit examples are not enough, pin **invariants** across random schedules.

## High-value properties

| Property | Idea |
|---|---|
| Journal ≡ model | Random command sequences; store fold equals pure reference model |
| Fence monotonic | Epoch never decreases for a stream key |
| Positions monotonic | `readAll` positions strictly increase |
| OCC | Concurrent appends never both commit same seq |
| Codec round-trip | encode∘decode = id for supported codecs |
| Effect staging | Commit atomicity under crash injection |
| Idempotency | Keys collapse duplicates |

## Tooling notes

- Prefer deterministic seeds (resilience profiles already use them).
- Shrink failures to minimal command traces for humans/agents.
- Run property suites in package scope — not as default discovery diagnostics for unrelated changes.

## Related

[Durability](/HoBo/testing/durability/) · [Aggregates](/HoBo/testing/aggregates/) · [Benchmarks](/HoBo/testing/benchmarks/)

<!-- Testing · Behavior & Cucumber · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/testing/behavior/ -->

# Behavior & Cucumber

Behavior specs document **journeys** as executable evidence. HoBo does **not** use traditional live E2E against real downstream clouds in default PR gates.

## Allowed

| Pattern | Detail |
|---|---|
| Gherkin / Cucumber | Features under behavior specs |
| Playwright as **driver** | Browser UI with **mocked** service boundaries |
| Contract-derived mocks | From Pact / EffectSpec / fixtures |
| Local Camp lane | `hobo dev` / sandbox against in-memory or SQLite |

## Forbidden as default gates

- Real AWS/GCP/Azure mutates in PR CI
- “E2E” that requires live provider credentials
- Hand-written mocks that drift from contracts

## Behavior evidence

Behavior specs use executable features with contract-derived mocks.

## Related

[Testing overview](/HoBo/testing/) · [Contracts](/HoBo/testing/contracts/) · [Deployment rehearsal](/HoBo/testing/deployment/)

<!-- Testing · Benchmarks · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/testing/benchmarks/ -->

# Benchmarks

Benchmarks catch **algorithmic** regressions (O(n²) folds, accidental full-table scans, lock convoys) — not vanity ops/sec on laptops.

## What to bench

| Area | Signal |
|---|---|
| Append + head CAS | Throughput under single writer |
| Fold large streams | Snapshot amortizes re-fold |
| `readAll` catch-up | Position scans stay linear |
| Matching toy plans | Placement solve stays bounded |
| Effect lattice helpers | Pure CPU; should be boring-fast |

## Rules

1. Deterministic seeds and fixed datasets.
2. Report medians with clear environment notes — not single-shot peaks.
3. Fail CI on large regressions only when baseline is pinned intentionally.
4. Do not bench network to public clouds in default gates.

## Related

[Property tests](/HoBo/testing/property/) · [EventStore](/HoBo/reference/eventstore/)

<!-- Testing · Conformance & golden · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/testing/conformance/ -->

# Conformance & golden suite

## Port conformance

Every implementable port (runtime EventStore, provider adapters, IaC engines, …) ships a **conformance suite**. Human- and AI-authored adapters must pass the same suite to be certified. conformance suite hosts shared suites (for example EventStore append/idempotency/replay).

## SDK semantics annex

Resilience, cancellation, deadlines, lifecycle tables, and supervision are pinned by the **DX SDK resilience semantics** matrix — Contract-visible ResilienceProfile application **must** obey that matrix (never-retry rules, deterministic schedules, fact-based inspection).

## Golden suite (deploy gate)

The **golden suite** is a first-class Gatekeeper dimension: a signed, reproducible bundle that pins contracts, evals, conformance, benchmarks, chaos, and golden-master samples. Failures are structured, event-sourced, and can open Crew remediation (propose fix / A2H).

## Behavior / Cucumber

Executable Gherkin features live under `features/` for high-level evidence (durable journal scenarios, effects/resiliency scenarios). They complement package unit tests; they are not live multi-cloud E2E.

## What “green” means

| Lane | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Unit / package | Implementation correct in isolation |
| Contract consumer/provider | Boundary expectations hold |
| Conformance | Port claim is honest |
| can-deploy / Gatekeeper | Version skew + policy + cost ok |
| Golden | Reproducible multi-check bundle ok |

## Next

- [Reference overview](/HoBo/reference/)
- [Trail map](/HoBo/guide/status/)

---

<!-- Testing · What not to do · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/testing/anti-patterns/ -->

# What not to do

| Anti-pattern | Do instead |
|---|---|
| Hand-written long-lived mocks | Contract examples / effect harness mocks |
| `COUNT(*)` as stream revision | Stream head revision |
| Multi-writer shared SQLite over NFS as “HA” | Single-owner partitions; add partitions to scale |
| Retry `policy.Decided` denials “to be resilient” | Fix policy or satisfy obligations |
| Retry `STALE_FENCE` as OCC | Re-acquire lease; new fence |
| Live cloud E2E in every PR | Contract + local Camp + rehearsal |
| Broad full-repo test sweeps for discovery | Search first; narrow package tests |
| Wall-clock sleeps in pure domain tests | Virtual Clock |
| Assert process memory for audit | Replay events |
| Put LLM tokens in EventStore | Streamer |
| Bare `.hobo` hosts in fixtures | `.hobo.localhost` / `.hobo.test` |
| Invent parallel progressive plane beside Harness | Use Harness + Trails |
| Pool free-tier headroom across tenants in tests that claim “prod realism” | Model per-tenant isolation |

## Related

[Testing overview](/HoBo/testing/) · [Errors](/HoBo/reference/errors/) · [Security](/HoBo/security/)

<!-- Reference · Capability map · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/reference/packages/ -->

# Capability map

What you use day to day — **product surfaces**, not an inventory of private implementation modules.

## Authoring

| Surface | What you use it for |
|---|---|
| **Bindles** | Pack the app: services, resources, wiring, policy intent |
| **App Kits** | Entrypoint kinds (`api`, `web`, `service`, …) inside a Bindle |
| **Camps / Yards / Junctions** | Topology: home, provider scope, federation |
| **Trails** | Continuous migration recipes + live upgrade/migration executors (preflight evidence, expand→backfill→contract, pooled→siloed tenant moves) |

## Runtime (Camp)

| Surface | What you use it for |
|---|---|
| **EventStore** | Append-only domain and control facts |
| **Queue / messaging** | Deferred work and pub/sub |
| **Streamer** | High-volume frames (logs, tokens) |
| **ActorHost** | Single-writer leases and fencing |
| **Clock** | Deterministic time for workflows and tests |
| **Session Replay** | Privacy-first session capture on App Kits |

Default durable journal is a **single-owner SQLite** path. Alternate engines and component hosts (Wasmtime, OCI/Kubernetes, cloud-native) plug in behind the same ports.

## Control & identity

| Surface | What you use it for |
|---|---|
| **Stations & Conductor** | Control-plane isolation + placement decisions; routing control loop + progressive cutover |
| **Dispatcher** | Deterministic credit/budget-aware backend selection (`dispatch.Decided`) |
| **Jurisdiction & residency** | Region→jurisdiction catalog, per-tenant residency constraints, fail-closed residency gate |
| **Gatekeeper / contracts** | can-deploy and composed deploy gates |
| **Policy packs** | Deny-by-default authorization and obligations |
| **Identity** | Workload identity, brokered tokens, continuous identity |
| **Harness** | Flags, progressive delivery, experiments |
| **Connectivity** | Named endpoints, overlay, secretless connectors |

## Operator surfaces

| Surface | What you use it for |
|---|---|
| **`hobo` CLI** | Lifecycle, diagnosis, authoring, ops |
| **MCP** | Same verbs for agents |
| **Metering** | Usage facts and showback |

## Rules of thumb

1. Author **Bindles and topology** — not storage engines. 
2. Talk to **ports** (EventStore, Queue, Messaging); engines stay swappable. 
3. Prefer **secretless** federation over long-lived keys. 
4. **Conformance** is what “certified provider” means — same bar for every adapter.

## Related

[Architecture](/HoBo/architecture/) · [Component hosts](/HoBo/reference/component-hosts/) · [Runtime ports](/HoBo/reference/runtime-ports/) · [CLI](/HoBo/reference/cli/)

---

<!-- Reference · Component hosts · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/reference/component-hosts/ -->

# Component hosts

Camps separate two concerns:

| Concern | Role |
|---|---|
| **Durable EventStore engines** | Single-owner journal, fencing, staged effects |
| **Component hosts** | How Bindle components actually run |

App authors pick ports and Bindles; operators choose engines. Conformance certifies claims.

## EventStore engines (default path)

| Engine | Host | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Local SQLite | Node / server | Storage worker; crash-safe defaults |
| Browser SQLite | Browser | WASM + OPFS; fail-closed if durable required without OPFS |

See [EventStore](/HoBo/reference/eventstore/) · [Runtime ports](/HoBo/reference/runtime-ports/).

## Component host kinds

### Wasm (Wasmtime)

- Private components as **wasi:http** processes in sandboxes 
- Public web may stay process-local 
- Deny-by-default: only linked WIT imports are invokable 

### OCI / Kubernetes

1. Accept prebuilt wasi:http components 
2. Pack local OCI layout under the HoBo home directory 
3. Schedule on Kubernetes through a typed transport (version, apply, rollout) 

### Cloud-native registry

- Multi-cloud host registry with a **mock** path for parity tests 
- Cloud providers appear as they pass conformance 

## Optional sidecar runtime

Some Camps may opt into a **sidecar-style** runtime (for example Dapr-backed actors and pub/sub). It is never the default local path.

## Later engines

Postgres journals, Temporal, Restate, and similar remain future adapters behind the same ports.

## Related

[Capability map](/HoBo/reference/packages/) · [WASM guide](/HoBo/architecture/wasm/) · [Trail map](/HoBo/guide/status/) · [Conformance](/HoBo/testing/conformance/)

---

<!-- Reference · EventStore & journal · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/reference/eventstore/ -->

# EventStore & journal

## Ports

| API | Role |
|---|---|
| `EventStore` | `append`, stream `read`, live `subscribe`, `snapshot` |
| `DurableEventStore` | + `readAll` (positioned), `commit` (events + effects), durable subscription checkpoints |

### Positioned events

```ts
type EventPosition = bigint; // branded / parse-don't-validate
interface PositionedEvent {
  position: EventPosition;
  event: EventEnvelope;
}
```

`position` is **database-local** within a partition. It is not the domain ULID and not per-stream `seq`.

### Append options

- `expectedSeq` — optimistic concurrency (CAS).
- `fenceToken?: bigint` — actor lease fence; full 64-bit, never coerced to unsafe JS numbers.

### Typed errors (stable codes)

`OPTIMISTIC_SEQUENCE_CONFLICT`, `STALE_FENCE`, `MISSING_FENCE`, `CHECKPOINT_REGRESSION`, `UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION`, `SNAPSHOT_AHEAD`, `PERSISTENCE_UNAVAILABLE`, `SQLITE_BUSY`, …

## Single-owner partition model

- One SQLite file (or equivalent partition) · one active writer.
- Scale by **adding partitions**, not multi-writer WAL over NFS/SMB.
- Native: WAL + `synchronous=FULL` (Node `node:sqlite` behind a storage worker).
- Browser: Worker + OPFS when available; fail-closed if durable required without OPFS.

## Stream heads

Revision and `owner_epoch` live on a **streams** head row. Append algorithm:

1. `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`
2. Ensure head; read revision + epoch
3. Resolve idempotency
4. Validate expectedSeq + fencing
5. Insert events (contiguous seq + positions)
6. Stage durable effects
7. CAS-update head
8. Commit → then live wake-ups

Legacy streams migrate with `owner_epoch = 0` (unfenced); first fenced append enters fenced mode permanently.

## Transactional effects

`commit` may stage: queue messages, actor signals, timers, cron mutations, outbox rows — **same transaction** as domain events. Network dispatch happens **outside** the transaction (at-least-once + idempotency).

## Delivery guarantees

| Guarantee | Claim |
|---|---|
| Per-stream OCC | Yes |
| Fenced single writer | Yes |
| At-least-once subscriptions/outbox | Yes |
| Exactly-once external delivery | **No** |

## Engines

SQLite storage engine · local runtime · browser runtime · WIT `hobo:storage@0.1.0`

## Related testing

[Durable EventStore tests](/HoBo/testing/durability/)

---

<!-- Reference · Schema & migrations · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/reference/schema/ -->

# Schema & migrations

Default durable journal schema lives in **SQLite storage engine**. Engines may differ physically; **semantics** (stream heads, positions, fencing, staged effects) must pass conformance.

## Versioning

| Constant | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `SCHEMA_VERSION` | Current (v2) |
| `LEGACY_SCHEMA_VERSION` | Prior on-disk (v1) |

`PRAGMA user_version` must match code. Opening a **newer** DB with older code → `UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION` (fail closed).

## Core tables (v2 conceptual)

| Table | Role |
|---|---|
| `streams` | Head row: stream id, revision, `owner_epoch`, metadata |
| `events` | Append-only bodies + per-stream `seq` + store `position` |
| `effects` / staged work | Queue, timer, outbox, signals pending dispatch |
| `subscriptions` / checkpoints | Durable consumer positions |
| `snapshots` | Optional fold caches (never source of truth) |

Exact SQL is owned by the storage engine; do not re-implement in apps.

## Native pragmas

Native single-owner partitions use WAL-friendly settings with **`synchronous=FULL`** (or equivalent durability) — throughput second to crash safety for the default path.

## Codecs

Event payloads encode via versioned codecs. Unknown codec → `UNSUPPORTED_CODEC`. Upcasters live in the data plane, not as silent rewrite of historical bytes without policy.

## Migration rules

1. Forward-only migrations; no destructive “fix by deleting the file” in production paths.
2. Legacy streams get `owner_epoch = 0` until first fenced write.
3. Integrity checks: contiguous seq, head matches last event, positions monotonic — failures → `STREAM_INTEGRITY` / `MIGRATION_FAILURE`.
4. Tests: [Migration fixtures](/HoBo/testing/migration/).

## What apps must not do

- Open the SQLite file and invent tables beside the journal.
- Use `COUNT(*)` as stream revision.
- Multi-writer mount the same file over NFS/SMB and call it HA.

## Related

[EventStore](/HoBo/reference/eventstore/) · [Durability testing](/HoBo/testing/durability/) · [WIT storage](/HoBo/reference/wit-storage/)

---

<!-- Reference · Queue port · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/reference/queue/ -->

# Queue port

The **Queue** is the Camp port for deferred and concurrent work: jobs, actor signals, delayed delivery, and outbox-style dispatch. Ports are product surfaces; engines implement lease semantics.

## Operations (conceptual)

| Op | Role |
|---|---|
| `enqueue` | Persist a message with optional delay, group, and idempotency key |
| `lease` | Claim work for a worker with visibility timeout + fence |
| `complete` / `fail` | Ack success or schedule retry / DLQ path |
| `signal` mapping | Deliver actor wake-ups without inventing a second bus |

## Guarantees

| Guarantee | Claim |
|---|---|
| At-least-once delivery | **Yes** |
| Exactly-once external side effects | **No** — use idempotency keys |
| Ordered per group/key (engine-dependent) | When configured |
| Survives process restart | When backed by durable journal |

## Transactional staging

When using **DurableEventStore.commit**, queue messages (and timers/outbox rows) may stage in the **same transaction** as domain events. Network dispatch happens **outside** the transaction. That yields:

- Domain fact + “work is pending” atomicity
- At-least-once dispatch after commit
- Need for consumer idempotency

## Leases and fencing

Workers hold leases. Completing work after a stolen lease must fail closed (stale fence). Same fence discipline as ActorHost / EventStore — do not coerce fence tokens to unsafe JS numbers.

## Testing

- Restart with staged messages still leased correctly.
- Double-complete after lease expiry fails closed.
- See [Queue, timer, outbox](/HoBo/testing/queue-outbox/).

## Related

[Messaging, Kafka & Dapr](/HoBo/reference/messaging/) · [EventStore](/HoBo/reference/eventstore/) · [ActorHost](/HoBo/reference/actor-host/) · [Runtime ports](/HoBo/reference/runtime-ports/)

---

<!-- Reference · Messaging, Kafka & Dapr · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/reference/messaging/ -->

# Messaging, Kafka & Dapr

HoBo unifies app messaging behind **ports**, not vendor SDKs. Bindles declare `topic()` / queue / actor `signal`; Camps select backends. **In-process wasm stays the default**. Dapr is **opt-in**.

## Authoring (ports only)

```ts
import { topic } from "hobo/bindles";
// Backend is Matching / Camp runtime selection — never import Kafka or Dapr clients here.
const events = topic("user-created").allow("publish");
```

Actors use the same definition surface under **native** or **dapr** placement.

## Capability map

| Capability | Role |
|---|---|
| Messaging port | Delivery guarantees, tenant scoping, in-memory adapter |
| Kafka provider | Kafka / Redpanda / MSK / Confluent capability + resource definitions |
| Optional Dapr runtime | Optional Camp runtime: ActorHost + pubsub + secretless component YAML |
| Runtime placement | Native or Dapr actor placement and signal routing |
| Junction federation | Cross-Yard topic / actor-signal **federation plan** (control plane + identity) |
| Messaging policy | Exactly-once, deny-Dapr, tenant quotas |
| Conformance suite | Messaging conformance against Kafka and Dapr adapters |

## Fidelity honesty

| Mode | How | Label |
|---|---|---|
| Simulated | No transport / no Dapr client | `simulated` |
| Live harness | In-memory Kafka / Dapr test doubles | `live` |
| Live process | Real broker or daprd client implementing the same interfaces | `live` |
| Forbidden | `live: true` without transport/client | **throws** |

Never treat a boolean flag as live while still on the pure emulator.

## Delivery guarantees

- Portable default: **at-least-once**
- **Exactly-once** / transactional produce are **capability flags** Matching and `can-deploy` can require
- Dead-letter after `maxDeliveryAttempts` (subscription); permanent failure advances the consumer group (commit under lease — do not nack-then-commit)

## Secretless + multi-tenant

- Credentials are binding refs only (`fromBinding`, federation, `secretRef`)
- Generated Dapr component YAML must not embed passwords
- Topics, consumer groups, and Dapr app-ids are tenant-scoped by default

## CLI

| Command | Role |
|---|---|
| `hobo doctor` | Reports Kafka + Dapr readiness and messaging hazards |
| Authoring | Declare `topic()` in the Bindle; backends are Camp/Matching choices |

Messaging plane diagnostics surface through `doctor` and contract/conformance suites — apps never import Kafka or Dapr clients.

## Permanent non-goals

- Kafka cluster operator / managed-service UI
- Full Dapr workflow **engine** parity (supported: **activity-name map only**)
- Advanced schema-registry Avro/Protobuf wire protocol end-to-end
- Junction **data-plane** byte relay (control-plane federation is in; overlay carries data)

## Related

[ActorHost](/HoBo/reference/actor-host/) · [Queue](/HoBo/reference/queue/) · [Component hosts](/HoBo/reference/component-hosts/) · [Capability map](/HoBo/reference/packages/) · [CLI](/HoBo/reference/cli/) · [WASM & WIT](/HoBo/architecture/wasm/)

---

<!-- Reference · Streamer port · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/reference/streamer/ -->

# Streamer port

The **Streamer** carries **per-frame** high-volume payloads — LLM tokens, progressive UI chunks, log lines, exec stdout — without turning the domain EventStore into a blob store.

## Separation of concerns

| Layer | Holds |
|---|---|
| **EventStore** | Domain and control **facts** (past-tense, foldable, audit) |
| **Streamer journal** | Frame **bodies** for a run (dev-grade in-memory until teardown unless upgraded) |
| **Optional audit opt-in** | Policy may require selected frames as events — not the default |

Yard is **never** on the streaming data path. Live tails (`hobo logs`) go Camp → Streamer.

## Lifecycle

Run lifecycle may be event-sourced even when bodies are not:

- `StreamRunOpened` / related open facts
- Frames append with monotonic sequence within the run
- `StreamRunClosed` (or failure terminal)

Readers attach with `fromSeq` for **replay-then-live**: catch up stored frames, then subscribe for new ones — same mental model as EventStore subscriptions.

## Guarantees

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| Ordered frames per run | Yes (seq) |
| Durable domain audit of every token | **No** by default |
| Exactly-once delivery to all subscribers | **No** — at-least-once / best-effort per engine |
| Cross-Camp frame federation | Out of scope for the port |

## Coupling rules

- Aggregates and workflows **must not** dump large progressive payloads into EventStore “for convenience.”
- Executors stream `exec.Output` through Streamer; Dashboard projections show live progress from those frames + control events.
- Deterministic replay of **domain** state never depends on Streamer contents.

## Testing

- Unit: mock Streamer; assert open/close and `fromSeq` contract.
- Behavior: `hobo logs` / Bridge live-tail modes against contract fixtures.
- Do not require live cloud sinks for PR gates.

## Related

[Runtime ports](/HoBo/reference/runtime-ports/) · [Data plane](/HoBo/architecture/data-plane/) · [CLI](/HoBo/reference/cli/)

---

<!-- Reference · ActorHost & fencing · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/reference/actor-host/ -->

# ActorHost & fencing

**ActorHost** is the Camp port that hands out **single-writer leases** for aggregates (and similar actors). Without it, optimistic concurrency alone cannot stop a zombie process from appending with a stale view of the world after a steal.

## AggregateLease

A lease (conceptual shape):

| Field | Role |
|---|---|
| Aggregate / actor key | Who is leased |
| `holderId` | Process or worker identity |
| `fenceToken` | Monotonic **bigint** epoch for this key |
| Expiry | Optional lease deadline |

In-memory hosts exist for tests; production Camps use durable hosts that persist epoch across restarts, backed by the journal.

## Dual placement (native · dapr)

The same actor definitions run under either host:

| Mode | When | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **native** (default) | No Camp dapr requirement | Lease + fence on local / wasm hosts |

Prefer native unless you need the sidecar path. See [Messaging, Kafka & Dapr](/HoBo/reference/messaging/).

## Append algorithm coupling

When an aggregate is fenced:

1. Acquire/renew lease → receive `fenceToken`.
2. `decide` pure business rules in memory.
3. `append` / `commit` with `expectedSeq` **and** `fenceToken`.
4. Store compares token to stream head `owner_epoch`:
 - equal → accept (and may bump epoch per engine rules)
 - lower → `STALE_FENCE`
 - missing on fenced stream → `MISSING_FENCE`

Legacy streams start with `owner_epoch = 0` (unfenced). First fenced append enters fenced mode permanently.

## Error policy

| Code | Meaning | Aggregate retry? |
|---|---|---|
| `AGGREGATE_CONFLICT` / OCC | Stale expectedSeq | Yes — reload & retry |
| `STALE_FENCE` | Lost lease | **No** as blind OCC retry |
| `AGGREGATE_INVARIANT` | Business reject | No |

## Rules

- Never coerce `fenceToken` through `Number` — full 64-bit.
- Lease steal must advance epoch so the previous holder fails closed.
- Passivate emits facts; do not rely on process memory for “I still own it.”

## Related

[EventStore](/HoBo/reference/eventstore/) · [Messaging, Kafka & Dapr](/HoBo/reference/messaging/) · [Aggregates testing](/HoBo/testing/aggregates/) · [Durability testing](/HoBo/testing/durability/)

---

<!-- Reference · Clock port · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/reference/clock/ -->

# Clock port

The **Clock** port supplies time and sleep/cron primitives so workflows and tests can be **deterministic**. Wall-clock `Date.now()` inside pure decide/fold paths is a bug.

## Responsibilities

| API family | Role |
|---|---|
| `now` | Current instant in the active clock domain |
| `sleep` / delay | Schedule wake-ups (pairs with timer journal) |
| `cron` / schedule | Recurring triggers as durable facts + wakes |
| Advance (test) | Virtual clocks jump without waiting real time |

## Why it exists

- **Replay** of workflows must re-enter the same branches.
- **Timers** staged in the journal must fire once-after-restart with the same deadlines.
- **Property tests** need controlled time to explore schedules without flakiness.

## Rules

1. Aggregates that need “business time” take it as a **command field** or injected clock reading at the boundary — not ad-hoc OS time inside pure functions.
2. Event envelope timestamps are assigned at append by the store/runtime — folds treat them as data.
3. Resilience timeouts use the same clock domain as the runtime so virtual tests remain meaningful.
4. Never sleep with real wall timers inside pure unit tests of domain logic.

## Coupling

- Durable timers may stage beside events in `DurableEventStore.commit`.
- ActorHost leases may use clock for expiry.
- Streamer and logs may show wall time for humans; domain correctness does not depend on it.

## Related

[Runtime ports](/HoBo/reference/runtime-ports/) · [Queue](/HoBo/reference/queue/) · [Aggregates testing](/HoBo/testing/aggregates/)

---

<!-- Reference · Runtime ports · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/reference/runtime-ports/ -->

# Runtime ports

A **Camp** provides the durable substrate app runtimes need. **Ports** are product surfaces; **engines** implement them (SQLite storage engine, local runtime, browser runtime, future Postgres/Temporal/… adapters).

## Port table

| Port | Responsibility | Default notes |
|---|---|---|
| **EventStore** | Append-only facts, stream read, live subscribe, snapshots | OCC via `expectedSeq` |
| **DurableEventStore** | + positions, `commit` with staged effects, durable checkpoints | SQLite partition |
| **Queue** | Enqueue / lease / complete; actor signal mapping | At-least-once |
| **Streamer** | High-volume frames **outside** domain log | Replay-then-live `fromSeq` |
| **ActorHost** | Single-writer lease + monotonic `fenceToken` | Fence couples to append |
| **Clock** | Deterministic time + sleep/cron for replay | Virtual in tests |

## Coupling rules

1. Aggregates acquire **ActorHost** leases and pass **fenceToken** into EventStore `append` / `commit`.
2. Queue / timer / outbox may **stage inside** the journal transaction when durability is configured; network I/O happens after commit.
3. Streamer frame bodies are **not** domain events unless an audit policy opts in.
4. Clock reads during replay must not inject wall-clock nondeterminism into pure folds.
5. Yard control plane is **not** on the Camp data path for live user requests.

## Default engine

| Engine | Role |
|---|---|
| SQLite storage | Schema, migrations, journal semantics |
| Local runtime | Node EventStore + storage worker |
| Browser runtime | SQLite WASM + OPFS policy (fail-closed if durable required) |
| `hobo:storage@0.1.0` | Component-host storage capability |

Scale by **adding partitions** (single active writer each), not multi-writer WAL over shared network filesystems.

## Port descriptors

Port descriptors carry WIT-style interface refs and stability (`stable` | `preview` | `experimental`). Apps depend on ports; engines stay swappable behind conformance.

## Testing

| Concern | Page |
|---|---|
| CAS, fencing, restart | [Durable EventStore](/HoBo/testing/durability/) |
| Pure decide + conflicts | [Aggregates](/HoBo/testing/aggregates/) |
| Queue/timer/outbox | [Queue, timer, outbox](/HoBo/testing/queue-outbox/) |
| Engine swap | [Conformance](/HoBo/testing/conformance/) |

## Related

[EventStore](/HoBo/reference/eventstore/) · [Queue](/HoBo/reference/queue/) · [Streamer](/HoBo/reference/streamer/) · [ActorHost](/HoBo/reference/actor-host/) · [Clock](/HoBo/reference/clock/)

<!-- Reference · Contracts & Gatekeeper · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/reference/contracts/ -->

# Contracts & Gatekeeper

## BoundaryContract (Contract IR)

Versioned producer/consumer boundary:

- `id`, `version` (semver), `mode` (`declared` \| `inferred` \| `observed` \| `promoted`)
- `edge` — kind, producer, consumer, channel, operation
- `requiredShape` — format + required/provided fields
- `contractHash` — content address (`sha256:…`)
- optional **`effects`** — [EffectSpec](/HoBo/reference/effects/)
- optional **`resilience`** — [ResilienceProfile](/HoBo/reference/effects/)

Contracts are parse-don’t-validate: invalid shapes never become live values past the boundary.

## Compatibility

Compatibility checks compare previous vs next revisions:

| Change | Result |
|---|---|
| Added provided fields | Compatible |
| Removed required/provided field consumers need | Breaking (`required-field-removed`) |
| Channel change / version regress | Breaking |
| Effect widening when effects declared | Breaking (`effect-widened`) |

## can-deploy

Given deployed contract state + candidate deployment plan → compatibility matrix + gate pass/fail events with agent-actionable reasons.

## Gatekeeper

Composes into one decision (`allow` \| `allow-degraded` \| `deny` \| `require-approval`):

1. can-deploy (contracts)
2. policy pack — **always** emits `policy.Decided`
3. obligations
4. cost/quota
5. optional secretless-config / can-migrate dimensions

Also surfaces effect summaries and optional reasons with `gate: "effects" | "resilience"`.

## Describe / export

CLI and MCP can describe a contract as human text or export an effect manifest for policy and SRE tooling.

## Testing

See [Testing: contracts](/HoBo/testing/contracts/) for harness usage.

## Related

[Testing: contracts](/HoBo/testing/contracts/) · [Testing: deployment](/HoBo/testing/deployment/)

---

<!-- Reference · Effects & resiliency · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/reference/effects/ -->

# Effects & resiliency

. Names are locked: **Effects** on contracts; **Resiliency** as secondary visible layer. 

## EffectSpec

```ts
interface EffectSpec {
 schemaVersion: "hobo.effect-spec/v1";
 purity: "pure" | "varies" | "transacts" | "noRollback";
 capabilities: ("decides" | "suspends" | "allocates" | "concurrent")[];
 domains: (
 | "network" | "storage" | "identity" | "policyEval" | "eventEmit"
 | "metering" | "overlayTunnel" | "iac" | "secretsResidual" | "clock"
 | "externalCall" | "agentTool"
 )[];
}
```

### Lattice helpers

| Helper | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `isPure` | No domain I/O; purity pure |
| `mayFail` | Has `decides` |
| `requiresNetwork` | `network` or `externalCall` |
| `effectUnion` | Join purity + union sets |
| `effectSubtype` | Safer provided ⊆ required |
| `isEffectWideningBreaking` | Next adds domains/caps or dirties purity |

### Defaults

Missing effects are valid (opt-in). External reasoning applies a **conservative** default (`noRollback` + `decides` + network/externalCall) without rewriting the content hash of contracts that omitted effects.

## Capture

| Fact | When |
|---|---|
| `contract.EffectDeclared` | Contract effects registered |
| `contract.EffectInvoked` | Boundary invocation recorded |

Effect capture writes to an event sink. Replay **reads facts** — does not re-execute handlers.

Effect manifests export purity, domains, and flags (`mayFail`, `requiresNetwork`, `isPure`) for CLI, MCP, policy, and SRE tooling.

## ResilienceProfile (secondary)

Strategies (metadata + thin applicator):

- `retry` — deterministic seed, max attempts, delays; `retryOn: "transient-only"`
- `circuitBreaker`, `timeout`, `bulkhead`, `fallback`, `hedging`

Always enforce **neverRetry**: `policy.Decided`, `terminal`, `cancellation`.

Applying a profile emits `resilience.Attempt` / `resilience.Terminal`. Inspection rebuilds terminal state from those facts without re-running ops.

Circuit-breaker / hedging require network/externalCall domains on the contract.

## Testing entry

[Effect-aware isolation](/HoBo/testing/effects/)

---

<!-- Reference · Policy plane · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/reference/policy/ -->

# Policy plane

Policy is **versioned, signed-pack evaluated** authorization and obligation logic. It is not “config flags scattered in YAML.” The policy engine holds IR and agent guardrails; Gatekeeper composes policy with contracts and cost.

## Packs

A **policy pack** attaches to Yard/Junction (and can be proposed by Platform Engineer Crew):

| Kind | Behavior |
|---|---|
| **Mandatory** | Deny ceilings — children may only further restrict |
| **Default** | Overridable baselines |

Evaluation is deny-by-default for unlisted `(role, action, resource)` on control-plane surfaces. CLI/MCP verbs map to `hobo:<resource>:<verb>` or conformance fails.

## Decisions

Every evaluation emits **`policy.Decided`** — including **allows**. Reasons are machine-readable for agents and humans.

High-risk actions (destroy, prod mutate, spend above cap) resolve to:

- `allow`
- `require-approval` (obligation)
- `deny`

## Obligations

When decision is `require-approval` or similar, Gatekeeper records **obligations** (who, deadline, what satisfies). Unsatisfied obligations block mutate paths. A2H handoffs create human obligations with the same machinery.

## Never retry policy denials

Resilience layers **must not** retry `policy.Decided` denials. That class is terminal for the attempt — change policy or request approval, do not spin.

## Guardrails

AI operators and generation paths evaluate content/tool guardrails (PII, jailbreak, unsafe tools). Blocks emit `guardrail.Blocked` **and** `policy.Decided`.

## Composition order (Gatekeeper)

1. Contracts / can-deploy 
2. **Policy pack** 
3. Obligations 
4. Cost / quota 
5. Optional secretless-config / can-migrate / effects visibility 

## Related

[Contracts & Gatekeeper](/HoBo/reference/contracts/) · [Security](/HoBo/security/) · [Effects](/HoBo/reference/effects/)

---

<!-- Reference · Matching & ResourceActors · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/reference/matching/ -->

# Matching & ResourceActors

## Matching

**Matching** resolves each Bindle resource against **Resource Definitions** and provider capability to choose *where* and *how* a resource is realized. It is the placement brain inside plan/up — not a separate product noun beside Gatekeeper.

Flow (conceptual):

1. Resource collection produces provider-agnostic **manifest IR**.
2. Each node lowers to **ResourceIntent** (FinOps/routing-friendly, provider-neutral).
3. Matching + policy + cost solve a **DeploymentPlan** DAG.
4. Gatekeeper admits or denies the plan.
5. ResourceActors converge desired → actual.

## ResourceActor

One **ResourceActor** (controller-style grain) per resource owns reconciliation:

| State (conceptual) | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Desired | From DeploymentPlan |
| Progressing | Executor in flight |
| Ready | Provider reports healthy |
| Failed | Past no-go threshold → compensation choreography |
| Drifted | Actual ≠ desired → governed remediation |

## Choreography over orchestration

- Independent subtrees provision **concurrently**.
- No single coordinator SPOF for every resource.
- Compensation is also choreographed: `resource.Failed` past threshold → `deployment.RolledBack` fans out.
- **DeploymentView** projection reconstructs the saga graph for humans/agents.

## Executors

Sandboxed runners (Firecracker-class) apply IaC/builds with **short-lived scoped tokens** — no ambient cloud creds. Stdout streams via Streamer; state events hit the control log.

## Continuous re-placement

Dispatcher re-enters Matching when price/policy/reliability signals change. Same plan → gate → converge path as human `hobo up` — migration is not a special engine.

## Related

[Control plane](/HoBo/architecture/control-plane/) · [Conductor](/HoBo/primitives/stations/#the-conductor) · [Continuous migration](/HoBo/cicd/migration/) · [Event families](/HoBo/reference/events/)

---

<!-- Reference · Harness & progressive · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/reference/harness/ -->

# Harness & progressive delivery

**Harness** is the flags / progressive delivery / experiments plane. It is **not** a second infrastructure control plane — it routes **traffic and contract observation** safely.

## Standards-shaped cores

| Core | Role |
|---|---|
| **OpenFeature** | Sole public flag evaluation API for application code (`HoboOpenFeatureProvider` / `HoboFeatureClient`) |
| **OpenDelivery** (HoBo-shaped) | Progressive delivery / weight shifts |
| **OpenExperiment** (HoBo-shaped) | Bounded experiments with metrics hooks |
| **OpenTelemetry hooks** | Export observation without inventing a parallel telemetry product |

`FeatureFlagStore` + delivery + experiment engines are composed by `Harness`.

## Capabilities

| Capability | Role |
|---|---|
| Feature flags | Ranked evaluation with audit facts |
| Experiments | Bounded exposure |
| Gateway weights | Shift traffic across revisions/camps |
| Sandbox lanes | Isolate experimental contract observations |
| Delivery composition | Safe rollout steps shared with Trails |
| Continuous delivery plane | Workload-attested apply of Gatekeeper-approved sets (cloud control plane CD) composes Harness |

## Rules

1. Baseline subscribers **ignore** sandbox-lane events by default.
2. Flag changes are **facts** — replayable, not console memory.
3. Progressive steps still pass **Gatekeeper** when they mutate infra.
4. Trails compose Harness for cutover; pure flag flips need no Trail.
5. Agents change flags only under RBAC + policy (often require-approval in prod).
6. App code evaluates flags through **OpenFeature** — not ad-hoc env bools that bypass audit.

## CLI

`hobo feature …` for flag/progressive ops. Observe via `inspect` projections and event replay.

## Testing

- Dual fixtures for flag on/off paths.
- Bridge shadow mode to compare experimental vs baseline.
- Chaos: partial weight shifts must not break claimed session consistency.

## Related

[Progressive delivery guide](/HoBo/cicd/progressive-delivery/) · [Trails](/HoBo/primitives/trails/) · [Bridge modes](/HoBo/testing/bridge-modes/) · [Identity](/HoBo/reference/identity/) · [Matching](/HoBo/reference/matching/)

<!-- Reference · Event families · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/reference/events/ -->

# Event families

Event names use **`family.PastTenseFact`** shape. The design suite keeps a **canonical inventory**; new families must be cataloged before inventing backticked names in design or site prose.

## Envelope (conceptual)

Every fact rides a shared envelope family of fields:

| Field | Role |
|---|---|
| `id` | ULID — global causal-ish order |
| `seq` | Per-stream total order |
| `type` | `family.PastTenseFact` |
| `stream` / aggregate id | Ownership boundary |
| `causationId` / `correlationId` | Why / which workflow |
| `tenant` (+ project/env as applicable) | Isolation claims |
| `meta.idempotencyKey` | Exactly-once *effects* over at-least-once delivery |
| `position` | When read from DurableEventStore — store-local |

## Families you will hit often

| Family | Examples | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `compat.*` | `GatePassed`, `GateFailed` | can-deploy outcomes |
| `contract.*` | `Observed`, `Verified`, `EffectDeclared`, `EffectInvoked` | Contract IR lifecycle |
| `policy.*` | `Decided`, `ObligationCreated`, `ObligationSatisfied` | **Always** decide, even allows |
| `gatekeeper.*` | `Decided` | Composed gate result |
| `resilience.*` | `Attempt`, `Terminal` | Secondary resiliency layer |
| `actor.*` | `Activated`, `StateAppended`, `Passivated` | Actor host lifecycle |
| `crew.*` | `AgentDispatched`, `ActionProposed`, `ActionApplied`, `HandoffRequested` | Thin roster — no per-operator silos |
| `incident.*` | Opened → … → Resolved / PostmortemFiled | SRE loop |
| `run.*` | `Started`, `StepCompleted` | Workflows / generation runs |
| `deployment.*` | Planned / Applied / Deployed / Failed / RolledBack | Control plane |
| `broker.*` | `Resolved`, `Rejected` | Conductor placement |
| `resource.*` | Provisioned / Failed / DriftDetected | ResourceActors |
| `token.*` / `identity.*` | Issued / Rotated / Accessed | Refs only for secrets |
| `config.*` / `secret.*` | `Resolved`, `Accessed` | Refs only |
| `meter.*` | `UsageRecorded` | Showback facts |
| `guardrail.*` | `Blocked` | AI safety |
| `trail.*` | Plan/run/cutover facts | Continuous migration recipes |
| `station.*` | Station/Rail lifecycle | Control-plane isolation |
| `replay.*` | `Started` / `ChunkIngested` / `Ended` / `Accessed` / … | Session Replay lifecycle (not event-log replay) |

Domain apps add **their own** families under app namespaces — do not overload `crew.*` or `deployment.*` for business cart events.

## Sandbox lanes

Boundary virtualization tags envelope **lane** metadata. Baseline contract promotion **ignores** sandbox-lane observations by default so experiments cannot poison production contracts or training trajectories.

## Rules

1. Past tense only — commands are not events.
2. Inspection and audit are **replay of the log**, not process memory.
3. Poison bodies → `*.Quarantined` so folds skip deterministically.
4. Crew roster facts stay on thin `crew.*` — operator-specific detail is payload, not family explosion.
5. Streamer frames are **not** automatically domain events.

## Related

[Architecture](/HoBo/architecture/) · [Data plane](/HoBo/architecture/data-plane/) · [Crew shared model](/HoBo/operations/shared-model/) · [EventStore](/HoBo/reference/eventstore/)

<!-- Reference · Errors & codes · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/reference/errors/ -->

# Errors & codes

Prefer **stable codes** over string matching. Map adapter errors at package boundaries. Do **not** leak SQL, filesystem paths, or secret material into app-facing errors.

## Shape conventions

Errors that cross a boundary should carry:

| Field | Role |
|---|---|
| `code` | Stable SCREAMING_SNAKE or dotted machine code |
| `message` | Human-safe summary (no secrets) |
| `retryable` | Explicit when known (do not infer from message) |
| `cause` chain | Internal only; strip before external MCP/CLI if sensitive |

Parse-don’t-validate constructors throw typed parse errors (`CoreParseError`, `EffectValidationError`, …) rather than returning “maybe invalid” DTOs.

## EventStore / storage

| Code | Meaning | Typical retry |
|---|---|---|
| `OPTIMISTIC_SEQUENCE_CONFLICT` | Stale `expectedSeq` | Yes — reload stream |
| `STALE_FENCE` | Fence below `owner_epoch` | No as OCC retry |
| `MISSING_FENCE` | Unfenced write to fenced stream | No — acquire lease |
| `CHECKPOINT_REGRESSION` | Non-monotonic checkpoint | No |
| `UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION` | DB newer than code | No — upgrade binary |
| `MIGRATION_FAILURE` | Migrate failed | No until fixed |
| `STREAM_INTEGRITY` | Noncontiguous / head mismatch | No |
| `UNSUPPORTED_CODEC` | Unknown payload codec | No |
| `PERSISTENCE_UNAVAILABLE` | e.g. OPFS required but missing | No / change mode |
| `SQLITE_BUSY` | Busy timeout | Maybe — backoff |
| `SNAPSHOT_AHEAD` | Snapshot seq > head | No |
| `STORAGE_WORKER_TERMINATED` | Worker crash | Restart worker |

## Aggregates 

| Code | Meaning | Retry? |
|---|---|---|
| `AGGREGATE_CONFLICT` | OCC / concurrent writers | Yes — reload & retry |
| `AGGREGATE_INVARIANT` | Business rule reject | No |
| Stale fence surfaced at aggregate | Lost lease | No blind retry |

## Resilience failure classes

| Class | Retry via ResilienceProfile? |
|---|---|
| `transient` | Yes (within profile) |
| `policy.Decided` | **Never** |
| `terminal` | **Never** |
| `cancellation` | **Never** |
| `deadline` | Policy-dependent; not infinite retry |

## Contracts / Gatekeeper

Compatibility and gate denials surface as structured reasons (`MachineReadableReason` with `gate: contracts | policy | obligations | cost | effects | resilience`), not only thrown exceptions. CLI/MCP should print reason codes agents can act on.

## Identity / config

Prefer ref-safe messages (“resolution rank failed at provider-federation”) over embedding token fragments. Static-escape expiry is a hard fail, not a silent fallback to plaintext.

## Related

[EventStore](/HoBo/reference/eventstore/) · [Effects](/HoBo/reference/effects/) · [ActorHost](/HoBo/reference/actor-host/) · [Contracts](/HoBo/reference/contracts/)

---

<!-- Reference · CLI surface · https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io/HoBo/reference/cli/ -->

# CLI surface

The `hobo` CLI is deliberately **small and stable**. The same canonical verb set appears as MCP tools. Docs examples use only this list.

## Lifecycle

| Verb | Role |
|---|---|
| `up` | Realize the object graph (build, plan, gate, provision, deploy) |
| `down` | Reverse |
| `dev` | Offline local Camp / inner loop |
| `plan` | Dry-run the up decision (approvable diff) |
| `verify` | Unified Gatekeeper preflight (read-only) |
| `can-deploy` | Producer/consumer compatibility diagnosis |

`up` still runs the same gate as `verify` automatically before mutation. Continuous delivery *observation* uses `deploy` (below), not a second ship verb.

## Identity, access, progressive

| Verb | Role |
|---|---|
| `login` | Authenticate / associate default broker |
| `claim` | Bind anonymous deployment to an account |
| `identity` | Continuous identity status / inspect |
| `access` | Elevated / cross-env access or break-glass |
| `connection` | Connection management (Station-bound) |
| `feature` | Flags / progressive delivery (Harness) |
| `deploy` | CD status / logs / rollback (attested apply plane) |
| `incident` | CD failure disposition / A2H |
| `trails` | Continuous migration recipes (`status` \| `plan` \| `inspect`) |
| `station` | Station **ops/setup** (not app lifecycle) |
| `yard` | Bare-metal Yard install / inspect |
| `broker` | Conductor config + resolve + matrix |
| `serve` | Local control-plane HTTP+SSE for the Yard game UI |

## Authoring

| Verb | Role |
|---|---|
| `new` | Scaffold |
| `collect` | Resource collection → manifest IR |
| `codegen` | Regenerate project bindings (`--check` fails on drift) |
| `build` | Compile to wasm components (OCI fallback) |
| `stub` | Contract-backed stub behind a WIT port |
| `generate` | Generation pipeline entry |
| `sandbox` | Isolated lane; out-of-scope boundaries from contracts |
| `test` | Contract-backed sandbox test lane (not a jest replacement) |

## Observe & operate

| Verb | Role |
|---|---|
| `inspect` | Projections / time-travel (`run`, `deploy`, `topology`, …) |
| `logs` | Live-tail Camp Streamer |
| `replay` | **Session Replay** — `list` \| `get` \| `open` \| `summarize` \| `retention` \| `doctor` |
| `doctor` | Environment / credential / portability hazards (incl. messaging readiness) |
| `messaging` | Inspect messaging capability and delivery-guarantee readiness |
| `drift` | Drift + governed remediation |
| `runbook` | Execute runbooks (writes still policy-gated) |
| `attest` | Signed evidence exports from audit facts |
| `erase` | Crypto-shred subject + projection rebuild |
| `derivative` | Derived implementation upgrade / conformance |

## Distribution

| Verb | Role |
|---|---|
| `add` | Install provider or listing (sig + provenance + conformance) |
| `registry` | Registry admin; signed offline bundle import |
| `import` | Adopt estate in place — never destroy/recreate on import |

## Station context

For `station`, `broker`, `connection`, and station-aware `up` / `login`:

1. `--station` / `--station-uri`
2. `HOBO_STATION` / `HOBO_STATION_URI`
3. `profile.defaultStation`
4. Fail closed with remediation `hobo station init`

Receipts pin `stationId` + `railHash`.

## Policy mapping

Control-plane verbs map to `hobo:<resource>:<verb>` policy actions (**deny-by-default**). Unmapped verbs fail conformance.

## Related

[The hobo CLI](/HoBo/guide/cli/) · [MCP](/HoBo/agents/mcp/) · [Stations](/HoBo/primitives/stations/) · [Trail map](/HoBo/guide/status/)
